HORA (HOUR), years: St Eucherius, L, 741.

HORDEUM (BARLEY), action: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1012. — The administration of earthly things: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 434.

HORTUS SPONSAE CONCLUSUS (THE ENCLOSED GARDEN OF THE BRIDE) denotes the virtue of chastity, fortified by continence: St Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 399.

HOSPITALITAS (HOSPITALITY) is the daughter of mercy: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 324.

HUMERUS (SHOULDER), the social life; a work of justice; one’s proper work; labour; sufferings; strength; strenuous modes of life: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 959. — The bond of social life; action: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 191.

HUMILITAS (HUMILITY), the virtue of gentleness; delight; satisfaction: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 59.

HYDRIA (WATER-JAR) is said to be wisdom: ibid., 1088.

HYSSOPUS (HYSSOP) is a type of faith: St Peter Damian, CXLIV, 909; Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 424. In hyssop are denoted humility and patience: St Eucherius, L, 742; St Bernard, CLXXXIII, 999.

IACINTUS (HYACINTH), heavenly desire: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 965.

IGNIS (FIRE), charity; good desire; zeal for holiness; the light of knowledge; persecution; doctrine; temporal eminence; zeal; tribulation: ibid., 966. — Zeal of charity; compunction; fervour of suffering: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 355. — By fire is understood the fervour of charity: Rabanus Maurus, CXI, 1079. — Fire denotes severity: Adam of Scotland, CXCVIII, 788.

IMBER (RAIN), preaching about divinity; abundant doctrine; humble doctrine; persecution; words of teachers: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 970. — Rain denotes a flood of temptations: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 69.

INAURIS (EARRING), obedience: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 970.

[Col. 0204] INCASTRATURAE (INSERTS) in the sides of the boards denote the virtue of humility in the mountains of the righteous: ibid., CVIII, 169.

INTESTINA (INTERNAL ORGANS), the inward parts of our mind: ibid., CXII, 971.

IRA DEI (WRATH OF GOD), experience of just vengeance: ibid., 975.

JANUA (DOOR), conscience; mercy: ibid., 965.

JASPUS (JASPER), faith: ibid., 965. — The greenness of inward desire: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 354.

JERUSALEM denotes the faithful soul: Rabanus Maurus, CXI, 337, 379.

JORDANIS (JORDAN), humility; instability of this life: CXII, 971.

JUDICIUM (JUDGMENT), discernment; separation: ibid., 973.

JUGUM (YOKE), religious life; captivity: ibid., 972.

JUMENTA (BEASTS OF BURDEN), chastity; helps; virtues: ibid., 973. — Beasts of burden are called worldly entanglements: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 85.

JUSTITIA (JUSTICE), faith; good action; chastening scourges: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 973.

JUNIPERUS (JUNIPER), stability of charity: ibid., 972.

JUVENTUS (YOUTH), the earliest age; the beginning of good conduct; return to good: ibid., 975.

LABIA (LIPS), speech of the mouth: ibid., 977. — The beloved’s lips signify pure and clean doctrine: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 924.

LABRUM (BASIN), compunction: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 977. — The bronze basin of the tabernacle denotes the washing of compunction and tears: Adam of Scotland, CXCVIII, 768.

LAC (MILK), a symbol of simpler and more rudimentary doctrine: Rabanus Maurus, CVII, 551; CVIII, 1137. — Milk: simple doctrine; innocence; good action; temporal administration: ibid., CXII, 978. — Doctrine is compared to milk: Gillebert, CLXXXIV, 142.

LACTUCAE (LETTUCES), afflictions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 979. — The bitterness of repentance: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 429.

LAEVA (LEFT HAND), temporal gifts: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 985. — Prosperity in the present life: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 199. — The left hand signifies temporal goods and suffering: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1103.

LAGUNCULA (LITTLE FLASK), conscience: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 979.

LAMINA (PLATE), works of piety: ibid.

LAMPAS (TORCH), good works; the brightness of miracles: ibid., 981; Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 457.

LANA (WOOL), simplicity; good action; temporal provisions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 980. — Wool, [reading uncertain], mystically denotes divine love: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 1126.

LANCEAE (LANCES), darts of temptations: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 328.

LAPIS (STONE), a hard thought: ibid., 350. — By stones, works are expressed: St Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 492.

LATITUDO (BREADTH), charity: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 983.

LATUS (SIDE), defence; meditation in contemplation: ibid., 982. — The side signifies the union of flesh and soul: Venerable Hildebert of Le Mans, CLXXI, 678–679.

LAVACRUM (WASHING) denotes purification of the mind: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 78, 170.

LECTULUS (LITTLE BED), holy leisure; inward hope; inward rest: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 983; Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1090, 1123.

LECTUS (BED) denotes rest of the flesh: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 459. — Rest of mind: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 72.

LEGUMINA (PULSES) can signify continence from lust and mortification of the body: Rabanus Maurus, CXI, 506.

LEX (LAW), charity: ibid., CXII, 984.

LIBANUS (LEBANON) conveys whiteness: Gillebert, CLXXXIV, 89, 148. — Virginity: ibid., 89–90. — Faith: ibid., 197.

LIBER (BOOK), the hidden things of a human being: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 987.

LIGNUM (WOOD), spiritual delights: ibid., 985. — Wood indicates a person’s repentance and strength: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 476. — Woods: spiritual virtues; good actions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 986. — All the woods of Lebanon are all virtues: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1173. — The good ordering of thoughts is denoted by shittim wood: Adam of Scotland, CXCVIII, 747.

LILIUM (LILY), good works; the whitenesses of truth: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 986. — The brightness of the eternal homeland: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 421. — The lily denotes virginity: ibid., CXI, 528. — Chastity and humility: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 71. — The splendour of the lily denotes the soul’s joyfulness: St Bernard, CLXXXIV, 673. — Sacred discourses: lilies: Gillebert, CLXXXIV, 142.

LIMEN (THRESHOLD), faith: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 986.

LINEA (LINE), the norm of suitable instruction: ibid., 987.

LINGUA (TONGUE), open speech: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 176.

[Col. 0205] LINUM (LINEN), subtlety; spiritual understanding: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 987.

LITTUS (SHORE), the end of the world; the stability of immortality: ibid.

LOCULUS (LITTLE PLACE), a good conscience: ibid., 989.

LOCUS (PLACE), innocence; love of the present life; holy conduct; holiness of life; anxieties of the mind: ibid., 988.

LOCUSTA (LOCUST), resurrection: ibid., 988.

LONGITUDO (LENGTH), long-suffering; faith: ibid., 989.

LORUM (STRAP), the precept of discipline; the bonds of our guardianship: ibid.

LUCERNA (LAMP), good work; divine grace; the word of preaching; good inward life; visitation: ibid. — Prayer: St Bernard, CLXXXV, 66. — Brightness of preaching; brightness of good works; empty joy: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 364. — Lamps denote good works: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1031.

LUCIFER (MORNING STAR), bright understanding: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 989.

LUMBI (LOINS), the propagation of mortality: ibid., 990. — Desire for praise: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 229.

LUMEN (LIGHT), intention of heart: St Eucherius, L, 741. — Knowledge of truth; preaching; miracle; grace of God; intention; doctrine: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 990.

LUNA (MOON), reputation accompanied by praise; mobility of mind; knowledge; adversity: ibid., 991. — The reputation of a good work; temporal mutability: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 40.

LUTUM (MUD), the first condition; doctrine: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 991.

LUX (LIGHT), good action; preaching; the glory of life; sword of the heart: ibid., 989. — Brightness of the eternal homeland; glory of the present life; empty joy; justice; brightness of preaching: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 361. — Light signifies prosperity: Philip of Harveng, CCIII, 1176.

MACERIA (WALL), discipline of heart; its side is faith and action: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 992. — The fortification of discipline; difficulties of perfection: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 393.

MALA (APPLES) are understood as the fruits of good action with a good fragrance—that is, the grace of a good reputation together with the fruits of good conduct: St Eucherius, L, 742. — Pomegranates: virtues: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 992. — Pomegranate: good actions: ibid., 992. — A symbol of fraternal union: Adam of Scotland, CXCVIII, 492. — Pomegranates: unity of faith: Garner of St Victor, CXCVIII, 349.

MAMMAE (BREASTS), natural faculties: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 992.

MANDRAGORAE (MANDRAKES), good reputation: ibid., 995.

MANE (MORNING), the light of human actions, or prosperity in the present life: St Eucherius, L, 741. — The beginning of faith; prosperity in the present life; the outset of the present life; inward consolation; brightness of the future life; the first age of the world; childhood: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 992; Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 368.

MANIPULUS (SHEAF), the fruit of justice: St Eucherius, L, 742. — Good works; the rewards of saints: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 995. — A sheaf signifies fruits worthy of repentance: Rupert, abbot, CLXX, 29.

MANNA enclosed in the ark, a symbol of grace: St Augustine, XXXIV, 733. — Heavenly blessedness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 995. — Manna signifies grace: Eugyppius, abbot, LXII, 678.

MANUS (HAND), power; impulse; discipline; grace; generosity; vengeance; good work; daytime persecution; discernment; spiritual concerns: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 993. — The active life; power; action; strength; the severe strictness of the law: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 194. — The hands of a human being beneath the wings of the living creatures in Ezekiel denote the twofold life: by the hands, the active life; by the wings, the contemplative: St Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 809. — In Scripture, hands are taken for works: Alcuin, C, 684. — Hand is taken for power: St Bruno the Carthusian, CLII, 717. — For impulse: ibid., 784. — For vengeance: ibid., 886. — For help: ibid., 1129.

MARE (SEA), secular action: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 995. — The unrest of secular persons: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 287. — The sea denotes a repentant heart: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 434.

MARGARITA (PEARL), heavenly desire; earthly delights: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 996.

MARGO (BORDER), faith: ibid., 995.

MARMOR (MARBLE), good firmness: ibid., 996.

MATUTINUM (MORNING), prosperity; exercise; justice; delay: ibid., 993.

MAXILLA (JAW), preaching: ibid., 997.

MEDULLA (MARROW), earthly riches; intentions: ibid. — Subtlety of intellect; riches; intentions of the flesh: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 219.

MEL (HONEY), spiritual wisdom; contemplation; sweetness of the flesh: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 997.

[Col. 0206] MENSES (MONTHS), limits of actions; good rest of mind: ibid.

MERIDIES (MIDDAY), the plain clarity of doctrines and deeds: St Eucherius, L, 741. — Tribulation; faith; ardour of charity: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 998. — Midday is called the blessed vision: St Bernard, CLXXXIII, 953.

MESSIS (HARVEST), open action; the present age: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 998. — The gift of right understanding: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 432.

MILITES (SOLDIERS), spiritual virtues: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 999.

MILITIA (MILITARY SERVICE), an arduous life: ibid.

MILLE ARGENTEI (A THOUSAND SILVER PIECES) denote all worldly substance: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 396. — The thousand shields hanging from David’s house are all the teachings of the virtues that fortify us: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1153. — The number one thousand denotes perfection: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 108.

MODIUS (MEASURE), temporal advantage; perfection: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1000.

MOENIA (WALLS), ornaments of virtues: ibid., 998.

MONILIA (NECKLACES), instruments of virtues: ibid., 1000. — A necklace denotes chastity: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 98.

MONS (MOUNTAIN), the loftiness of this world; inward contemplations: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1001. — A mountain: the height of a good life; the height of contemplation; the swelling pride of ecclesiastical dignities; lofty contemplations: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 252. — The Mount of Olives denotes the height of virtues and spiritual graces distributed to believers through the gift of the Holy Spirit: Rabanus Maurus, CXI, 361. — The mountain on which Lot is saved is perfection: Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 410. — The mountains upon which the beloved says that he comes leaping are eminent virtues: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1117. — Mountains denote contemplation: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 77, 78. — The mountains of spices: excellence of virtues: ibid., 109. — Chastity and humility are like mountains: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 175.

MORS (DEATH), extinction of secular life: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1002.

MORTARIOLUM (LITTLE MORTAR), martyrdoms: ibid., 1002.

MULIERES (WOMEN). Good and bad affections are denoted by the women contending before Solomon: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 523.

MUNITIONES (FORTIFICATIONS): Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1003.

MURENULAE (LITTLE CHAINS), ornaments of virtues: ibid.

MURUS (WALL), adversity of the world; discipline: ibid. — The defence of Christian faith; the fortification of discipline: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 392. — A wall denotes firmness: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 107.

MUSTUM (NEW WINE), spiritual fervour: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1003.

MYRRHA (MYRRH), mortification; endurance of suffering: ibid., 999. — Mortification: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 986, 987; Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1173; Alanus of Lille, CCX, 86. — Myrrh: sweetness of virtues: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 423. — Myrrh signifies incorruptibility and virginity: St Bruno the Carthusian, CLII, 829. — Myrrh and frankincense, symbols of perfected prayer: Gillebert, CLXXXIV, 148. — Myrrh and frankincense denote the bitterness of suffering: ibid., 646. — Faith, hope, and charity are represented by myrrh, frankincense, and every powder of the perfumer: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1132.

MYRTUS (MYRTLE), moderation of thought: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 999. — By the myrtle are signified the tribulations of neighbours, tempered by compassion through the consolation of the Word: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1275.

MYTRA (MITRE), stability of mind: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 999.

NARDUS (NARD), faith; inward charity; sweetness of mind: ibid., 1004. — Nard signifies charity: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1078. — Humility: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 854; St Bernard, CLXXXIII, 428, 989. — Humility fervent with charity: ibid., CLXXXIV, 428. — Rest of mind: Gillebert, CLXXXIV, 190.

NARES (NOSTRILS), snares that breathe forth; foreknowledge: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 171.

NASUS (NOSE), discernment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1004; Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 171; Alanus of Lille, CCX, 99.

NAVICULA (LITTLE BOAT) denotes heavenly rest: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 918, 923.

NEBULAE (MISTS), abolition of sins: St Eucherius, L, 739. — Mist is taken for light and for purity of heart: Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 696.

NEMUS (GROVE), the brilliance of secular eloquence: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1005.

NERVI (SINEWS), a forceful sentence of strictness: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 220.

NIDULUS (LITTLE NEST), simplicity: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1006.

NIDUS (NEST), a good conscience: St Eucherius, L, 748. — Faith; holy conduct: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1006.

[Col. 0207] NIGREDO (BLACKNESS), humility; outward tribulation; labour: ibid.

NITRUM (NITRE), outward cleanliness of the flesh: ibid.

NIX (SNOW), heavenly desire: ibid. — The brightness of heavenly life; the judgment of the supreme tribunal: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 63. — Snow sometimes signifies evil, sometimes good: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 776. — The whiteness of snow: justice: St Eucherius, L, 739.

NOVACULA (RAZOR) signifies the force of divine love: Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 857.

NOX (NIGHT), the present life; sadness: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 376.

NUBES (CLOUDS), temporal goods: ibid., 49.

NUMERUS DENARIUS (THE NUMBER TEN) signifies the Decalogue: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1137, 1212. — The number six signifies perfection: ibid.

OBRYZUM (REFINED GOLD), earthly riches: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1009.

OCCIDENS (WEST), old age: ibid., 1010.

OCTONARIUS NUMERUS (THE NUMBER EIGHT), resurrection of the flesh: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 450.

OCULUS (EYE), intention of heart; clarity of understanding; inward desire; work; outward sight; spiritual senses: ibid., 1009. — Intention of heart; one who enlightens by teaching; contemplative or active life; hope; actions: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 166. — The eye denotes intention: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 278. — Intention of mind: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1034. — Intention of work: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 927. — Contemplation: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 278.

ODOR (FRAGRANCE), the sweetness of holiness; good life; holiness of speech: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1010. — A good fragrance is a good example: Venerable Godefrid, abbot, CLXXIV, 408. — The fragrance of ointment, a symbol of repentance: ibid., 937.

OLEUM (OIL), inward grace; devotion of mind; charity; testimony of the heart; consolation; a mode of praise: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1011. — Oil is called divine grace: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 233. — Oil signifies good works: Alcuin, C, 705. — To have oil in vessels is to have the joy of good works in one’s conscience: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1043. — Charity is compared to oil: ibid., 1031.

OLIVA (OLIVE), mercy; works of the righteous: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1011. — The olive signifies charity: St Bernard, CLXXXIV, 733.

OLLA (POT), tribulation: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1011.

ONYCHA (ONYCHA), prayer: ibid., 1012.

ORGANUM (INSTRUMENT), joy of mind; preachings: ibid.

ORIENS (EAST), childhood; holiness of life: ibid. — The east is understood as justice: Philip of Harveng, CCIII, 949.

OS (MOUTH), the secret place of a good mind; speech: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1013. — Thought of heart; speech: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 173.

OS (BONE), strong deeds; strength of flesh: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1013. — Bone: virtues; the hardness of strength; strength of flesh: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 214.

OSCULUM (KISS), charity; deceptions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1014.

OSTIUM (DOORWAY), entrance into the heavenly kingdom; love of God and neighbour; desires of the flesh: ibid. — Faith, or the vision of God; beginning of divine knowledge; understanding; exit; barriers of divine fear; virtues: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 406. — A doorway is called obedience: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 86.

OVIS (SHEEP), innocence; pure thoughts: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1015. — Innocence of thoughts: Garner of St Victor, CXCIII, 105.

OVUM (EGG), hope: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1014.

PALEAE (CHAFF), necessities of life: ibid., 1018.

PALIURUS (CHRIST’S THORN), excuse: ibid., 1019.

PALLIUM (CLOAK), reverence; joy of heart; aid; consideration of one’s own weakness; action: ibid., 1018.

PALMA (PALM), perfection or victory: St Eucherius, L, 742. — Right intention; spiritual victories; eternal rewards: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1017. — A symbol of victory: Venerable Hildebert of Le Mans, CLXXI, 503; Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1193.

PALPEBRAE (EYELIDS), thoughts; inward counsels: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1018.

PANIS (BREAD), spiritual grace; good action; strength of charity; humility; consolation; sustenance of life; spiritual graces; understanding of the most holy Trinity; inward consolations: ibid., 1021. — By “bread” are understood delights: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 395.

PAPYRUS, secular knowledge: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1021.

PARADISUS (PARADISE), serenity of mind; temporal glory; heavenly joy: ibid., 1022. — The paradise of delight denotes the fullness of sweetness in Christ: Adam of Scotland, CXCVIII, 249. — The spiritual life is like paradise: Venerable Godefrid, CLXXIV, 145. — The four kinds of tears or compunction are denoted by the four rivers of paradise: Adam of Scotland, CXCVIII, 771.

[Col. 0208] PASCUA (PASTURES), spiritual refreshment: St Eucherius, L, 742.

PASTUS (FEEDING), instruction; the refreshment of inward wisdom: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1022.

PAX (PEACE), social love; rest of mind; tranquillity of contemplation; preaching; future rest; carnal agreement: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1016.

PAXILLUS (PEG), compunction: ibid., 1023.

PECCATUM (SIN), sacrifice for sin: ibid., 1024.

PECTUSCULUM (BREASTPIECE), correction: ibid.

PELLIS (SKIN), slight adversity; the surface of actions; the weak things of the world; bodily virtues: ibid., 1026. — Solomon’s skins denote the variety of virtues: Alanus of Lille, CCX, 57.

PENNAE (WINGS), the action of outward things; commandments of charity; moral virtues: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1026.

PENNULAE (LITTLE WINGS), holy desires: ibid.

PEPONES (MELONS), earthly sweetnesses: ibid.

PERA (BAG), the burden of the age; a devout mind: ibid., 1027.

PERSECUTIO (PERSECUTION) is a judgment by which a person is judged either approved or rejected: Tertullian, II, 103. — Persecution is that chaff which even now purifies the Lord’s threshing-floor, namely the Church, winnowing the mixed heap of believers—both the wheat of martyrs and the chaff of those who deny him: ibid. — Persecution is the ladders which Jacob dreams of, showing ascent to higher things for some and descent to lower things for others: ibid., 103.

**FOOT (PES):** preaching; the works of heavenly commandments; thoughts; intentions; afflictions; actions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1025.---**Feet (PEDES):** the steps of deeds; the two loves; thoughts: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 233.---Feet are affections: Alan of Lille, CCX, 86.---Affection and intellect are the feet of the soul: Venerable Abbot Godfrey, CLXXIV, 601.---The soul’s affections are denoted by feet: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 273.---The Lord’s feet are mercy and justice: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 935, 941.

**ROCK (PETRA):** faith; confession of faith; steadfastness in good action; spiritual strength; good examples; lofty contemplations: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1028.---Steadfastness of faith: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 349.

**BOWLS (PHIALAE):** signify abundance of tongues: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 774.---Spiritual things, ibid., 814.---Bowls: abundant preaching: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 459.

**PICTURES (PICTURAE):** varieties of virtues: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1028.

**HAIRS (PILI):** afflictions; weak thoughts, ibid.

**FINS OF FISH (PINULAE PISCIUM):** signify joyfulness: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 506.

**PINE (PINUS):** truth of faith: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1029.

**POOL (PISCINA):** compunction; the doctrine of preaching, ibid., 1030.

**FISH (PISCIS):** unfeigned faith: St. Eucherius, L, 742; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1030.---A fish signifies our good senses: Venerable Abbot Godfrey, CLXXIV, 815, 818.---The scales of fish signify patience: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 506.

**BLOW / WOUND (PLAGA):** a harsh stroke; transitory tribulation; corrections; afflictions; present infirmities: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1019.

**SOLE OF THE FOOT / PLANT (PLANTA):** discernment of heart; the end of the world, ibid.---The action of life; the end of life: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 238.

**STREET (PLATEA):** breadth of authority; liberty of one’s own will; the breadth of this present life, ibid., 259.

**BRAIDS (PLECTAE):** concord: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1026.

**RAIN (PLUVIA):** inward grace; holy preaching; temptation, ibid., 1034.---The grace of preaching: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 989.

**FRUITS (POMA):** good works: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1070.---The beginnings of our works: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 348.

**GATE (PORTA):** faith; a work of righteousness; departure from this life; moral virtues; the five bodily senses: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1031.---Faith; action; life’s departure; good actions: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 404.---A gate denotes good works or human hearts: Rabanus Maurus, CXI, 385.---In Ezekiel, the eastern gate is faith; the northern gate, hope; the southern gate, charity: St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 1021.

**SPOIL / PREY (PRAEDA):** the salvation of the elect; persecution: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1027.

**MANGER (PRAESEPE):** heavenly blessedness, ibid.---The manger is a type of monastic life: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 684.

**DEPTH (PROFUNDUM):** depth of thoughts: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 303.

**BATTLEMENTS (PROPUGNACULA):** miracles: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1032.

**FROST (PRUINA):** abstinence, because through it the heat of the body is cooled [Col. 0209]: St. Eucherius, L, 739.---Frost: heavenly beauty; temporal adversity; maturity in religious life: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1035.

**COALS (PRUNAE):** worldly consolations, ibid.

**BOYS / CHILDREN (PUERI):** circumspections of the heart: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 145.

**DUST (PULVIS):** fruitfulness of holiness; inward thought; worldly desire; worldly action; weak action; spiritual weakness; inward discernment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1033.---Earthly understanding; earthly business; subtlety of works; reconsideration: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 250.

**POINT (PUNCTUM):** haste; the brevity of this life: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1034.

**PURPLE (PURPURA):** the radiance of chastity, ibid.

**WELL (PUTEUS):** the depths of hearts: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 300.---The secret of contemplation; the secret of the heart: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1035.

**SQUARENESS (QUADRATURA):** spiritual squareness is faith, hope, charity, and action: Abbot Wolbero, CXCV, 1181.

**THE NUMBER FOUR (QUATERNARIUS):** the principal virtues; the four parts of the world: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 444.

**ROOT (RADIX):** holy preaching; intention; good perceptions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1036.---Holy preaching; hidden thought: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 342.

**BRANCHES (RAMI):** good affection; good works: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1037.---Branches: works; the words of a sentence: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 346.

**BREASTPLATE (RATIONALE):** inward purity: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1037.

**COUCH / RECLINING PLACE (RECLINATORIUM):** inward purity, ibid., 1039.

**KING (REX):** the inner senses; bodily senses, ibid., 1037.

**LAUGHTER (RISUS):** spiritual joy; worldly gladness, ibid., 1040.

**STREAM (RIVUS):** flows of preaching: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 296.

**DEW (ROS):** heavenly contemplation; fullness of holiness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1040.

**ROSE (ROSA):** delights of the present life, ibid.

**WHEEL (ROTA):** is a likeness of the human race: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 291.

**REDNESS (RUBOR):** heavenly desire: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1041.

**BURNING BUSH (RUBUS IGNEUS):** in which God appeared to Moses, prefigured His strength against the Egyptians: Rupert, CLXVII, 578.

**SABBATH (SABBATUM):** rest of mind and rest of eternity; works of holiness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1042.

**PRIEST (SACERDOS):** our reason, ibid.

**ARROW (SAGITTA):** words of preaching; manifest persecution; afflictions; snares, ibid., 1044.---Arrows: the striking force of preaching and correction: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 326.

**SALT (SAL):** spiritual understanding; wisdom; discernment; admonition: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1044.---The sun signifies discernment: Rupert, CLXVII, 753, 1258.---Wisdom: Rabanus Maurus, CXI, 460; Abbot Wolbero, CXCV, 1224.

**SPITTLE (SALIVA):** the savor of contemplation; wisdom: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 181.

**SALINITY (SALSUGO):** good desire; holiness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1045.

**PSALTERY (SALTERIUM):** good action, ibid.

**WOODLAND / FOREST (SALTUS):** works are denoted by woodland: Abbot Wolbero, CXCV, 1037.

**SAPPHIRE (SAPPHIRUS):** holy contemplation: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1044.

**FRYING-PAN (SARTAGO):** zeal for souls; tribulation, ibid., 1046.

**LADDER (SCALA):** charity, ibid., 1043.

**SHOULDER (SCAPULA):** exercise in good work; defenses, ibid.

**SHIELD (SCUTUM):** protection; judgment; excuses, ibid., 1061.---A shield: human resistance: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 321.

**AXE (SECURIS):** correction; the gift of grace; grievous persecution: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1047.---The gift of understanding; the pronouncement of strict correction; rebuke: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 328.

**SEED (SEMEN):** divine preaching: St. Eucherius, L, 742.---A good work; speech of the mouth: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1048.

**PATH (SEMITA):** humility; inward thought; perfection, ibid., 1049.---Action; narrowness; regular life; subtle preachings; thoughts: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 264.

**THE NUMBER SIX (SENARIUS):** perfection of a thing; perfection of the active life; the six ages of the world, ibid., 445.

**OLD AGE (SENECTUS):** maturity of perfection; failure of strength: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1049.

**HEDGE (SEPES):** good commandments, ibid.

**THE NUMBER SEVEN (SEPTENARIUS):** the summit of perfection; the ensuing [Col. 0210] rest of eternity; the totality of temporal things: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 448.

**TOMB (SEPULCRUM):** the secret of contemplation: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1050.

**SERPENT (SERPENS):** faith is compared to the serpent’s head: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 266.

**WHISTLE / HISSING (SIBILUS):** amazement; divine inspiration; admonitions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1053.

**SEAL (SIGNACULUM):** the virtue of chastity, ibid.

**FLINT (SILEX):** good action, ibid., 1054.

**FINE FLOUR (SIMILAGO):** purity of heart, ibid.

**FINE LINEN (SINDO):** subtle preaching; worldly occupation, ibid.

**LEFT HAND / LEFT SIDE (SINISTRA):** delight in human praise; adversity, ibid., 1055.---The glory of the present life: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 200.---The left side signifies adversity: Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 1426; Alan of Lille, CCX, 56.

**BOSOM (SINUS):** security; secret rest: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1054.

**THIRST (SITIS):** good desire, ibid., 1057.

**SUN (SOL):** preaching; charity; joy; contemplation; zeal for righteousness; the heat of temptation; tribulation; the acuteness of the wise; present time; the brightness of the heavenly homeland, ibid.---The sun is called persecution; the making manifest of some matter; the radiance of a good work; the fervor of love; the light of truth; the burning of temptation: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 37.

**SOLITUDE (SOLITUDO):** rest of mind: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1059; Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 269.

**THRONE (SOLIUM):** elevation of mind; seat of counsel; worldly eminence: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1058.

**SLEEP (SOMNUS):** death of the flesh; rest of mind, ibid., 1059.

**SOUND (SONUS):** faith; the groaning of repentance, ibid.

**MIRROR (SPECULUM):** faith; good examples, ibid., 1050.

**CAVE / DEN (SPECUS):** the inward parts of the heart, ibid., 1051.

**CAVERN (SPELUNCA):** holiness of life, ibid., 1050.

**LITTLE SPHERES (SPHAERULAE):** the revolutions of thought, ibid.

**EAR OF GRAIN (SPICA):** good works; the fruitfulness of years, ibid., 1055.---Progress in good work: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 434.

**THORN (SPINA):** compunction for sins; fearful suspicions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1056.---Spiritual doctrine; strength; the stings of temptations; riches: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 339.

**SPIRIT / WIND (SPIRITUS):** a sharp wind; fear of the Lord: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1056.---Spirit is called spiritual affection; inward thought; wind: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 155.

**SCALES (SQUAMAE):** the strengths of good works: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1046.

**STACTE (STACTES):** prayer, ibid.

**BALANCE (STATERA):** discernment; judgments, ibid., 1047.

**STATURE (STATURA):** holy conduct; strength; progress, ibid.

**STAR (STELLA):** faith, ibid., 1052.

**DUNG (STERCUS):** remembrance of sins, ibid., 1053.---A transitory thing: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 278.

**SNEEZING (STERNUTATIO):** agitation: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1053.

**DROPS (STILLICIDIA):** words of preachers: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 303.

**ROBE (STOLA):** the virtue of innocence; new joy; heavenly glory; good works; thoughts; the adornment of the external senses, ibid., 1060.

**STYLUS (STYLUS):** a forceful judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1057.

**AWL (SUBULA):** subtlety of speech, ibid.

**PRIDE (SUPERBIA):** authority, ibid., 1061.

**EPHOD / SHOULDER-GARMENT (SUPERHUMERALE):** strength in good work, ibid.

**LINTEL (SUPERLIMEN):** the intention of the mind: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 406.

**TABERNACLE (TABERNACULUM):** heavenly homeland; conduct; earthly happiness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1062.---A tabernacle: the dwelling of the mind; bodily habitation; thoughts; the construction of earthly happiness: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 396.

**TABLETS (TABULAE):** knowledge and power; breadth of heart; breadth of work: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1062.

**TALENT (TALENTUM):** understanding; a good weight; bodily senses; understanding and action, ibid., 1063.---Talents: gifts of grace: Garner of St. Victor, CXIII, 307.

**ANKLE (TALUM):** life’s limit: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 237.

**WEB (TELA):** the brevity of this life: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1064.

**TEMPLE (TEMPLUM):** the devout mind; the capacity of human understanding, ibid.---The temple is a house of delights: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 461.---The temple is signified by Lebanon, ibid., 1783.

**DARKNESS (TENEBRAE):** adversities: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 378.

[Col. 0211] **THE NUMBER THREE (TERNARIUS):** the three theological virtues; the three times of life, ibid., 442.

**EARTH (TERRA):** the holy mind: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1065.---Earth is called the firmness of the heavenly homeland; earthly action: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 239.

**POTSHERD (TESTA):** the force of strictness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1066.

**BRIDAL CHAMBER (THALAMUS):** the devout mind, ibid., 1063.

**TREASURE (THESAURUS):** heavenly reward; good desire; holy speech; good intention, ibid., 1066.

**CENSERS (THURIBULA):** denote actions: Alan of Lille, CCX, 270.

**INCENSE (THUS):** devotion in prayer: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1070.---The offering of love; the virtue of prayer: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 423.---Incense signifies contemplation: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 986, 987.---Prayer: Abbot Wolbero, CXCV, 1156.

**INCENSE / PERFUME (THYMIAMA):** devotion in prayer: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1067.

**TIARA (TIARA):** the adornment of virtues, ibid.

**FEAR (TIMOR):** is the guardian of grace: St. Bernard, CLXXXII, 577.---A savor, ibid., CLXXXIII, 892.---Fear is compared to water, ibid., 879, 1044.

**DYES (TINCTURAE):** adornments of virtues: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1067.

**MOTH (TINEA):** temptation, ibid.

**BELLS (TINTINNABULA):** sounds of preaching, ibid.

**THUNDER (TONITRUS):** threatening; rebukes, ibid., 1068.---Preaching of heavenly terror: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 62.

**TOPAZ (TOPAZION):** things precious in this world: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1068.

**TORRENT (TORRENS):** the flow of life, ibid.---The course of mortal life: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 297.

**BEAMS (TRABES):** signify faith: Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 1150.

**THREE HUNDRED (TRECENTI):** Abraham’s victory over four kings with three hundred servants mystically signified the victory which the Christian person must obtain over four enemies: St. Paulinus of Nola, LXI, 300.

**THISTLE (TRIBULUS):** piercing of the heart: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1067.

**WHEAT (TRITICUM):** the word of preaching; good work, ibid., 1067.---The Lord’s wheat are the humble and the righteous: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 1363.

**TRUMPET (TUBA):** the sound of preaching; human favor; the two commandments of charity; preaching: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1069.

**TUNIC (TUNICA):** completed action; worldly occupation; inward sins, ibid.---Joseph’s ankle-length tunic is a good work continued unto completion: Abbot Wolbero, CXCV, 1053.---A tunic denotes worldly care: Alan of Lille, CCX, 85.

**TOWER (TURRIS):** strength of preaching; the virtue of humility: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1070.---Circumspection; the height of grace: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 394.

**TURTLEDOVE (TURTUR):** love of God; secret compunction: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1069.---Spiritual understanding or chastity: St. Eucherius, L, 748.---An example of chastity; a form of simplicity: St. Bernard, CLXXXIV, 337.

**TAMBOURINE (TYMPANUM):** good work: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1067.---The tambourine represents the mortification of the flesh: St. Bruno the Carthusian, CLII, 1169.

**BREASTS (UBERA):** are called the two commandments of charity: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1084.---Congratulation and compassion: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 749, 754, 819.---Arguments of a gross hope: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 221.---The bridegroom’s two breasts are long-suffering and kindness: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 816.---Forgiveness of sins and distribution of gifts: Abbot Wolbero, CXCV, 1023.---Adversity and prosperity are the bride’s two breasts, between which is the beloved: St. Bernard, CLXXXIV, 646.

**NAVEL (UMBILICUS):** denotes charity: Alan of Lille, CCX, 98.

**SHADOW (UMBRA):** illumination of faith; life: St. Eucherius, L, 741.---The refreshment of consolation; forgetfulness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1085.---Refreshment of mind; torpor of mind; obscurity of allegory; instability of life; forgetfulness; the refreshment of eternal rest; perfection of mind; our actions: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 383.---A shadow signifies labor: CXCV, 1156.

**OINTMENT (UNGUENTUM):** holy conduct: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1085.---Ointment signifies the best grace: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 1287.

**NAILS (UNGUES):** the end of every thing: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 240.

**HOOF (UNGULA):** perfection; final works; the ends of this world: [Col. 0212] Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1085.---Perfection of virtues: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 240.

**ONLY ONE / ONLY BELOVED (UNICA):** our soul: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1085.

**UNITY (UNITAS):** is called the beginning of living well: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 437.

**WATERSKIN (UTER):** denotes temperance: Venerable Guibert, CLVI, 162.

**GRAPES (UVAE):** fruits of righteousness: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

**WIFE (UXOR):** a good example; good action; good will: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1087.---Good activity: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 142.

**SHEATH (VAGINA):** mercy: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1072.

**“AH!” (VAH):** joy of mind; reproach of evils, ibid., 1071.

**VALLEY (VALLIS):** the present life; the humble mind, ibid., 1072.---Valleys are called the contritions of a humble heart: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

**VAPOR (VAPOR):** the state of the present life: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1072.

**VESSEL (VAS):** love of the present life; fervor of love, ibid., 1086.

**VEIN (VENA):** the sublimity of inward speech, ibid., 1073.

**BELLY (VENTER):** our conduct; a contrite heart; human memory, ibid., 1071.---The mind; our weakness: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 226.---A belly distinguished with sapphires is bodily chastity adorned by chastity of mind: Abbot Wolbero, CXCV, 1198.---The belly denotes memory: Alan of Lille, CCX, 86.

**WIND (VENTUS):** the present life; tribulation; persecution; inward temptation: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1071.---Winds: transitory prosperity; the shaking inflicted by the strict Judge: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 51.

**SPRING (VER):** the beginning of a good work: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1075.

**CROWN OF THE HEAD (VERTEX):** the mind’s reason; holiness, ibid., 1075.---Faith: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 162.

**EVENING (VESPERA):** temptation; life’s end; adversity; the end of the world: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1077.---Evening: life’s end; adversity; the torpor of idleness; temptation to sin: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 374.---In the evening: perfection: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1076.

**VESTIBULE (VESTIBULUM):** humility; faith: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 415.

**GARMENT (VESTIMENTUM):** good work; works of righteousness; good examples: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1075.---Good works are likened to garments: Gillebert, CLXXXIV, 180.

**CLOTHING (VESTIS):** charity: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1076.

**WAY (VIA):** good conduct; the rectitude of churches; our life; rectitude in the present life; the Creator’s works; inward thoughts; our actions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1077.---Charity: Peter Lombard, CXCI, 1244.---The path of rectitude; the breadth of one’s own liberty; holy conduct; our actions; modes of living: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 260.

**VINEYARD (VINEA):** signifies the actions of good works: Rabanus Maurus, CXI, 507.---The fruit of the vineyard is charity: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 1070.

**WINE (VINUM):** spiritual understanding; compunction; correction; contemplation; vengeance: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1078.---The gift of charity is rightly represented by the name of wine: St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 46.---By wine are understood the fervor of charity and love: Cassiodorus, LXX, 1100.---Charity is compared to wine: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 743, 1044.---The commandment concerning charity is compared to wine: Abbot Wolbero, CXCV, 1097.---Wine represents earthly delight: Alan of Lille, CCX, 227.---Wine is called virginity that gladdens God: Venerable Guibert, CLVI, 497.

**VIOLET (VIOLA):** a symbol of humility: St. Bernard, CLXXXIV, 667.

**MAN (VIR):** understanding; our spirit; bodily sense: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1080.

**ROD (VIRGA):** faith; correction; divine chastisement, ibid., CXII, 1081.---Rectitude; a stroke; discipline; severity: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 345.

**VIRGINITY (VIRGINITAS):** denotes the barrenness of the soul: Adam the Scot, CXCVIII, 363.

**GREEN CIRCLE (VIRIDIS CIRCULUS):** a sign of eternal blessedness, ibid., 702.

**VISCERA / INNER PARTS (VISCERA):** affections of the heart: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1081.

**LIFE (VITA):** temporal glory; approval of outward action, ibid.---The active and contemplative life are represented by sons and daughters: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 693.---By doves and turtledoves, ibid., 710.

**VINE (VITIS):** a symbol of humility and obedience: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 821.---The vine’s fruit is charity: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 832.---Vine: faith: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1081.

[Col. 0213] **GLASSY (VITREUS):** innocence is signified by the glassy sea: Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 643.

**BAND / FILLET (VITTA):** holy preaching; hope of heavenly things: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1082.

**BIRDS (VOLUCRES):** denote spiritual subtlety: Venerable Guibert, CLVI, 104.

**PLOUGHSHARE (VOMER):** preachings: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1083.

**VOICE (VOX):** contemplation; the preaching of teachers; compunction; the terror of persecution, ibid.

**WOUND (VULNUS):** tribulation; charity; the pain of a scourge; our distresses, ibid., 1084.---Christ’s spiritual wounds within us are fear and love: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 771.

**COUNTENANCE (VULTUS):** knowledge of truth: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1083.

**ZEAL (ZELUS):** is called spiritual fervor, ibid., 1088.

**BELT (ZONA):** the bond of charity; discipline of mind; mortification of the flesh, ibid.

## II.---Vices

**ABYSS (ABYSSUS):** confusions arising from evil works: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 852.---The depth of avarice: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 348.

**VINEGAR (ACETUM):** deceit; unbelief: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 853.

**FAT (ADEPS):** carnal joy, ibid., 854.---Pride: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 213.

**THE EGYPTIAN WOMAN** who solicits Joseph is a type of lust: Adam the Scot, CXCVIII, 814.

**EGYPT (AEGYPTUS):** darkness; sins of unbelief: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 915.---By the name Egypt, the darkness of this world is denoted: St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 409.---Egypt is denoted by Pharaoh’s daughter: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 291.

**BRONZE (AES):** an unfeeling heart: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 917.

**WINGS (ALAE):** signify pride: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 80.

**FILM ON THE EYE (ALBUGO):** blindness of heart; arrogance of mind: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 857.

**ALOES (ALOE):** pleasure of the flesh, ibid.

**AMBITION (AMBITIO):** is worship of the devil: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 198.---It is compared to a dragon, ibid., 241.

**AMPHORA (AMPHORA):** avarice: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 858; Garner, CXCIII, 460.

**ANIMALS (ANIMALIA):** irrational movements of the soul, ibid., 93.

**WATER (AQUA):** erroneous knowledge; prosperity of this world; subtle talkativeness; desire for the world; worldly prosperity; adversity; pleasure of the flesh; the learning of heretics; persecutions; unstable thoughts; the blandishments of temptations: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 860.---Erroneous knowledge; slippery hearts: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 279.---Water denotes original sin and concupiscence: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 720.---Actual sins, ibid., 806.---Waters: temptations: St. Eucherius, L, 742.---Waters customarily denote erroneous learning or tribulation: St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 100.---Waters denote tribulation: Alan of Lille, CCX, 106.

**EAGLE (AQUILA):** earthly things: St. Eucherius, L, 748.

**NORTH WIND (AQUILO):** the coldness of sins, ibid., 739.---The severity of persecution: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 860.---A sign of pride: St. Bernard, CLXXXIV, 1130; Alan of Lille, CCX, 133.

**TREE (ARBOR):** evil will: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 865.

**BOW (ARCUS):** hidden malice; threats, ibid., 862.---Bows denote deceitful temptations: Richard of St. Victor, CXCVI, 663.

**SAND (ARENA):** is called love of the world; the frailty of things: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 849.

**SILVER (ARGENTUM):** by silver is understood every earthly substance: St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 545.

**RAM (ARIES):** a movement of anger: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 863.

**ARMS / WEAPONS (ARMA):** open assaults, ibid., 864.---Weapons denote violent temptations: Richard of St. Victor, CXCVI, 663.

**REED (ARUNDO):** a symbol of inconstancy: Venerable Abbot Godfrey, CLXXIV, 66, 69.

**SHE-ASS (ASINA):** lustful movements of the heart: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 90.

**ASS (ASINUS):** lust; evil life, ibid., 88.---Asses signify carnal love: Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 412.

**ASP (ASPIS):** a flattering and hidden suggestion: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 129.

**SOUTH WIND (AUSTER):** the blandishments of the world: Rabanus Maurus, CXI, 262.---A lax life: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 56.

**BIRD (AVIS):** frivolity of words: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 871.---Birds are called superfluous thoughts: St. Eucherius, L, 748.---Birds: thoughts: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 65.---The birds which Abraham drove away signify the Egyptians: Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 385.

[Col. 0214] **BABYLONIA:** the city of the devil: Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 1510.

**BABYLON:** is called sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 872.---The king of Babylon is a type of the devil: Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 1500.

**BEL:** Lust is like the idol Bel destroyed by Daniel: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 255.---By the altar of the idol Bel is signified every instance of simony: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 91, 124, 366.

**WAR (BELLUM):** persecution; adversity of the world; conflict with vices: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 874.

**BEAST (BESTIA):** grave sin; unstable movements of the heart, ibid., 875.---Beasts: movements of the flesh: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 106.---Vices are compared to beasts: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 1120, 1128.

**BITUMEN (BITUMEN):** the hardness of discord: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 876.

**OX (BOS):** desires of the senses; exaltations of the heart, ibid., 876.

**LOCUST (BRUCHUS):** gluttony in eating, ibid., 877.

**TRUMPET (BUCCINA):** persecution, ibid.

**BUTTER (BUTYRUM):** promptings of the flesh, ibid.

**ABSALOM’S HAIR (CAESARIES ABSALON):** superfluity of temporal goods: Adam the Scot, CXCVIII, 816.

**SHOE (CALCEAMENTUM):** death-dealing action; outward evils: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 880.

**PEBBLE (CALCULUS):** the punishment of a lying tongue, ibid.

**GLOOM (CALIGO):** is called confusion of mind; sin, ibid., 879.

**CUP (CALIX):** worldly pleasure, ibid.

**PATH (CALLIS):** perverse doctrines, ibid., 880.

**CAMEL (CAMELUS):** the strength of vices, ibid., 882.

**CRAB (CANCER):** the usury of sin is like a crab: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 157.

**HAIR (CAPILLI):** denotes abundance of earthly substance: St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 35.

**HEAD (CAPUT):** grave vices: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 884.

**PRISON (CARCER):** the weight of our corruption; tribulation, ibid., 886.

**FLESH (CARO):** sin; carnal love; the corruption of mortality; carnal wisdom; concupiscence; softness; weak works, ibid.---Carnal life; carnal delight; carnality; weakness of work; the punishment of the flesh or vices; movements of the flesh: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 207.---When flesh is taken to mean corruption, it is said not to possess the kingdom of God: St. Augustine, XXXIII, 948.---By the terms “flesh and blood,” the Apostle designated corruption itself of flesh and blood, or the works of flesh and blood: XXXIII, 943, 945, 946; XXXIX, 1625.---Flesh and blood signify sins: Rupert, CLXVIII, 466.

**CARODION:** the vice of talkativeness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 887.

**CARTILAGE (CARTILAGO):** pretence: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 217.

**CHAINS (CATENAE):** the bonds of vices: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 890.

**CHAIR (CATHEDRA):** evil teaching, ibid., 889.

**TAIL (CAUDA):** disgrace; blandishments, ibid., 890.

**CEDARS (CEDRI):** denote the arrogance of pride: Richard, CXCVI, 295.

**ONION (CEPA):** The Fathers describe the nature of vainglory after the manner of onions and bulbs: when one covering has been peeled off, they are found clothed again in another, and are discovered to be covered as often as they have been stripped: John Cassian, XLIX, 404.

**NECK (CERVIX):** pride: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 393; Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 161.

**FOOD (CIBUS):** love of the world: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 893.

**SCARS (CICATRICES):** sins, ibid., 894.

**HAIR-SHIRT (CILICIUM):** signifies sin: St. Anselm of Canterbury, CLVIII, 635.

**KEY (CLAVIS):** enclosure of an ungodly heart: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 881.

**OVEN (CLIBANUS):** torment of flesh and soul, ibid., 894.

**SHIELD (CLYPEUM):** pride, ibid., 895.

**KNOWLEDGE (COGNITIO):** sexual intercourse, ibid., 901.

**HILLS (COLLES):** heights, ibid., 900.

**NECK (COLLUM):** the extension of pride: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 190.---An outstretched neck signifies pride: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 944.

**COLOR (COLOR):** evil conduct: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 900.

**TO EAT (COMEDERE):** to harass; to slander, ibid.

**COUNSEL (CONSILIUM):** Isaiah calls every spectacle “the counsel of the ungodly,” from the genus to the species: Tertullian, I, 635.

**BASKET (COPHINUS):** servile work; corruption: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 898.

**HORN (CORNU):** pride, ibid., 903; St. Bruno the Carthusian, CLII, 1017.

**BODY (CORPUS):** sin; corruption: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 902.

[Col. 0215] **RAVEN (CORVUS):** the blackness of sins: St. Eucherius, L, 748.---The raven released from the ark signified malice: St. Ambrose, XIV, 391.

**QUAIL (COTURNIX):** carnal pleasures: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 904.

**LEG (CRUS):** corruption, ibid., 905.

**CRYSTAL (CRYSTALLUS):** hardness of heart, ibid., 896.

**BEDCHAMBER (CUBILE):** an evil mind, ibid., 901.

**CHARIOT (CURRUS):** great sins; unstable worldly things, ibid., 905.

**SKIN (CUTIS):** softness; sin, ibid.---The softness of weakness; sin of the flesh: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 203.

**SWAN (CYGNUS):** pride: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 894.

**CYMBAL (CYMBALUM):** the vice of talkativeness, ibid., 895.

**GNATS AND DOG-FLIES (CYNIPHES ET CINOMYA):** denote flattery and slander: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 140.

**TEETH (DENTES):** are called the vices of gluttony; hardnesses; cruelties: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 907.---Evil suggestions: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 178.

**DAY (DIES):** delight in sin; heat of temptation; the eternity of day: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 909.---Day is called delight in sin: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 370.

**FLOOD (DILUVIUM):** sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 911.

**HOUSE (DOMUS):** evil thoughts, ibid.

**SLEEPING (DORMITIO):** torpor; sickness; blindness; falling; sexual intercourse, ibid., 913.

**DRAGON (DRACO):** malice: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 124.

**LEADER (DUX):** principal vices: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 913; Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 151.

**DRUNKENNESS (EBRIETAS):** is called error: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 914.

**EDOM:** sin, ibid.

**KID (EDUS):** correction; sins of the flesh; unclean thoughts, ibid.

**HORSE (EQUUS):** denotes the deceptive prosperity of the world: Peter Lombard, CXCI, 334.---A horse is called a slippery life: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 87.---Lust is like horses: Venerable Godfrey, CXLIV, 78.

**HEDGEHOGS (ERINACII):** the vice of excuse-making: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 917.

**CATERPILLAR (ERUCA):** lust, ibid., 916; Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 134.

**RUST (ERUGO):** pride: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 916.

**EXACTOR / TAX-COLLECTOR (EXACTOR):** the concupiscence of the belly; evil habit, ibid., 918.

**ARMY (EXERCITUS):** vices, ibid.

**ISSUE / DEPARTURE (EXITUS):** failure, ibid., 919.

**HUNGER (FAMES):** lack of virtue; temptation; evil silence, ibid., 921.

**FLOUR (FARINA):** the thought of an evil person, ibid.

**BUNDLE (FASCICULUS):** sins are so called, ibid., 920.

**HONEYCOMB (FAVUS):** worldly pleasure, ibid., 922.

**GALL (FEL):** unbelief, ibid., 923.

**WOMAN (FEMINA):** carnal affection, ibid.

**THIGH (FEMUR):** delight of the flesh, ibid.; Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 231; Alan of Lille, CCX, 87.

**HAY (FENUM):** vain glory: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

**WILD BEAST (FERA):** like a most evil wild beast: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 201.

**LEAVEN (FERMENTUM):** pride; pretence; malice; desire for praise: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 924.---Leaven signifies corruption: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 106.---The old leaven is called sin: Richard of St. Victor, CXCVI, 1074.

**IRON (FERRUM):** the habit of sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 925.

**DREGS (FEX):** sins, ibid.

**FIG (FICUS):** By fig leaves is signified the itch of lust: St. Augustine, XXXVIII, 442.

**FLAME (FLAMMA):** pleasure; the vehemence of evil desire: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 921.---The heat of carnal desires: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 358.

**FLOWER (FLOS):** the praise of hypocrites: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 929.

**WAVES (FLUCTUS):** temptations: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

**RIVER (FLUMEN):** is the doctrine of heretics: Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 1760.

**LEAVES (FOLIA):** lightness of mind: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 347.

**FOUNTAIN (FONS):** the penalty of mortality; the sin of avarice; sins: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 929.

**FURNACE (FORNAX):** the burning of concupiscence, ibid., 931.

**DITCH (FOSSA):** earthly desire, ibid., 932.

**PIT (FOVEA):** the malice of deception; the vice of excuse-making; earthly desire, ibid.

**SWORD (FRAMEA):** temptations, ibid., 922.

**BRIDLE (FRENUM):** ignorance, ibid., 925.

**FOREHEAD (FRONS):** shamelessness of flesh or heart, ibid., 971.

**GRAIN (FRUMENTUM):** delight of the flesh, ibid., 938.

[Col. 0216] **FLIGHT (FUGA):** fear of slaughter; failure, ibid., 933.

**SMOKE (FUMUS):** the pride of evil teaching, ibid., 935.---Smoke signifies blindness: Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 1291.

**FOUNDATION (FUNDAMENTUM):** carnal delights: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 935.

**CORD (FUNICULUS):** evil delights, ibid., 937.

**NATION (GENS):** vices, ibid., 944.

**GIANT (GIGAS):** grave sin, ibid., 946.---Giants signify proud movements of the soul: Venerable Guibert, CLVI, 86.

**ICE (GLACIES):** the hardness of sins: St. Eucherius, L, 739.

**SWORD (GLADIUS):** a word of corruption; speech of detraction; evil persuasion; vengeance; sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 940.---Anger: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 322.---A hidden sword is flattery: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 142.

**HAIL (GRANDO):** violent plundering: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 943.---By snow and hail are understood bodily afflictions: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 358.

**SPEAR (HASTA):** is called pride: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 948.

**GRASS / HERB (HERBA):** luxuriant and slippery concupiscence; carnal pleasures, ibid., 950.---Herbs filled with thorns: vices and the inflictions of temptations: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

**WINTER (HIEMS):** the present life; persecution or tribulation: St. Eucherius, L, 741.---Abundance of iniquity; malice: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 953.---The present life is represented by winter: St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 498.---Winter signifies sin: Abbot Rupert, CLXVIII, 867.---Winter denotes unbelief: Alan of Lille, CCX, 69.

**GOAT (HIRCUS):** movements of lust; impurities of the flesh: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 954.

**KID (HOEDUS):** appetite of the flesh, ibid., 953.---Kids are called movements of the flesh: St. Eucherius, L, 752.

**MAN (HOMO):** guilt; weakness: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 135.

**MOISTURE (HUMOR):** concupiscence of the flesh: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 959.

**FIRE (IGNIS):** is called the avaricious person; vengeance; the madness of impatience; lust; concupiscence; indignation; anger, ibid., 966.---Malice; lust; avarice; envy: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 355.---Usury is compared to sacred fire: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 157.

**IMAGE (IMAGO):** evil examples: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 969.

**IMPETIGO:** avarice, ibid.

**HELL (INFERNUS):** avarice; despair; grave sin, ibid., 970.

**ENVY (INVIDIA):** is signified by a sorrowful heart: Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 1275.---Envy is the mother of detraction: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 53.---Envy is compared to a worm: Alan of Lille, CCX, 128.

**JERICHO:** is a figure of worldly pleasures: St. John Damascene, XIII, 350.

**YOKE (JUGUM):** sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 972.

**JUNIPER (JUNIPERUS):** sins are so called, ibid.

**WILD VINES (LABRUSCAE):** are called vices, ibid., 977.

**MILK (LAC):** the blandishment of sin, ibid., 978.---Pride is compared to curdled milk: Peter the Chanter, CCV, 46.

**LAKE (LACUS):** the calamity of the world; corruption of the flesh; vices: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 978.---Sin: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 302.

**LAMIA:** pretence: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 979.

**SPEARS (LANCEAE):** darts of temptation; premeditated deceits, ibid., 980.

**STONE (LAPIS):** hardness of heart; a hard habit of sin; the hard hearts of gentiles: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 350.---Stone: hardness of heart: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 981.

**COFFERED CEILINGS (LAQUEARIA):** represent weaknesses: Alan of Lille, CCX, 64.

**NOOSE (LAQUEUS):** suggestion; deception: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 982.

**BED (LECTUS):** flesh; concupiscence; delight of the flesh; a reprobate sense, ibid., 983.

**LEPROSY (LEPRA):** sin or false doctrine, ibid., 985.---Spiritual leprosy: sin: Alan of Lille, CCX, 279.

**LAW (LEX):** corruption; the stimuli of the flesh: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 984.

**WOOD (LIGNUM):** the deceits of iniquity, ibid., 985. **Woods (LIGNA):** vices; envious thoughts, ibid., 986.---Wood is called insensibility of mind: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 329.

**TONGUE (LINGUA):** the doctrine of falsehood, ibid., 176.

**BLEARY-EYED PERSON (LIPPUS):** gloom of mind: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 987.

**SHORE (LITTUS):** the end of the world: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

**CASKET / SMALL COMPARTMENT (LOCULUS):** an evil conscience: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 989.

**LOCUST (LOCUSTA):** vain glory, ibid., 988.

**LOINS (LUMBI):** lust, ibid., 990.---Lust: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 229.

**WOLF (LUPUS):** fraud and deceit: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 991.

LUTUM, the sticky mire of sins: St. Eucherius, L, 742.---Worldly things, the enticement of the flesh, the stench of vices: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 991.

LUTUS, the enticement of carnal desire: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 276.

MACULA is sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 992.

MAGI. Hypocrisy is figured by the magi: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 450.

MALLEUS, a heavenly blow: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 997.

MALUM, adversity, ibid., 992.

MAMMAE, the preaching of error: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 223.

MORNING and evening signify mutability: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 135.

MANUS is taken to mean vengeance: St. Bruno the Carthusian, CLII, 886.

MARE, the world: St. Eucherius, L, 742.---The sea signifies worldly wisdom or the present age, heaving with the waves of persecutions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 311.---The sea is taken to mean bitterness: St. Bruno the Carthusian, CLII, 939.

MAXILLA signifies the throat: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 174.

MOAB, sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1000.

MONILIA, the blandishments of vices, ibid.

MONS, proud hearts, ibid., 1001.

MORS, pride, heavenly hatred, sin, ibid., 1002.---Carnal habit is signified by death: St. Augustine, XL, 79.---By the name of death, sin is meant: Alcuin, C, 431.---Every worldly enticement is called the gate of death: Rabanus Maurus, CXI, 385.

MULIER, the vanity of the world, cruelty, heretical doctrine, impiety: idem, CXII, 1002.---Impiety, weakness, vices: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 147.---Woman is a type of soft or self-indulgent life: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 825.

MURUS signifies vain hope: Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 390.---A wall: an impediment to doing good: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 392.

MUSCA, the filth of idolatry: St. Eucherius, L, 748.---Restlessness of heart: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1003.---Insolent cares: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 84.

MUSTUM, the vehemence of a depraved mind: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1003.

MYRRH signifies bitter things and the harshness of tribulations: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 993.

NARES denote expectation and foolishness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1004.

NEBULA, ignorance, ibid., 1005.

NERVUS, affliction, ibid.

NIGREDO, an evil conscience, ibid., 1006.

NITRUM, a perverse mind, ibid.

NIX sometimes signifies good, sometimes evil: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 176.

NOX, iniquity, unbelief, adversities, error, the blindness of ignorance: St. Eucherius, L, 741.---Tribulation, ignorance, sin, the darkness of the world, afflictions: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1007.---The life of the world: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 105.---Ignorance, ibid., 1196.---Consent to guilt, the darkness of ignorance: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 376.---Night commonly signifies adversity: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 183, 956.

NUBES is called the darkness of ignorance: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 49.---A cloud signifies goodness: Adam the Scot, CXCVIII, 788.

OCCIDENS, the failure of a better life: St. Eucherius, L, 741.---Failure of virtue: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1010.

OCULUS, concupiscence, unlawful thoughts, movements of the heart, harsher looks, ibid., 1009.---The eye signifies ignorance: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 927.

OLEUM signifies flattery: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 180.

OLLA, the carnal heart, carnal works: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 459.

ORTUS, pleasure: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1013.

OSTIUM, desires of the flesh: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 406.

OS, depraved habits, depraved doctrine: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1013.

OS, depraved thought, a grave sin, ibid.

OTIOSI are to be called sinners: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 134.

OVES morally signify foolishness: Venerable Guibert, abbot, CLVI, 115.---A wandering sheep is a sinner straying from God: St. Fulgentius, LXV, 232.

PALLIUM denotes outward sins, depraved oldness, pride, exaltations: Rabanus Maurus, 1018.

PANIS, carnal pleasure, ibid., 1021.

PARIES, obstinacy, past sins, ibid., 1022.---The hardness of sin: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 401.---A wall signifies our sins: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 864.---A whitewashed wall is called hypocrisy: Peter Lombard, CXCI, 879.

PECCATUM, the punishment of sin, the tinder of sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1024.

PECTUS, the thought of lust, the heart: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 220.---Pride: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1023.

PELLIS, movements of the flesh: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 282.

PERA in Scripture signifies public property: Alcuin, C, 425.

PEREGRINUS, concupiscence: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1027.

PES, an evil example, ibid., 1025.

PETRA, the hardness of torpor: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 349.

PHIALAE denote the punishment of persecution: ibid., 459.

PILI, sins: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1028.---Superfluous thoughts of human corruption or of the old life: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 164.---Hairs signify worldly substance: Venerable Guibert, abbot, CLVI, 515.

PLAGA, sins: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1019.

PLANTA, the lowest action, ibid.

PLUMBUM, the weight of sin, ibid., 1034.---The sin of avarice: Garner, CXCIII, 318.

POPULUS. Carnal thoughts are designated by the people: Alan of Lille, CCX, 195.

PORTA, evil works, depraved habits: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1031.---Evil actions, depraved thoughts: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 492.

PRESSURA of the nations denotes the pressure of vices: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 56.

PRIMOGENITUM, pride: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1029.

PRUINA is temporal misery: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 995.

PULMO. In the lung pride is indicated: there is swelling, there is panting: St. Eucherius, L, 752.

PULVILLUS, flattery: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1034.

PULVIS, the vanity of the flesh: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

PUTREDO: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1033.---The darkness of earthly thought: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 250.

PURPURA, pride: Rabanus Maurus, 1034.

PUTEUM, mortality, the depth of vices, ibid., 1635.---Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 300.

QUADRANS, small sins: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1041.

QUERCUS is called the hardness of despair, barrenness of mind, ibid., 1036.

RAMUS is called pleasure of the flesh, ibid., 1037.

RANA signifies talkativeness: St. Bruno the Carthusian, CLII, 1048.

RAPINA, presumption: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1037.

REGINA, worldly pride, ibid., 1038.

REGULUS, concupiscence, ibid., 1039.

RENES, works of lust, generative acts, pleasure of the flesh, ibid.---Pleasure of the flesh: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 231.

REPTILIA, earthly thoughts: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1039; Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 130.

RETE, sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1039.

REX, sin, ibid., 1037.

RHAMNUS, the delight of sin, ibid.

RUBIGO, irascibility, malice, ibid., 1041.

RUGA, faithlessness, ibid.

SABBATUM is called torpor and negligence, ibid., 1042.

SACCULUS in Scripture signifies the hidden substance of riches: Alcuin, C, 425.

SAGITTAE signify mortality: St. Bruno the Carthusian, CLII, 792.

SALIUNCA, earthly thought: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1045.

SANGUIS, carnal understanding, sin, distress, vengeance for sin, cruelty, works of lust, ibid.---Carnal understanding, sin, the bloody malice of the mind: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 212.

SANIES, pleasure of the flesh: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1046.

SCABIES, lust, a stain upon the heart, ibid., 1043.

SCORPIO, despair, ibid., 1060.

SCUTUM denotes excuses: Richard of St. Victor, CXCVI, 663.

SEMEN, sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1048.---An evil thought is the seed of sin: Adam the Scot, CXCVIII, 449.

SEMITA, pride, the anguish of death: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1049.

SENTES, depraved pleasures, ibid.

[Col. 0219] SEPULCRUM, depraved speech, earthly works, ibid., 1050.

SERPENS, unbelief, detractions, sins, ibid., 1051.---A serpent is an evil thought: St. Paulinus of Aquileia, XCIX, 231.---Bodily pleasure assumed the type of the serpent; woman is the symbol of our sense-perception, Adam of the mind: St. Ambrose, XIV, 311.

SIMULACRA. The pomp of the world is compared to images: Gillebert, CLXXXIV, 286.

SINISTRA, a depraved work: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1055.

SITIS, covetousness, ibid., 1057.

SOL signifies the heat of temptations: Venerable Guibert, CLVI, 284.

SOLITUDO, separation from the Church: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 269.

SOMNUS, the torpor of negligence: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1059.

SPECTACULA are the devil’s church: Tertullian, I, 658.

SPINA, pride of heart, malice of heart: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1056.---Sin, the pricks of vices: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 339.---The thorn is a symbol of sin: Adam the Scot, CXCVIII, 759.---Thorns: harmful anxieties over riches, choking the mind, and the cares of this world: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

SPIRITUS is called the swelling of pride: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 155.

SQUAMAE, depraved excuses: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1046.

STANNUM, false doctrine, ibid.

STATURA, pride, ibid., 1047.

STERCUS, a worldly thing loved above God, the stench of lust, sins of the flesh, ibid., 1053.---The stench of lust, sin: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 278.

STERQUILINIUM, the stench of inward things: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1053.

STIPULA, human abjection: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 437.

STRUTHIO, hypocrisy, ibid., 79.

SULPHUR, the stench of vices, the burning stench of punishment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1061.

TALENTUM is called the weight of sin, ibid.

TELAE ARANEARUM, works of temporal concupiscence, which are made firm by no subtlety and which the deadly wind carries off: St. Eucherius, L, 754.---A lie is compared to spiders’ webs because of its weakness: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 128.

TEMPESTAS, the onset of persecutions or tribulations: St. Eucherius, L, 739.

TEMPLUM, the heavenly homeland: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1064.

TENEBRAE, the darkness of ignorance, iniquity: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 378.---Distresses are signified by darkness: Philip of Harveng, CCIII, 1175.

TERNARIUS NUMERUS designates the three kinds of sin: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 442.

TERRA, a depraved mind, a weak action: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1065.

TINEA, temptation of the flesh: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 133.

TORRENS, the assault of persecution: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

TRABS, hatred: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1063.

TRIBULUS, depraved pleasures, ibid., 1067.---Tribuli: the stings of vices or temptations: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

TUNICA, inward offenses: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1069.---Original sin is compared to a tunic: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 39.

TURRIS, the pride of this world: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1070.

TYRUS signifies pride: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 147.

UBERA are called unlawful blandishments, unlawful desires: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1084.

ULCUS, an evil habit, sins, ibid.

UMBILICUS, lust: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1085; Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 942; Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 228.

UMBRA, forgetfulness or sins, the pleasure of sins, forgetfulness of the mind: St. Eucherius, L, 741.---A shadow denotes weakness of both body and soul: Alan of Lille, CCX, 71.

UNCINUS POMORUM signifies avarice: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 355.

UNGUENTUM, pleasures of the flesh: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1085.

URTICA, the harshness of vices, depraved affections, ibid., 1086.---The burning of vices, the itching of earthly desires, [Col. 0220] the itchings of thoughts: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 424.

UTER, the thought of a carnal heart, ibid., 460.

UXOR, pleasure of the flesh: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1087.---Carnal thought: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 142.---A wife is a symbol of concupiscence: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 908.

VACCA is called sensuality: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1072.

VAGINA, depraved thought, ibid.

VAPOR, blindness of heart, ibid.

VAS, a depraved work, ibid., 1086.

VENENUM, malice, ibid., 1073.

VENTER, avarice, ibid., 1071.---Avarice, a work of lust: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 226.

VENTUS, iniquity of mind: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1071.---Winds: pride: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 51.

VEPRES, the pricks of vices: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1074.

VERMIS, lust: ibid., 1075.---Worms: restless thoughts, carnal cares: Garner, CXCII, 130.

VESPERE, the end of life or of the age, or punishment: St. Eucherius, L, 711.

VESPERTILIO, error of mind: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1077.---Bats: monstrosities of idols, or unclean thoughts: St. Eucherius, L, 748.

VESTIGIA, evil examples: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1076.

VINCULA, sins, ibid., 1079.

VINDEMIA, the consummation of the age, or vengeance upon the people: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

VINUM, the delight of sin, love of the world: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1078.---Worldly pleasures are signified by wine: Wolbero, abbot, CXCV, 1188.

VIPERA, an act of sin: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1079.---A sudden temptation: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 128.

VITIS ALIENA is called Adam: Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 831.

VITRUM, the deceptive blandishment of this age: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1082.

VITULUS, pride of heart, wanton movements of the heart, ibid.---The calves of Lebanon denote presumption: Richard of St. Victor, CXCVI, 295.

VOLUCRES driven away from Abraham’s sacrifice are a figure of evil and useless thoughts: Venerable Hildebert of Le Mans, CLXXI, 143, 430.

VOX, a movement of desire: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1083.

VULNUS, sin, ibid., 1084.

VULPES, temptations: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 1083.---Foxes are called those vices which deceive us under the appearance of virtue, ibid., 1084.

ZELUS is called envy: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1088.

ZIZANIA, scandals: St. Eucherius, L, 742.

## ARTICLE XII. Allegories concerning our last things

ABYSSUS is called hell, the pains of death: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 852.---Hell: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 284.

ACCUBITUS, the heavenly homeland: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 854.

ACERVUS LAPIDUM, the rebuke of the last judgment, ibid.

ADAMANS is called eternity: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 356.

AEGYPTUS, hell: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 915.

AES, damnation, ibid., 917.

AESTAS, the day of judgment, ibid., 917; Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 388.

AQUA, the punishments of hell: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 860.---The torments of hell: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 279.

ARCUS, the threat of judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 862.---The day of the last judgment, the heavenly judgment: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 324.

BABYLON is called hell: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 872.---Babylon is a type of hell: Philip of Harveng, CCIII, 1140.

BATUS, judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 874.

BELLUM, final damnation, ibid.

CADAVER denotes the punishment of the damned, ibid., 878.

CALCULUS, the eternity of the heavenly homeland, ibid., 880.

CALIGO, the last day, the examination of final judgment, ibid., 879.

CALOR, the punishment of the reprobate, ibid., 880.

CAMINUS, infernal life, ibid., 882.

CARCER, hell, ibid., 886.

CARO, the punishments of the reprobate, ibid.

CATULUS, reprobate people, ibid., 889.

[Col. 0221] CEDRUS. In Sacred Scripture, by the name *cedar* is sometimes meant the lofty excellence of heavenly glory, sometimes the height of heavenly glory: St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 649.

CELLARIUM is called heaven: Alan of Lille, CCX, 56.

CENTENARIUS NUMERUS, which in counting on the fingers is transferred from the left to the right hand, sometimes represents heavenly life in Scripture: Rabanus Maurus, CIX, 470.

CETUS, death: idem, CXII, 893.

CISTERNA, hell, ibid., 896.

CIVITAS, the heavenly homeland, hell, ibid., 897.---A fortified city: heaven: St. Bruno of Würzburg, CXLII, 231.---Hell, ibid., 400.

CLIBANUS, the examination of judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 894.

COELUM, heavenly blessedness, ibid., 891.---Heavenly life: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 30.

COENA, the refreshment of eternal life, ibid., 892.

CRYSTALLUS signifies the brightness and firmness of the eternal homeland: Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 1435.

DESERTUM, heaven: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 268.---By the desert hell is rightly understood, where none of the elect is found and where none of the consolations of affliction is felt: St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 355.

DIADEMA is called judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 909.

DIES, the heavenly homeland, ibid.---Eternity: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 370.

DILUVIUM, the final judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 911.

DOMUS, death, ibid.---The dwelling-place of heaven: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 395.---A house sometimes signifies hell: Rupert, abbot, CLXVIII, 740.

DORMITIO, death: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 913.

EDOM, hell, ibid., 914.

ESCA, the refreshment of the heavenly homeland, ibid., 917.

FALX is called death, ibid., 921.

FINIS, eternal life, eternal destruction, eternity, ibid., 932.

FLUVIUS, the final examination, ibid., 934.---The fire of the final judgment: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 291.

FONS, eternal blessedness: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 932.

FOVEA, hell, ibid.---The abyss of hell: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 274.

FRAMEA, death: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 922.

FRIGUS, the severity of final judgment, ibid., 937.

FRUCTUS, eternal blessedness, eternal rewards, eternal death, ibid., 938.

FULGUR, the sentences of final judgment, ibid., 933.---The dreadful sentences of final judgment: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 60.

FUMUS, the darkness of damnation: Rabanus Maurus, CXIII, 935.

GAZOPHYLACIUM, the heavenly homeland, ibid., 943.

GLADIUS, death, final judgment, eternal damnation, ibid., 940.---The sentence of the future judgment, the punishment of eternal damnation: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 322.

GOMORRHA. In Sodom and Gomorrah is signified the day of final judgment: St. Prosper of Aquitaine, LI, 745.

HERBA is called eternal joy: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 950.

HIEMS, the last judgment, ibid., 953.

HODIE, eternity, ibid., 954.

IGNIS, eternal punishment, ibid., 966.---The burning of Gehenna: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 355.

JACINTHUS denotes eternal rewards, ibid., 965.

JERUSALEM, the dwelling of the heavenly homeland, ibid., 966; CXI, 337, 379.

JUDAEA signifies the heavenly homeland, ibid., 339.

JUDICIUM, damnation: idem, CXII, 973.

JUGUM, the burdensome habitation of hell, ibid., 972.

LACUS, hell, ibid., 978; Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 302.---The lake of hell, a place of punishment: St. Hilary, IX, 840.

LAMPAS, the examination of judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 981.

LECTULUS, eternal blessedness, ibid., 983.

LILIUM, heavenly blessedness, ibid., 986.---By lilies is designated the loveliness of paradise, fragrant with the flowers of the brightness of the heavenly homeland and of immortality: idem, CIX, 457.

LOCUS, the heavenly homeland: idem, CXII, 987.

LONGITUDO, eternity, ibid., 989.

MARE, hell, the punishment of Gehenna, ibid., 995.

MATER is called the heavenly Jerusalem: St. Eucherius, L, 755.

MATUTINUM is called the day of judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 793.

MENSA, the heavenly homeland, ibid., 998.

MONS. Heaven is compared to a mountain: St. Bernard, CLXXXIII, 626.

MORS, eternal punishment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1002.

NIX is called eternal damnation, ibid., 1006.

NOX, the bitterness of death: St. Eucherius, L, 741.

[Col. 0222] NUPTIAE, the joys of the heavenly homeland: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1008.

OCTONARIUS NUMERUS designates the day of eternal judgment: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 450.

ORTUS, the heavenly homeland: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1013.

PISCIS, death, ibid., 1030.

PLAGA, eternal damnation, ibid., 1019.

PORTA, the last judgment, ibid., 1031.---The day of judgment: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 402.

PROFUNDUM, hell, ibid., 303.

PUTEUS. The wells of hell are called by the name of destruction: St. Hilary, IX, 836.

REGNUM, the heavenly homeland: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1038.

SANGUIS, the punishments of hell, ibid., 1045.

TEMPLUM, the heavenly homeland, ibid., 1064.

TENEBRAE, the punishments of hell: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 378.

TERRA, the kingdom of heaven, hell: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1065.---Hell: Garner of St. Victor, 239.

THRONI, the tribunal of the future judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1069.

TINEA, the torment of hell, ibid., 1067.

TORRENS, death’s flowing-away: St. Eucherius, L, 742.---The last judgment: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1068.---The fire of final judgment: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 297.

UMBRA, the death of the flesh: St. Eucherius, L, 741.---The darkness of hell: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1085.

VALLIS, the lowest places of punishment: Garner of St. Victor, CXCIII, 258.

VELUM, heaven: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1075.

VENTILABRUM, the separation effected by judgment, ibid., 1071.

VERMIS, the garments of hell, ibid., 1075.---By the name *worm* may be understood the memory in the soul of a sinner placed in the punishment of hell: idem, CXI, 236.

VESTIBULUM, eternal life: idem, CXII, 1076.

VIA, the condition of the reprobate, ibid., 1077.

VIRENTIA, eternal goods, ibid., 1081.

VIRGA, the sentence of the judge, ibid.

## ARTICLE XIII. Allegories concerning Sacred Scripture

ABYSSUS is called the depth of the Scriptures; likewise, the depth of the Old and New Testaments: St. Eucherius, L, 739; Alcuin, C, 423.---The Old and New Testaments are called an abyss: Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 852.---The two abysses are the two Testaments: St. Bruno of Würzburg, CXLII, 178.

ACERVUS. The sacred books are a heap of wheat: St. Bernard, CLXXXV, 182.
