**Boniface (St.)**, bishop of Mainz and apostle of the Germans, sets out to convert the Frisians (A.D. 716), St. Boniface, LXXXIX, 609, 611; preaches in Frisia, Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 465; Marianus Scotus, 761; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 135, 158; in Germany, St. Boniface, LXXXIX, 641; Anastasius, CXXXII, 975; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1341; Helinand, CCXII, 812; converts the Saxons and Hessians to the faith, St. Boniface, LXXXIX, 617–642; the Bavarians, ibid., 622, 648; again preaches among the Frisians and Danes, ibid., 624, 641; St. Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 123; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 158.

**Bosel and Ottcar**, the first bishops of Worcester, proclaim the faith at Worcester in the province of the Mercian English (A.D. 730), William, CLXXIX, 1587.

**Bruno**, bishop, preaches among the Slavs and brings many to the faith (A.D. 980), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 503, 504.

[Col. 0532] **Burchard**, bishop of Würzburg, evangelizes Germany with St. Boniface of Mainz (A.D. 730–751), St. Boniface, LXXXIX, 646; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1312.

## C

**Caesara**, queen of the Persians, baptized at Antioch, converts her husband Anaulf and a great multitude of the Persian people to Christ (A.D. 588), Fredegarius Scholasticus, LXXI, 613; Heriger, CXXXIX, 885; Ekkehard, CLIV, 837.

**Calocerus**, disciple of St. James the apostle, proclaims Christ in Carpetania in Spain (A.D. 44), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 155.

**Candidus** sets out with St. Augustine to convert the English, and preaches the faith with him throughout England (A.D. 596), St. Gregory the Great, LXXVII, 835–841.

**Capito**, bishop of Lugo and disciple of St. James, publishes the faith in Spain (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, 129, 130.

**Charlemagne**, king of the Franks and emperor of Germany, imposes baptism upon the Saxons (A.D. 777), Einhard, XCVII, 33; Ekkehard, CLIV, 857, 893; Honorius of Autun, CLXXII, 190.

**Charles the Simple**, king of the Franks and emperor of Germany, imposes the faith upon the Northmen as a condition of peace (A.D. 912), Dudo, dean of St. Quentin, CXLI, 651.

**Carpus**, disciple of St. Paul, proclaims Christ through the Troad (A.D. 60–100), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129.

**Cedd**, a Scottish priest and subsequently bishop of Lichfield, preaches the faith in the province of the Mercians and among the Middle Angles (A.D. 653), Bede, XCV, 150; restores the faith, which had been cast off, to the Anglo-Saxons (A.D. 654), ibid., 151; William, CLXXIX, 1603.

**Ceddus**, bishop of London and successor of St. Mellitus, proclaims Christ in England (A.D. 610), William, CLXXIX, 1514; among the East Saxons, Bede, XCV, 151; at Tilbury and Ythancaestir, ibid., 152, 154.

**Cella**, a Scot by nation and bishop of Lindisfarne, evangelizes the Mercian English (A.D. 650), William, CLXXIX, 1603.

**Celsus**, bishop of Milan, publishes the faith at Milan (A.D. 72–100), Regino, abbot of Prüm, CXXXII, 18.

**Christians**, dispersed in the persecution against St. Stephen as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, proclaim the word of the Gospel in the synagogue of the Jews (A.D. 34), Anastasius, CXXVII, 454; carry the faith as far as Europe (A.D. 34), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 95, 97.

**Christianus** preaches Christ at Aarhus in Denmark (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 616.

**Clement (St.)**, is sent by St. Peter into Gaul to preach (A.D. 50), Anonymous, CLIV, 1117; elected pope, succeeds St. Peter and, consecrated at Rome, preaches the faith (A.D. 69), Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 649; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 25–26; Ekkehard, CLIV, 670; while exiled in Lycia, converts many peoples, Freculf, CVI, 1156.

**Clement (St.)**, bishop of Metz, preaches in Gaul (A.D. 50), Anonymous, CLXIII, 579.

**Cletus (St.)**, disciple of St. Peter, ordained by Peter at Rome, publishes the faith of Christ (A.D. 45–69), Ekkehard, CLIV, 670.

**Clotildis**, queen of the Franks, works with Vedastus and St. Remigius for the conversion of Clovis and the Frankish people (A.D. 496), St. Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 152; Anonymous, XCVI, 1433; Hincmar, CXXV, 1157; Rorico the Monk, CXXXIX, 598.

**Caecilius**, bishop of Elvira and disciple of St. James the apostle, preaches throughout Spain (A.D. 43–54), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 151–173.

**Coelestis (St.)**, disciple of St. Clement and second bishop of Metz, preaches the faith in Gaul (A.D. 70), Anonymous, CLXIII, 581.

**Colmannus**, bishop of Lindisfarne, proclaims the faith to the West Saxons on the island of Lindisfarne (Holy Island) (A.D. 650), William, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry, CXCV, 865.

**Columba (St.)**, an Irishman and teacher of the Scots and Picts, preaches the Word of Christ in Britain (A.D. 565), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1329; in Scotland, Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 112; preaches and dies on the island of Hii near Ireland (A.D. 596), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1332.

**Columbanus (St.)**, abbot, proclaims Christ to the people of the Picts in southern England and converts King Bridius.

[Col. 0533] (A.D. 600), Bede, XCV, 121; at Centula in Gaul (A.D. 620), Harnulf, abbot, CLXXIV, 1220.

**Constantine the Great**, emperor, embraces the faith and sees to it that it is preached throughout the world (A.D. 312), Aurelius Cassiodorus, LXIX, 888; Freculf, CVI, 955; Anastasius, CXXVII, 1510; Hugh, CLIV, 96; Sigebert, CLX, 1190; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 204.

**Crispinius**, bishop of Écija, preaches in Baetica (A.D. 66), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 198.

**Crispinus and Crispinianus**, Roman priests, proclaim the faith in Gaul (A.D. 250), Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1494.

**Men of Cyprus and Cyrene**, dispersed after the martyrdom of Stephen the deacon, proclaim the Gospel to Greeks (A.D. 35), Anastasius, CXXVII, 456.

## D

**Dąbrówka, or Dubrowka**, married to Mieszko, the first king of the Poles, proclaims the Gospel to the Poles and brings the king and nation to the faith (A.D. 966), St. Matilda the Queen, CLI, 1334; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 848–849.

**Derso**, deacon and companion of St. Boniface of Mainz, evangelizes Germany with him (A.D. 730), St. Boniface, LXXXIX, 860.

**Deruvianus and Phaganus**, sent by Pope Eleutherius, preach in England and baptize King Lucius (A.D. 166), William, CLXXIX, 1688.

**Dethmar**, a Saxon by nation and bishop of Prague, proclaims Christ to the Bohemians (A.D. 973), Cosmas, dean of Prague, CLXVI, 90.

**Deusdedit**, with St. Augustine, spreads the faith in England (A.D. 598–603), William, CLXXIX, 1443.

**Diego**, bishop of Osma, defends the faith against the Albigensian heresy (A.D. 1206), Peter of Vaux-de-Cernay, monk, CCXIII, 549.

**Dionysius (St.) the Areopagite**, is converted to Christ by St. Paul at Athens (A.D. 50), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116–124; Peter Comestor, CXCIV, 1701; himself preaches at Athens, Ekkehard, CLIV, 679; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129; at Corinth, Freculf, CVI, 1166; Haymo, CXVIII, 830; in Gaul and at Paris, St. Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175–183; Othlo the Monk, CXLVI, 387; Folcard the Monk, CXLVII, 1182; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 26; Ekkehard, ibid., 679.

**The disciples of Christ** baptize (A.D. 30), Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1561; are sent out to evangelize, ibid., 1565; scattered through the cities of Judaea, sow the words of life and perform many miracles, Ekkehard, CLIV, 663; dispersed throughout all Judaea, Samaria, Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, proclaim the faith (A.D. 34), Haymo, CXVIII, 825; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 109.

**Seven disciples of St. James the apostle and first bishop of Jerusalem**, after his martyrdom, carry his body in a ship to Spain and, first in Galicia among the Iberians and then throughout all Spain, preach (A.D. 44), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 113.

**A certain disciple of St. Saturninus** preaches the faith at Bourges in Gaul (A.D. 80), St. Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 176.

**Diuma**, a Scottish priest and later bishop of Lindisfarne, proclaims Christ among the Mercians in Middle England (A.D. 653), Bede, XCV, 130; William, CLXXIX, 1603.

**Dominic (St.)** defends the true faith against the Albigensian heresy (A.D. 1208), Peter of Vaux-de-Cernay, monk, CCXIII, 555.

**Dominic**, bishop of Trier, sent into Bulgaria by Pope St. Nicholas, converts many to the faith (A.D. 858), Anastasius, CXXXIII, 1371.

**Donatus**, bishop of Ostia, sent by Pope St. Nicholas, evangelizes Bulgaria (A.D. 858), Anastasius, CXXVIII, 1374.

**The twelve apostles**, on Pentecost receive the Holy Spirit and preach the faith to all peoples assembled together (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 64–65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII.

## E
EARCOMBERT, king of the English, destroys the idols of the gods and spreads the faith of Christ far and wide throughout his kingdom (A.D. 640), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 121. EBO, bishop of Rheims, preaches among the Danes and Swedes (A.D. 830–856), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 971; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 475. EDBERT, bishop of Leicester, preaches the faith among the Middle Angles (A.D. 630), William, CLXXIX, 1605. [Col. 0534] EDDESIUS and FRUMENTIUS, boys and captives of the Tyrian philosopher Meropius, preach the faith in Nearer India, where no ploughshare of apostolic preaching had yet made an impression (A.D. 328), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 478.—Eddesius, having become a bishop, evangelizes the Iberians and Armenians, Freculf, CVI, 1198. EDILFRID, bishop of Crediton, preaches in West Saxony (A.D. 850), William, CLXXIX, 1547. EGINON, bishop of Dalby, first preaches in the province of Scania, at Dalby, Lund, and Skara (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, 617.—He preaches in the Orkney Islands, ibid., 617.—Then he evangelizes the Pleicanos, a people of Scania, on the island of Hulmo, and again at Skara, ibid. EGWARD, or Evagrius, first bishop of Oldenburg, preaches in Wagria (A.D. 980), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 508. EILBERT, first a monk and then a bishop, [preaches] in the Danish islands of Farria and Fiune (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI. ELOQUIUS, a Scot, and St ETTO preach in Gaul (A.D. 651), CLX, 123. ELPIDIUS, first bishop of Toledo, extends Christ’s kingdom in Spain (A.D. 37), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129. EMMING, a count and disciple of St Willehad, is granted martyrdom while preaching at Leri among the Saxons (A.D. 780), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 1017. EOBAN, bishop of Ahr [in] Frisia, fellow-worker of St Boniface of Mainz, obtains the crown of martyrdom with him (A.D. 755), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 660, 667, 805. EPAPHRAS, disciple of St Paul, teaches the Colossians the faith (A.D. 60–100), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129. EPELPINE, or Edelwine, bishop of Dorchester, proclaims Christ among the Middle Angles and in West Saxony (A.D. 651), William, CLXXIX, 1608. EPHREM, disciple of St James, evangelizes the Asturians in Spain (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129–130. ERASTUS, disciple of St Paul, preaches the word of life at Philippi in Macedonia (A.D. 60–100), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129. ERIMBERT, disciple of St Boniface, bishop of Freising, proclaims Christ in Bavaria (A.D. 730), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 649. ERIMBERT, priest and disciple of St Ansgar, preaches among the Swedes (A.D. 850), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 997–998; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 481. ETHELRED, king of Kent, receives St Augustine and his companions and grants them power and permission to preach the Gospel throughout the kingdom (A.D. 596), Henry, CXCV, 842.—He arranges for the building of the church of Saints Peter and Paul east of the city of Canterbury, Henry, CXCV, 848. ETHERIUS, bishop of Barcelona, preaches the faith in Spain (A.D. 37), Lucius Dexter, 129, 130. Etto the Scot sows the word of life in Gaul (A.D. 651), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 123. EUCHARIUS is sent by St Peter the Apostle to preach in Gaul (A.D. 50), Heriger, CXXXIX, 1010; Anonymous, CLIV, 1117.—Made bishop among the Treveri, he preaches the Gospel also among the Tungri, Heriger, CXXXIX, 1010; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1118. EUGENIUS (Marcus Marcellus) proclaims Christ at Valencia in Spain (A.D. 37), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129.—At Toledo (A.D. 60), ibid., 273. EUPHRASIUS, ordained bishop at Rome by St Peter the Apostle, is sent to preach in southern Spain, that is, coastal Baetica (A.D. 43), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 151. EUTROPIUS proclaims Christ among the Santones and at Bordeaux (A.D. 48), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493. EVODIUS, disciple of St Peter and first bishop of Antioch after Peter (A.D. 45–60), St Prosper of Aquitaine, LI, 553; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 644; Ekkehard, CLIV, 667. EWALD THE WHITE, a priest and one of Willibrord’s twelve companions, is crowned with martyrdom while preaching with him in Frisia (A.D. 694), Bede, XCV, 243. EWALD THE BLACK, brother of Ewald the White, dies bravely while preaching with him (A.D. 694), Bede, XCV, 243 (note). EZZO, bishop of Oldenburg, proclaims Christ in Slavonia and Sweden (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 574, 617.

## F

FELIX, bishop of Metz, preaches in Gaul (A.D. 80), Anonymous, CLIV, 1119. FELIX, bishop of Lincoln, a Burgundian by birth, sows the word of faith among the East Angles (A.D. 634–640), Henry, CXCV, 857–858. [Col. 0535] FERONTIUS evangelizes Besançon in Gaul (A.D. 48), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493. FINAN, bishop on the island of Lindisfarne (Holy Island), teaches the faith to the Middle Angles and converts King Penda together with his people (A.D. 653), Bede, XCV, 150; William, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry, CXCV, 863.—He converts the East Saxons in England, ibid., 864. FINGARIS, herald of Christ in Ireland (A.D. 431), St Anselm, spurious writings, CLIX, 325. FLEGUNTA, disciple of St Titus, proclaims the Gospel on the island of Crete (A.D. 68), Freculf, CVI, 1149. FOILAN, disciple of St Livinus, preaches with him through Scotland, England, and Ireland (A.D. 648), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 879.—With Saints Fursa and Ultan he sows Christ’s word in Gaul, Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 122. FOLCARD, priest and companion of St Willehad, receives the crown of martyrdom while preaching at Leri in Saxony (A.D. 780), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 1018. FOLEWARD, archbishop in Slavonia, proclaims Christ in Sweden and Norway (A.D. 992), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 533. FOLRAD, archchaplain or abbot, preached in Germany together with others (A.D. 751), Ekkehard, CLIV, 837. FRANCO, bishop of Rouen, preaches in Normandy and baptizes Rollo, leader of the Normans (A.D. 912), Dudo, dean of St Quentin, CXLI, 651; William of Jumièges, monk, CXLIX, 80; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 232. FRONTINUS, bishop of Périgueux, preaches in Gaul (A.D. 50), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1505. FRUMENTIUS carries the word of faith with Eddesius into Nearer India (A.D. 328), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 478.—Having been made a priest, he is sent into India to preach, same author, ibid., 480; Freculf, CVI, 1198. FURSEUS (St), an Irish bishop, preaches the Gospel in Aquitaine (A.D. 648), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 122; Freculf, abbot, CLXXIV, 1441; Helinand, CCXII, 776.—He evangelizes the East Angles, Bede, XCV, 145. FUSCIANUS and VICTORICUS, sent from Rome into Gaul with their other companions, proclaim Christ (A.D. 250), St Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1194; Folcard, monk, CXLVII, 1182.

## G

GALLUS, first apostle of the Alemanni (A.D. 648), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 465. GAUDBERT, bishop of the Swedes, preaches in Sweden (A.D. 840), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 476, 478. GAUDENTIUS (St), apostle first in Gerdania (Danzig), then in Prussia (A.D. 990), St Matilda the Queen, CLI, 1341. GAUZBERT evangelizes the Danes and Swedes (A.D. 830), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 971. GEPPAN, fellow-worker and companion of St Boniface, preaches the faith in Germany (A.D. 738), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 741. GERBRAND, bishop of Roskilde, proclaims Christ in Zealand (A.D. 1050), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 624. GERMANUS (St), bishop of Auxerre, defends the faith in England against the Pelagians (A.D. 429), Hincmar, CXXIV, 1164; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 82, 83; William, CLXXIX, 1688; Henry, CXCV, 826, 827. GERMANUS (St), bishop of Paris, preaches among the Franks in Gaul (A.D. 554–570), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1331. GERWALD (St), companion of St Willehad, receives the crown of martyrdom from the Saxons while preaching at Bremen (A.D. 780), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 1017. GISLA, queen of the Hungarians, brings her husband the king and her father the emperor to the faith, together with an innumerable multitude of peoples (A.D. 1010), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 200; Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 531. GISLEMAR proclaims Christ in Denmark and brings the king of Sweden to the faith (A.D. 840), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 971; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 475. GISLENUS, abbot of Celles, preaches in Gaul (A.D. 651), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 123. GOTEBALD, an Englishman, proclaims Christ in Sweden, Norway, and Scania (A.D. 981), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 529. GOWIBALD, bishop of Regensburg, spreads the Gospel in Bavaria (A.D. 738), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 649. GRATIANUS, bishop, preaches among the people of Tours in Gaul (A.D. 58), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175, 183. GREGORY (St) THE GREAT, pope, converts the Lombards through Theudelinda (A.D. 595), Mozarabic Liturgy, LXXXV, 581.—[He converts] the English through St Augustine and his companions (A.D. 596), St Gregory the Great, LXXVII, 835, 841; Bede, XCV, 52; Anastasius, CXXVIII, 645, 1370; Heriger, CXXXIX, 883; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1332; Sigebert, CLX, 112; Heuric, CXCV, 841. [Col. 0536] GREGORY, bishop of Utrecht, proclaims Christ in Germany (A.D. 736), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 646, 653. GRIMKIL, with Rudolf and Bernard, preaches the faith in Sweden, Gothland, and the islands of Norway (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLV, 541, 650. GRIMOALD, bishop of Polymartium, is sent by Pope Nicholas I to preach in Bulgaria and converts many to Christ (A.D. 858), Anastasius, CXXVIII, 1375.

## H

HADOLF, a monk and disciple of St Boniface of Mainz, preaches with him in Frisia and receives the crown of martyrdom (A.D. 755), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 660. HALITGARIUS, bishop of Cambrai, proclaims the Gospel to the Danes with Ebbo (A.D. 830), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 474. HAMUM, a priest and companion of St Boniface of Mainz, is granted the crown of martyrdom while preaching with him in Frisia (A.D. 755), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 660. HARALD, bishop of Schleswig, spreads the faith in Jutland and Denmark (A.D. 840–860), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 475, 621. HARED, or HORIT, bishop of Schleswig, preaches in Jutland (A.D. 948), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 503. HARTAGARIUS, a hermit, scatters the words of the Gospel in Sweden (A.D. 845), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 480. HEDHED, bishop of Dorchester, expounds the word of life to the Middle Angles (A.D. 650), William, CLXXIX, 1605. HELIAS, disciple of St Livinus, preaches through Scotland, England, and Ireland (A.D. 648), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 879. HEMMERAMNUS, first apostle of Bavaria (seventh or eighth century), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 465. HENRY I, king and emperor of the Alemanni, recalls the Northmen and Danes, together with their king Cnut, from their former error and brings them to the Catholic faith (A.D. 931), Thietmar of Merseburg, CXXXIX, 1193.—Likewise [he converts] the kings of the Obotrites and Danes (A.D. 971), Cosmas of Prague, CLXVI, 84. HENRY II (St), king and emperor of the Alemanni, converts the Rus’, Poles, and Hungarians to the faith (A.D. 1002), Honorius of Autun, CLXXII, 193. HERIBERT, bishop of Wiberg, scatters the words of the Gospel in Denmark and Saxony (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 616. HERIDAG, bishop of Hamburg, first proclaims Christ in Nordalbingia (A.D. 804), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 472. HERIGARIUS, prefect of Birka, converts the people of Birka to the faith (A.D. 840), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 980; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 478–479. HERIALD, king of the Danes, converted to the faith, brings with him to Christ a great multitude of his people (A.D. 826), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1347; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 158. HERMAGORAS, bishop, evangelized Aquileia (A.D. 50), St Ado, bishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 78. HERMANN, disciple of St Titus, preaches on the island of Crete (A.D. 68), Freculf, CVI, 1149. HEWALD, see EWALD. HIDDILA, a priest, evangelizes the island of Vectis (Wight) with St Wilfrid, bishop (A.D. 686), Bede, XCV, 196, 197. HIDIBALD, bishop of Cologne, proclaims Christ in Frisia (A.D. 780), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 471. HONORIUS, bishop of Canterbury, preaches among the East Angles in Kent with St Paulinus (A.D. 634), Bede, XCV, 108; Henry, CXCV, 857, 858. HUBERT (St), patron of the Ardennes, preaches the faith (A.D. 700–727), Anonymous, CLIV, 1344.

## I

IGNATIUS (St), bishop of the Church of Antioch, proclaims Christ in Asia Minor (A.D. 100), Freculf, CVI, 1158.—At Rome he is handed over to beasts for the faith (A.D. 101), St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 81. INDALECIUS (St), ordained at Rome by St Peter, is sent to preach in Spain (A.D. 45), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 151.—He preaches the faith to the Iberians, at Carthago Spartaria and Eliocroca (A.D. 45), ibid., 169. IRENAEUS (St), bishop of Lyons, proclaims Christ at Lyons in Gaul (A.D. 48), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493; John the monk, CLXII, 755. ISCIUS is sent by St Peter to preach in Spain (A.D. 43), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 167.—He preaches at Carteia near the strait (A.D. 52), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 167. [Col. 0537] ISLEF, bishop of Skálholt, preaches the faith on the island of Iceland and in Greenland (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 654.

## J

JAMES (St) THE APOSTLE, son of Alphaeus and brother of the Lord, receives the Holy Spirit with the other eleven on the day of Pentecost and preaches the Gospel (A.D. 33), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 64–65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1631.—He is ordained bishop of Jerusalem (A.D. 33–40), Freculf, CVI, 1122; Haymo, CXVIII, 823; St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 76; Regino, CXXXII, 16; Hermann the Lame, CXLIII, 57; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 638; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1304; Ekkehard, CLIV, 663; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 154. JAMES (St) THE APOSTLE, son of Zebedee, brother of St John the Apostle and Evangelist, called the Greater, receives the Holy Spirit with the other eleven Apostles on the day of Pentecost and preaches the Gospel (A.D. 33), Orderic, 64–65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1631.—Spain falls to his lot for preaching (A.D. 34), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87–88.—He travels through Spain preaching (A.D. 37), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 109; Freculf, CVI, 1147; Munio the monk, CLXX, 875.—He preaches through Judaea and Samaria, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 113; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1680.—He preaches the Gospel through Gaul, the Britains, and the towns of the Veneti (A.D. 41), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 135.—He proclaims Christ at Ephesus (A.D. 41), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 135.—[He preaches] in Asia Minor with his brother John, Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 148; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1698. JAMES (St) THE DEACON, disciple of St Paulinus, scatters the words of the Gospel at York in England (A.D. 640), Henry, CXCV, 859. JABUMANN, bishop, restores the lost faith to the East Angles and Saxons (A.D. 665), Bede, XCV, 170. JARUMNAS, bishop of London, proclaims Christ in England (A.D. 653), Henry, CXCV, 865. JESUS CHRIST, baptized in the Jordan by Blessed John the Baptist, opens the era of Gospel preaching in the thirtieth year of his age, Anastasius, CXXVII, 452.—In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, he begins the preaching of saving evangelical teaching, Anastasius, CXXIX, 525; Hermann the Lame, CXLIII, 57; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1304; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 101; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1562.—He calls the Apostles (A.D. 30), Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 16; Ekkehard, CLIV, 661.—He sends them to evangelize through the towns of Judaea, Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1565.—He himself openly disseminates his Gospel through Judaea (A.D. 30–33), Haymo, CXVIII, 822–823; St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 76; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 16; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 637; Ekkehard, CLIV, 661; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1562.—He dies on the cross for the salvation of the world (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 101; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1632. JOHN THE BAPTIST (St) prepares the way of the Lord and of the Gospel by preaching repentance and baptizing (A.D. 30), Freculf, CVI, 1121; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 16; Ekkehard, CLIV, 661; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1552; Sicard, CCXIII, 449.—He baptizes Christ the Lord in the Jordan, Anastasius, CXXVII, 452; Hermann the Lame, CXLIII, 57; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1304; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 101; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1562. JOHN THE APOSTLE AND EVANGELIST, son of Zebedee, receives the Holy Spirit with the other eleven on the day of Pentecost and begins to preach the Gospel (A.D. 33), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 64, 65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1631.—At the gate of the Temple in Jerusalem, he preaches with St Peter, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 103; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1655.—He preaches in Jerusalem with Peter and travels through many Samaritan regions evangelizing, Anastasius, CXXVII, 454.—He preaches in Asia, Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87–88; Freculf, CVI, 1154; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 148; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1698.—He preaches at Ephesus and neighbouring places, St Ambrose, XVII, 867.—He is banished in exile to the island of Patmos, St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 81; Anastasius, CXXVII, 486.—He writes his Gospel at Ephesus (A.D. 99), Ekkehard, CLIV, 679.—He preaches in Cyprus, Orderic, CLXXXVII, 116.—He writes the Apocalypse, or Revelation, Haymo, CXVIII, 834; Anastasius, CXXVII, 486. JOHN, bishop of Constantinople, converts the Celtic Arians and the Scythians to the true faith (A.D. 400), Aurelius Cassiodorus, LXIX, 1167. JOHN is sent by Blessed Pope Gregory to preach in England with St Augustine, apostle of the English, Mellitus [Col. 0538], and others (A.D. 596), Anastasius, CXXVIII, 645, 1370; Heriger, CXXXIX, 883; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1332. JOHN, bishop of Salzburg in Bavaria and disciple of St Boniface of Mainz, proclaims Christ (A.D. 730), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 649, 741. JOHN THE SCOT, or BRITON, bishop of Magnopolis, proclaims the Gospel in Sweden and Iceland (A.D. 1023), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 527, 540, 617, 650. JOHN, bishop of Borca, commonly called Hiltuin, evangelized the Baltic islands of Öland, Gotland, and Ösel (A.D. 1069), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 636. JONAH (St), disciple of Dionysius the Areopagite, proclaims the Gospel in Lusitania, especially at Caecilius’s Castle (A.D. 86), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 253.—He passes through Gaul preaching, ibid., 254. JORDAN, bishop of Poznań, proclaims Christ to the Poles (A.D. 966), St Matilda the Queen, CLI, 1336. JOSEPH OF ARIMATHEA, with eleven companions, is sent from Gaul by St Philip to preach in England and scatters the words of the Gospel on the island of Glastonbury (A.D. 63), William, CLXXIX, 1683.—With Mary Magdalene, Lazarus, and others, he lands at Marseilles and evangelizes Provence (A.D. 48), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 156; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493. JUDAS THE APOSTLE, called brother of James and brother of the Lord, proclaims the Gospel after Pentecost (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 64, 65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1631.—He spreads the seed of the Gospel in Mesopotamia and the inland regions of Pontus (A.D. 33–70), Freculf, CVI, 1132, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 115, 116.—He writes an epistle at Neritus in Armenia and dies, Freculf, CVI, 1135, 1147. JUSTUS, bishop of Canterbury and companion of St Augustine, preaches in England with Mellitus, Ruffinianus, and others (A.D. 604), Bede, XCV, 85; Lanfranc, CL, 743, 764; William, CLXXIX, 1443; Henry, CXCV, 844, 853.

## K

KILIAN, first apostle in Franconia, refreshes the peoples with the light of the Gospel (date uncertain: seventh or eighth century), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 465. KUNDEKAR, a monk and companion of St Boniface of Mainz, preaches with him in Frisia and receives the crown of martyrdom (A.D. 755), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 660.

## L

LAMBERT (St), bishop of Utrecht and disciple of St Landoald, [preaches] in Gascony (A.D. 677), Anonymous, CXXXIX, 1113, 1114.—He converts Toxandria (Tessenderlo) to the faith, Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 769, 793. LANDELIN (St), abbot of Lobbes, preaches in Gaul with St Gislenus (A.D. 651), Sigebert, CLX, 123. LANDGALD, archpriest, proclaims Christ in Gaul with St Amandus (A.D. 638), Sigebert, CLX, 120.—[He preaches] in Gascony (A.D. 650), Heriger, CXXXIX, 1113. LAURENCE (St), bishop of Canterbury in Kent and successor of St Augustine, preaches the faith in England (A.D. 645), Henry, XCV, 851, 852.—[He preaches] in Scotland (A.D. 609), Bede, XCV, 86; Goscelin of Canterbury, CLV, 115, 119. LAZARUS, raised by the Lord, is ordained bishop of Cyprus (A.D. 34), Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 638, 646.—With St Mary Magdalene, Martha, and the others, he lands at the port of Marseilles and spreads the Gospel in Provence (A.D. 48), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 156–158; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493. LEANDER, bishop of Seville, preaches in Spain and brings Reccared, an Arian king, to the right way of faith (A.D. 587), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1332. LEBUIN, a priest and one of Willibrord’s twelve companions, evangelizes Frisia (A.D. 692), Bede, XCV, 243. LENDRIC, bishop of Bremen, proclaims Christ at Bremen (A.D. 845), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 480. LEO, priest of the Holy Roman Church, spreads the faith in Bulgaria (A.D. 858), Anastasius, CXXVIII, 1374. LEUTHERIUS, bishop of Dorchester, preaches in West Saxony (A.D. 634–670), Bede, XCV, 126, 128. LINUS (St), disciple of St Peter the Apostle, ordained by him at Rome, scatters the seed of the Word (A.D. 45), Hugh, abbot, 26; Ekkehard, CLIV, 670. LIUDGER (St), bishop of Münster, evangelizes Frisia (A.D. 780), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 467. LIVINUS (St), a Scottish archbishop, proclaims Christ through Scotland, England, and Ireland (A.D. 648), St Boniface, CLXXXIX, 879.—[He preaches] at Ghent, ibid., 882. LUKE (St), Evangelist and companion of St Paul, writes his holy Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles at Rome (A.D. 58), [Col. 0539] Freculf, CVI, 1148; Anastasius, CXXVII, 468; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 101; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1643.—He accompanies St Paul everywhere, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 184.—He evangelizes Bithynia, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129, 185; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1698. LUCIAN, bishop, proclaims Christ to the people of Beauvais (A.D. 300), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 390. LUCIUS OF CYRENE preaches at Antioch (A.D. 44), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 114. LUCIUS, king of the Britons, asks Pope Eleutherius for preachers of the Gospel and embraces the faith (A.D. 167), Bede, XCV, 30; Anastasius, CXXVII, 528, 1249; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1310; William, CLXXIX, 1685; Henry, CXCV, 814. LOUIS THE GERMAN, king of the Franks, sends preachers to the Bulgars (A.D. 858), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1350. LUIDO, disciple of St Boniface, proclaims Christ in Bavaria and Alemania (A.D. 740), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 648. LULLUS, bishop-elect of Mainz, spreads the faith in Germany while St Boniface is still alive (A.D. 736), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 646, 653. LUPUS (St), bishop of Troyes, defends the faith in Britain against the Pelagians with St Germanus (A.D. 430), Sigebert, CLX, 82.

## M

MACLOVIUS (St), an Englishman by birth and bishop of Aleth, preaches with St Samson on the island of Aaron (Jersey) (A.D. 560), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 737. MADELGARIUS (St), who is also called Vincentius. See VINCENTIUS. MADELGISILUS, disciple of St Furseus, proclaims the Gospel at Centuria in Aquitaine (A.D. 650), Freculf, CLXXIV, 1443. MAGDALENE (St Mary), sister of Martha and St Lazarus, announces Christ’s resurrection to the Apostles (A.D. 33), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1474.—She lands at Marseilles and there preaches the faith with Blessed Lazarus (A.D. 48), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 156, 158; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493.—[She preaches] at Aix-en-Provence with St Maximinus (A.D. 48), CXII, 1494; Sigebert, CLX, 141.—She dies in Gaul (A.D. 88), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 255. MAGNUS, a monk, preaches on the Norwegian island of Windila (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 616. MALLONUS (St), bishop of Rouen, establishes Christ’s kingdom in Gaul (A.D. 280), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 390. MANAHEN (St) proclaims Christ at Antioch (A.D. 44), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 114. MANSCIUS, first [bishop] of York, promulgates the faith in Gaul (A.D. 90), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 255. MANSUETUS is sent by St Peter into Gaul to preach (A.D. 50), Anonymous, CLIV, 1117, 1124. MARCELLA (St), with St Mary Magdalene and Martha, lands at Marseilles (A.D. 48), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 156, 158; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493.—She preaches at Avignon with St Martha, Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1495. MARCELLINUS, one of Willibrord’s twelve companions, evangelizes Frisia (A.D. 692), Bede, XCV, 243. MARCELLUS proclaims Christ at Alexandria with St Mark the Evangelist (A.D. 72), Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 18. MARCELLUS (St), disciple of St Photinus of Lyons, evangelizes the Sequani in the city of Chalon (A.D. 180), Baldric, archbishop of Dol, CLXVI, 1210. MARK (St) THE EVANGELIST writes his Gospel at Rome (A.D. 46), St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 77.—He preaches at Aquileia and ordains Hermagoras bishop there, ibid., 78; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 181.—Taking his Gospel, approved by St Peter, into Egypt by way of Alexandria, he preaches there (A.D. 50), St Prosper of Aquitaine, priest, LI, 553; Freculf, CVI, 1149; Haymo, CXVIII, 829; St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 78; Anastasius, CXXVII, 460; Hermann the Lame, CXLIII, 57; Marianus Scotus, CXLVIII, 1305; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 181.—He preaches in Cyprus, ibid., 116.—He preaches through Libya, Marmarica, Pentapolis, Ammonica, Alexandria, and all Egypt, St Ado, CXXIII, 79; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 644, 648. MARCUS MARCELLUS EUGENIUS. See EUGENIUS. MARINUS II, deacon of the Apostolic See, is sent by St Nicholas I, pope, to preach in Bulgaria (A.D. 858), Anastasius, CXXVII, 1374. MARTHA, sister of St Mary Magdalene and St Lazarus, lands at the port of Marseilles (A.D. 48), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 156, 158; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493.—She proclaims Christ [Col. 0540] at Avignon, ibid., 1495.—[She preaches] at Tarascon, where she dies, ibid., 1497. MARTIAL (St), one of the seventy-two disciples and apostle of Limoges, is sent to Limoges to preach (A.D. 58), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175, 183.—He preaches at Toulouse and travels through Spain preaching, Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 169.—He preaches at Limoges, Ademar, monk, CXLI, 87, 42; Jordan, bishop of Limoges, CXLII, 1353; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1494.—[He preaches] at Toul and Agen, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 286.—[He preaches] at Garonne, ibid., 193. MARUTHAS, bishop, evangelizes the Persians (A.D. 379), Freculf, CVI, 1241, 1242; Sigebert, CLX, 80. MATERNUS (St), [sent] by St Peter the Apostle, proclaims Christ among the Treveri in Belgica (A.D. 50), Heriger, CXXXIX, 1010.—[He preaches] among the Tungri and the people of Cologne, ibid., 1013; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1118, 1125. MATTHEW (St), Apostle and Evangelist, receives the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost and preaches the faith (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 64, 65; Peter Comestor, CXXVIII, 1631.—Ethiopia falls to his lot for preaching, Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88; Haymo, 831.—He proclaims Christ first through Judaea, then through Macedonia, India, and Parthia, Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 111; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 168.—He writes his holy Gospel while preaching in Judaea (A.D. 45), St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 77; Anastasius, XXXVII, 458; Hermann the Lame, CXLIII, 57; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1305; Ekkehard, CLIV, 665.—He preaches through Ethiopia, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 168–172. MATTHIAS (St) is chosen by the Holy Spirit and the eleven Apostles in Judas’s place for the apostleship (A.D. 33), Haymo, CXVIII, 823; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 17.—On the day of Pentecost he receives the Holy Spirit and preaches the faith (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 64–65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1631.—He proclaims Christ in Judaea, Freculf, CVI, 1148; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 177. MARIA, queen of the Saracens, having embraced Christianity, requests for her people as bishop a certain Moses, a monk living in the desert (A.D. 374), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 514. MAXIMINUS (St), with St Mary Magdalene and Martha, lands at the port of Marseilles (A.D. 48), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 156, 158.—He preaches at Aix-en-Provence in Gaul, CXII, 1493; Sigebert, CLX, 141. MAXIMINUS, bishop of Trier, succeeds St Agricius, apostle of the Treveri (A.D. 342–368), Anonymous, CLIV, 1072, 1135. MEGENGAUD, disciple of St Boniface of Mainz, is granted the crown of martyrdom while preaching in Frisia (A.D. 730), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 647. MENHARD, bishop, proclaims Christ in Sweden, Norway, and the Orkneys, at Blasconia (A.D. 1069), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 653. MELLITUS (St), with Saints Augustine, Laurence, and others, is sent by St Gregory the Great, pope, to preach in England (A.D. 596), Anastasius, CXXVII, 645, 1370; Heriger, CXXXIX, 883.—He spreads the faith at London (A.D. 614), Bede, XCV, 85; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1332; Lanfranc, CL, 743, 764 (appendix); William, CLXXIX, 1443.—He converts the East Angles, together with their king Sigebert, to the faith (A.D. 604), Sigebert, CLX, 113; Henry, CXCV, 850. MELLO (St), archbishop, scatters the word of life at Rouen in Gaul (A.D. 119), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 386. MEMMIUS (St), Mancius, preaches through Gaul and Spain (A.D. 36–106), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 255, 256; Flodoard, CXXXV, 32; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1117, 1119. MENALCHIUS, archbishop, spreads Christ’s kingdom in England and Scotland with St Augustine (A.D. 630), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 874. METHODIUS, bishop, preaches in Moravia and converts Borivoj, king of the Bohemians, together with his people, to Christ (A.D. 885), Cosmas, dean of Prague, CLXVI, 71, 81. MOSES, first a monk living the ascetic life in the desert and then elected bishop of the Saracens, brings many to the faith (A.D. 374), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 515. TWO MONKS OF UNKNOWN NAME, coming from Bohemia, convert to Christ the Slavonic peoples—the Wagrians, Obotrites, Polabians, Warnabi, Chizzini, Circipani, and Linones—under King Gottschalk (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 573, 574.—They preach especially at Oldenburg, Lübice, Ratzeburg, and Mecklenburg, cities of the Obotrites, and receive the crown of martyrdom at Rethra, ibid., 574. [Col. 0541] A CAPTIVE WOMAN converts the people of the Iberians to Christ (A.D. 328), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 480.

## N

NAZARIUS, bishop, disseminates the words of life at Milan (A.D. 72), Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 18. NESTOR, bishop of Palencia, proclaims Christ in Spain (A.D. 37), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129, 130. NICASIUS (St), bishop of Rouen, is sent by St Dionysius the Areopagite into Gaul to preach (A.D. 70–100), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 386. NICHOLAS (St) I, pope, with Louis called the German, king of the Franks, sends apostles to preach the faith in Bulgaria (A.D. 858), Anastasius, CXXVIII, 1374. NICHOLAS, an Englishman by birth (later Pope Adrian IV), sent into Norway by Pope Eugenius III, brings the peoples to the faith (A.D. 1150), St Anselm, CLVIII, 1349. NINIA (St), or Ninian, a native of Britain, consecrated at Rome as bishop of Whithorn, converts to the faith the southern English, or Bernicians, of Scotland (A.D. 394), Bede, XCV, 121; William, CLXXIX, 1577; Henry, CXCV, 860.

## O

ODDO preaches at Ribe, a city of Denmark (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 616. ODINKAR THE ELDER, a native of Denmark and bishop in Sweden, extends Christ’s kingdom (A.D. 990, 1000), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 518, 526. ODINKAR THE YOUNGER, bishop of Ribe, proclaims the Gospel in Jutland (A.D. 1000), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 526, 535. OLAPH, king of the Norwegians, propagates Christ’s faith in his kingdom and sends preachers to Sweden, Gothland, and many islands beyond Norway (A.D. 1040), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 540. ANOTHER OLAPH labours to bring the peoples subject to him in Sweden to the Catholic faith; at his request Thurgot is ordained first bishop of Skara and preaches the Gospel in West Gothland (A.D. 1013), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 541. ONESIMUS (St), disciple of St Paul the Apostle, evangelizes Ephesus (A.D. 60–100), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129. OPPIUS, a centurion, sows the word of life in Spain (A.D. 35–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88. OSMAND, bishop, becomes a herald of the divine word in Sweden and Norway (A.D. 1069), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 568, 617. OSWALD, king of the English, restores the peoples to the faith and renews the religion that had been lost in his kingdom (A.D. 650), Bede, XCV, 115. OSTEAR, bishop of Worcester, proclaims Christ to the Mercian English (A.D. 730), William, CLXXIX, 1587. OSWALD, king of the Northumbrians, brings his people to the faith, appoints Aidan, summoned from Scotland, to Lindisfarne, and himself explains to the people, as interpreter, the bishop’s words (A.D. 640), Bede, XCV, 115, 117; Henry, CXCV, 860. OSWIU, king of the Mercian English, brings his people back to the faith (A.D. 655), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1336; Henry, CXCV, 863. OTTO THE GREAT, emperor of Germany, imposes the faith upon the Slavs (A.D. 940), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 503.

## P
PALLADIUS, first bishop of the Scots, sent by Pope Celestine, preaches the faith in Scotland (A.D. 430), Bede, XCV, 121 (n.); Henry, CXCV, 822. PARMENUS preaches at Avignon in Gaul with Saint Martha and Marcella (A.D. 48), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1495. PATERNUS (St), of Toledo and afterwards bishop of Constance, is converted to the faith by Saint Saturninus (A.D. 76), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 245.—He preaches at Bilbilis in Spain and brings the people of Bilbilis to Christ (A.D. 94), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 265.—He traverses Gaul, preaching after the manner of the apostles (A.D. 130), ibid., 311. PATRICK (St), bishop of Ireland, sent into Ireland by the blessed Pope Celestine, converts its peoples to the faith (A.D. 432), Bede, XCV, 122 (n.); Guigo II, prior of the Carthusians, CLIII, 789, 801; St Anselm, CLIX, 325; Sigebert, CLX, 79; William, CLXXIX, 1688.—He is recalled to England by Blessed Germanus, bishop of Auxerre (A.D. 433), ibid.; he dies in England, ibid., 1689. PATROBAS, disciple of Saint Titus, proclaims Christ on the island of Crete (A.D. 68), Freculf, CVI, 1149. PAULINUS (St), apostle of the English with Saint Augustine and others [Col. 0542], and bishop both of York and Rochester, travels through England preaching (A.D. 625), Bede, XCV, 94, 105; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1334; Lanfranc, CL, 743, 764; William, CLXXIX, 1500, 1553.—Edwin, king of the English, is converted to the faith by St Paulinus, XCV, 105; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1335.—Among the Northumbrian English he preaches in the eastern district, in the royal city of Adgebzim, at Melmim among the Bernicians, and at Cataracta among the Deirans, Bede, XCV, 107; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 118; Henry, CXCV, 856.—He converts the province of Lindsey, ibid., 844, 856. PAULINUS (St), patriarch of Aquileia, preaches the faith among the Carantanians and Avars and converts many to Christ (A.D. 790–804), St Paulinus, XCIX, 69, 70; Alcuin, C, 190, 192.—He labours tirelessly in converting the Hungarians, St Paulinus, XCIX, 73, 74.—And the Huns, ibid., 76–77; Alcuin, C, 187, 198. PAUL (St), the apostle, also called Saul for twelve years, until the conversion of Sergius Paulus at Salamis, is converted by Christ the Lord on the road to Damascus and receives baptism from Ananias, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 107; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1671.—He preaches in the synagogues (A.D. 34), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 131; Anastasius, CXXVII, 454; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 17; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1304.—He is called to the apostleship to the Gentiles, Haymo, CXVIII, 825; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 17.—At Antioch, with St Barnabas, he proclaims the Gospel, Freculf, CVI, 1125; Anastasius, CXXVII, 456, 458.—He traverses Asia preaching, ibid., 460.—In Asia Minor he first writes the Epistle to the Corinthians (A.D. 53), ibid., 464.—He preaches at Athens, Haymo, CXVIII, 827.—He converts Dionysius the Areopagite, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116, 124; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1701.—Through Cilicia and Syria, Illyricum, Moesia, Galatia, Troas, Macedonia, and Lydia, he spreads the faith with Silas, Timothy, and Barnabas, Freculf, CVI, 1130; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anastasius, CXXVII, 464; Heriger, CXXXIX, 1008; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639.—With Barnabas he sails through Seleucia, Cyprus, and Salamis, preaching, Anastasius, CXXVII, 460; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 114.—At Salamis he converts the proconsul Sergius Paulus to Christ, ibid.; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1690.—With Saint Barnabas he preaches through Iconium, Lycaonia, Lystra, and Pisidia, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 115; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1693.—Through Phoenicia and Samaria, ibid., 1691.—With Silas and Timothy through Syria, Cilicia, Derbe, and Lystra, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116, 125; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1692, 1698. At Jerusalem (A.D. 18), Anastasius, CXXVII, 466; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 17; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 640, 645; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 24; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 108; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1672, 1689.—At Corinth, Anastasius, CXXVII, 464; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 124; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1704.—At Ephesus and Miletus, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 125; Peter Comestor, CXXVIII, 1704.—He appeals to Caesar and reaches Rome in chains (A.D. 58), Sulpicius Severus, XX, 114; St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 173; Haymo, CXVIII, 830; St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 79; Anastasius, CXXVII, 466, 468; Hermann the Lame, CXLIII, 58; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 640; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1305; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 128; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1715.—He contends against Simon Magus, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 132.—At Rome he writes various Epistles, namely those to the Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, and Colossians (A.D. 58–69), Anastasius, CXXVII, 468.—He evangelizes the West and Gaul, Heriger, CXXXIX, 1008; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 128.—With Saints Philemon and Timothy he travels through Spain preaching (A.D. 64), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 190; St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 79.—At Rome, with Saint Peter, he receives the crown of martyrdom (A.D. 66), Freculf, CVI, 1132; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 136. PAUL (St) SERGIUS, proconsul, is converted by Saint Paul the apostle at Salamis (A.D. 48), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 114; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1690.—As bishop at Narbonne in Gaul, he proclaims the word of the Lord (A.D. 60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 195; St Gregory of Tours, LXXX, 175, 183; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493. PAUL, bishop of Populonia, is sent by Pope St Nicholas I to preach in Bulgaria (A.D. 858), Anastasius, CXXVIII, 1374. PETHELMUS, apostle of the West Saxons and bishop of Candida Casa, evangelizes Scotland in the remotest parts of England (A.D. 725), William, CLXXIX, 1577. PETER (St), apostle and chief of the apostles, with the other eleven receives the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost and by his first sermon converts three thousand Jews to Christ [Col. 0543] (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 64, 65, 102; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1631.—At the gate of the Temple in Jerusalem, with Saint John, he heals a lame man and brings many to Christ, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 103, 104; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1655.—He preaches in Jerusalem, Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 134.—He holds the first Council of Jerusalem, Anastasius, CXXVII, 456.—He evangelizes Caesarea and baptizes the centurion Cornelius with his whole household, Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 134; Freculf, CVI, 1125; Haymo, CXVIII, 826; Anastasius, CXXVII, 456; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 109, 120.—He travels through all Palestine and Asia preaching; he proclaims Christ at Lydda, Ptolemais, Tyre, Sidon, Berytus, Tripoli, Antaradus, Laodicea, and Antioch, where he held his first episcopal see, Anastasius, CXXVI, 456; Heriger, CXXXIX, 1008; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25; Ekkehard, CLIV, 667; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116, 122; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674, 1701.—He traverses Pontus, Asia Minor, Galatia, Cappadocia, and Bithynia, Freculf, CVI, 1135; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anonymous, CLIV, 1116; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 122, 124; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1679, 1696.—Returning to Jerusalem, he converts many Samaritans to the faith, Anastasius, CXXVII, 454, 462.—He comes to Rome, founds the episcopal see, and rules for twenty-five years, proclaiming the truth and working miracles (A.D. 45–69), Lactantius, VII, 621; Sulpicius Severus, XX, 145; St Prosper of Aquitaine, LI, 553; St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 173; Freculf, CVI, 1128; Haymo, CXVIII, 829; Anastasius, CXXVII, 438; Hermann the Lame, CXLIII, 57; Marianus Scotus, CXLVI, 641; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25; Ekkehard, CLIV, 667, 1116; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 122.—He preaches through Africa and Egypt (A.D. 50), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 162, 163.—Through Spain, ibid., 161, 162, 163.—Through Gaul and in England, Anastasius, CXXVII, 458, 466, 468; Heriger, CXXXIX, 1008.—After returning to Rome, he ordains priests and bishops in various places: namely Torquatus, Thesiphon, Caecilius, Iscius, Secundus, Indalecius, and Euphrasius, whom he sends into Spain to preach (A.D. 53), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 151.—He sends others into England, Anastasius, CXXVII, 460.—He writes his first Epistle to the Dispersion, ibid., 466.—He ordains Linus and Cletus at Rome, Abbot Hugh, CLIV.—He sends them into Gaul to preach, ibid., 25; Anonymous, CLIV, 1117.—At Rome, with St Paul, he is crowned with martyrdom, Aurelius Cassiodorus (A.D. 66), Freculf, CVI, 1132; Heriger, CXXXIX, 1008; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 123, 136. PETER (St), bishop of Braga, preaches in Spain (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 109. PETER (St), of Castro Novo, a Cistercian monk, upholds the true faith against the Albigensians (A.D. 1206), Sicard, CCXIII, 545, 549. PHAGANUS (St), sent into England by Pope Eleutherius, converts King Lucinus and his people to the faith (A.D. 166), William, CLXXIX, 1685. PHILEMON (St), with Saint Paul and Timothy, travels through Spain preaching (A.D. 64), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 190. PHILIP (St), apostle, having received the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, preaches the faith of Christ (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 64, 65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1631.—He receives Scythia and Gaul by lot as his field for evangelization, Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88.—Among the Gauls, the nations separated by the swelling ocean, and the Phrygians at Hierapolis, he proclaims Christ, Freculf, CVI, 1148; William, CLXXIX, 1683; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 156; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1698.—From Gaul he sends preachers into England, ibid., 1683. PHILIP (St), one of the seven deacons ordained with Saint Stephen, disseminates the faith in Samaria (A.D. 34), Freculf, CVI, 1123; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1490; Haymo, CXVIII, 825; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 106; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1668.—He baptizes the eunuch of Queen Candace, Haymo, CXVIII, 825; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 107; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1670.—From Azotus as far as Samaria he spreads the words of faith, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 107. PHILIP OF MILAN, surnamed Philotheus, converted by St Paul and sent into Spain, proclaims the kingdom of God at Toledo, Barcelona, Zaragoza, Seville, Valencia, and many other cities (A.D. 91), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 261, 263. PHOTINUS (St), first bishop of Lyons, preaches in Gaul (A.D. 116), Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 96; Balderic, CLXXII, 1209. PILATE, who unjustly handed over Our Lord Jesus Christ to be scourged and crucified, reports his death, miracles, and resurrection to the emperor Tiberius and the Roman senate [Col. 0544] (A.D. 38), Freculf, CVI, 1124; Haymo, CXVIII, 826; St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 75, 76; Hermann the Lame, CXLIII, 57; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1304; Ekkehard, CXLVIII, 663. PIUS, first bishop of Seville, proclaims the Gospel in Spain (A.D. 37–70), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 128. POLYCARP (St), disciple of Saint John and bishop of Smyrna (A.D. 125), Freculf, CVI, 1164. A certain PONTIUS, a soldier, converts Philip, emperor of the Romans, and his son Philip to Christ (A.D. 240), Freculf, CVI, 1178; Orderic, CXVIII, 70. POPPO, a cleric and afterwards bishop of Aarhus, preaches among the Danes and converts Harold, king of the Danes (A.D. 966), Anonymous, CXXXIX, 1207, 1208; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 525 (n.); Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 191. POPPO, bishop of Schleswig, proclaims Christ among the Danes and Swedes under King Eric (A.D. 1010–1015), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 525, 526.—With Odinkar, he evangelizes the Jutland town of Schleswig, or Slagwig, ibid., CXLVI, 535. POTENTIANUS preaches the faith among the Senones (A.D. 50), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493. PRISCA preaches in Asia Minor with Paul and Aquila (A.D. 50), Freculf, CVI, 1130. PRISCILLA evangelizes Asia Minor with Paul and Aquila (A.D. 50), Haymo, CXVIII, 829. PROCORIUS (St), sent by Pope John XIII, proclaims the Gospel of the kingdom to the Poles (A.D. 970), John XIII, CXXXV, 949. PUTTA, first bishop of Hereford, sows the faith in the province of the Mercian English (A.D. 720), William, CLXXIX, 1599.

## Q

QUADRATUS (St) gathers the Church at Athens (A.D. 120), St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 82. QUINTINUS (St), bishop of Amiens, evangelizes Amiens (A.D. 250), Folcard, CXLVII, 1182; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 390.—Preaching at Augusta, city of the Viromandui, he dies a martyr (A.D. 287), St Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1496. QUIRINUS (St), with Saint Nicaise and Saint Dionysius, preaches at Rouen in Gaul (A.D. 70), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 386.

## R

RADULFUS (St), a Cistercian monk, upholds the true faith among the Albigensians (A.D. 1206), Sicard, CCXIII, 545, 549. RAGIMBERTUS, priest, scatters seeds of the Gospel among the Danes and Swedes (A.D. 860), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 999. RATOLPHUS, or ROTOLPHUS, becomes a herald of the divine word at Schleswig, a Danish city (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 616, 623, 668. REGIMBRONDUS, bishop of Harusanna, apostle in Cismarine Denmark, or Jutland (A.D. 948), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 503. REHINERUS, first bishop on the island of Funen (A.D. 1040), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 623. REMIGIUS (St), bishop of Rheims, baptizes the Frankish nation together with its king Clovis (A.D. 496), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 152; St Ado, bishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 97; Hincmar, CXXV, 1157; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1329; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 79. RECCARED, the Arian king of the Visigoths dwelling in Spain, returns to the true faith and brings his people to Christ (A.D. 589), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 493; John of Biclaro, bishop, LXXII, 869. RIMBERTUS, a Danish priest, preaches among the Swedes in the city of Birka (A.D. 854), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 997; (A.D. 860), ibid., 999.—Chosen bishop of Hamburg, he proclaims Christ to Danes and Saxons, Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 486. ROGER, count of the Normans in Sicily, brings a certain Chamut, one of the leading men, with his whole family, to the faith (A.D. 1080), Geoffrey the monk, CXLIX, 1187.—He establishes bishops throughout Sicily, Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 486; Geoffrey the monk, CXLIX, 1188. RODOLPHUS, bishop of Schleswig in Denmark, preaches in Jutland and Sweden (A.D. 1036), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 541, 552, 621, 668. RUDOLFUS, disciple of St Boniface of Mainz, preaches the faith in Bavaria [Col. 0545] and Alemannia (A.D. 740), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 648. RUFINIANUS, sent into England with Saint Augustine, proclaims Christ (A.D. 596), Lanfranc, CL, 743, 764; Henry, CXCV, 844. RUFINUS (St), confessor, preaches among the people of Rheims in Gaul (A.D. 250), St Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1496.

## S

SABINUS (St), with Saint Potentianus, becomes a herald of the divine word in Gaul (A.D. 50), Rabanus, CXII, 1493. Certain captive PRIESTS preach in Thrace and Asia, and innumerable Asiatic barbarians are converted to the faith (A.D. 330), Aurelius Cassiodorus, LXIX, 939. SAMSON, bishop of Aleth, proclaims Christ on the island of Aarow (Jersey), with Saint Maclovius (A.D. 560), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 737. SANCTINUS (St), one of the seventy-two disciples, bishop of Meaux and Verdun, proclaims the Gospel with Saint Dionysius (A.D. 70), Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 27, 28.—At Trier in Belgica (A.D. 97), ibid. SATURNINUS (St) preaches at Toulouse in Gaul (A.D. 58), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175, 183; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1494. SAUL. See PAUL the apostle. SCUVICULUS, deacon, sent into Gaul by Saint Dionysius with Nicaise, preaches at Rouen (A.D. 70), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 388. SECUNDUS, ordained at Rome by St Peter the apostle, returns to Spain to preach (A.D. 43), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 151, 154.—He preaches at Castrum near Turgia (A.D. 100), ibid., 275. POPE SERGIUS baptizes Ceadual, king of the Saxons (A.D. 688), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1339. SEVERINUS, abbot, apostle and patron of the Norici (A.D. 482), St Paulinus of Aquileia, XCIX, 69. SEVERUS, a native of Gaul and bishop of Trier, defends the faith in England against the Pelagians with Saint Germanus, bishop of Auxerre (A.D. 432), Henry, CXCV, 827. SEWARDUS preaches in Norway (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 650. SEXIFIRMUS, bishop, spreads the faith of Christ in Baetica (A.D. 50), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 163. SIGOFRIDUS, monk of Glastonbury, extends the kingdom of Christ in Sweden, Normandy, and Norway (A.D. 1050), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 651. SIGUARDUS, bishop, preaches in Normandy and Norway (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 651. SILAS, with Paul the apostle, proclaims the Gospel through Macedonia, Achaia, Syria, and Cilicia (A.D. 50), Anastasius, CXXVII, 464.—He preaches at Derbe and Lystra, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1692. SILVESTER (St), pope, baptizes the Emperor Constantine the Great (A.D. 312), St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 91; Anastasius, CXXVII, 1511; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 44. SIMEON, son of Cleophas, called the Zealot, one of the twelve apostles chosen by the Lord, receives the Holy Spirit with the other apostles on the day of Pentecost and proclaims the faith of the Gospel to the peoples (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 64, 65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1631.—He preaches in Babylonia in Persia, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 172–176.—He is ordained bishop of Jerusalem (A.D. 70), Freculf, CVI, 1146; Haymo, CXVIII, 833.—At Antioch, while preaching, he receives the crown of martyrdom (A.D. 107), Freculf, CVII, 1158. SIMEON JUDAS, or THADDAEUS, preaches through Mesopotamia, inner Pontus, and Persia (A.D. 34), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 172; see Thaddaeus. SIMEON, bishop of Hälsingland, preaches in Sweden to the Scriptefingi, Weimilani, and Finns (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 641. SIMEON, called Niger, preaches at Antioch (A.D. 44), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 114. SINICIUS (St) is sent by Saint Peter the apostle into Gaul to evangelize the people of Trier (A.D. 50), Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25.—He preaches at Rheims and Soissons (A.D. 90), CXXXV, 32; Abbot Hugh, CLVI, 1124. SISEBUTHUS, king of the Goths in Spain, brings his subjects who still remain Arians to the faith of Christ (A.D. 639), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 121. SIXTUS (St), first bishop of Rheims, is sent by Blessed Peter the apostle into Gaul to preach (A.D. 50), Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25.—He preaches at Rheims and Soissons (A.D. 90), Flodoard, CXXXV, 32. SKIRBALT, deacon and companion of St Boniface of Mainz, proclaims Christ with him in Germany and Frisia [Col. 0546] (A.D. 730), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 660. SOLEMNIS, bishop of Chartres in England, preaches among the Franks in Gaul and converts many to Christ (A.D. 490), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 93. SOSTHENES, disciple of Saint Paul the apostle, preaches at Corinth (A.D. 60–100), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129. STEPHEN (St), one of the seven deacons first ordained by the apostles and the protomartyr of Jerusalem, proclaims Christ (A.D. 34), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 105; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1663. STREMONIUS (St) is sent by St Peter the apostle into Gaul to preach and evangelizes the Arverni (A.D. 58), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175, 183. STURMIUS, companion and fellow worker of St Boniface of Mainz, preaches in Germany and Frisia (A.D. 740), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 647, 805. SWIBERTUS (St) spreads the faith through Lower Frisia and in Ireland (A.D. 692), Bede, XCV, 243.

## T

TADICUS preaches in Sweden (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617. TATUINUS, disciple of Saint Boniface, was a preacher of the Gospel in Germany and Frisia (A.D. 750), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 741. TAURINUS (St), bishop of York, apostle in Gaul (A.D. 119), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 386. THADDAEUS (St), one of Christ’s twelve apostles, preaches at Edessa and converts King Abgar to Christ (A.D. 36), Freculf, CXI, 1123; Haymo, CXVIII, 824.—He propagates the Gospel through Mesopotamia, inner Pontus, and Persia, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 172. THEODORUS (St) travels throughout all Carpetania preaching (A.D. 52), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 167. THEODORUS, bishop of Malmesbury, preaches in England (A.D. 613), William, CLXXIX, 1443; Peter Comestor, CXCVLI, 782. THESIPHON, ordained at Rome by Saint Peter, proclaims the Gospel in Spain (A.D. 41), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 135.—Having become bishop of Vergilia, he evangelizes all Baetica, ibid., 175. QUEEN THEUDELIND brings her husband Agilulf, king of the Lombards, with his people, to Christ (A.D. 595), Mozarabic Liturgy, LXXXV, 541; Ekkehard, CLIV, 797. THIRSUS (St), deacon, sent into Gaul by Saint Polycarp, proclaims Christ (A.D. 140), St Augustine, apostle of the English, LXXX, 41, 187; John the monk, CLXII, 756.—Among the Lingones, St Augustine, LXXX, 188, 199. Among the Senones, John the monk, CLXII, 757. THOMAS (St), one of the twelve apostles, having received the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, preaches the Gospel (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 64, 65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1631.—He receives India and Parthia by lot as his field for evangelization (A.D. 34), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 478; Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88; Haymo, CXVIII, 831.—He proclaims the faith in Parthia, Bactria, and India (A.D. 34–53), Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 157.—At Calamina in India he receives the crown of martyrdom (A.D. 70), Freculf, CVI, 1147. THOOLFUS, bishop of Trondheim, preaches in Norway and Sweden with Saint Sewardus (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 650. THURGOTHUS, first bishop of Sacrana, summoned into West Gothland by King Olaf, converts the Gothic peoples to Christ (A.D. 1013), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 541, 640. THUROLFUS, bishop of Blascona, preaches in the Orkney Islands (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 653. TIBERIUS, Roman emperor, reports Christ’s resurrection and miracles to the Roman senate and people, and unsuccessfully attempts to have him enrolled among the gods of the empire (A.D. 38), Haymo, CXVIII, 826. TIMOTHY (St), disciple of Saint Paul, preaches throughout Asia (A.D. 60), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129.—At Ephesus (A.D. 68), Freculf, CVI, 1149.—With St Paul he travels through Galatia, Phrygia, Mysia, Troas, Macedonia, and Lydia (A.D. 50), Orderic, CLXXXXVIII, 116.—He preaches in Spain, Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 190.—At Rheims in Gaul with Saint Apollinaris (A.D. 90), Flodoard, CXXXV, 31. TITUS (St), disciple of Saint Paul the apostle, sows the words of faith on the island of Crete (A.D. 58), Freculf, CVI, 1149; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129.—At Jerusalem with Saint Paul (A.D. 50), Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 640, 645. TORPES proclaims Christ at Alexandria with Saint Mark the Evangelist [Col. 0547] (A.D. 72), Regino of Prüm, CXXXIII, 18. TORQUATUS, ordained at Rome by Saint Peter, evangelizes the southern parts of Spain and Baetica (A.D. 44–70), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 155. TOTTA, bishop of Leicester, evangelizes the southern English (A.D. 640), William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1605. TRITEL, bishop of Hereford, teaches the Mercian English the faith of Christ (A.D. 740), William, CLXXIX, 1599. TROPHIMUS (St), first bishop of Arles, sent by Saint Peter into Gaul, preaches at Arles (A.D. 58), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175, 183; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1495; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129. TRUDO, abbot of Hasbania, preaches in Gaul (A.D. 651), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 123. TYCHICHUS, disciple of Saint Paul, proclaims the Gospel at Paphos (A.D. 58–100), Orderic, CXXXVIII, 129.

## U

ULTANUS (St), with Saints Froillanus and Furseus, preaches in Gaul (A.D. 640), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 122. UNNI, bishop of Hamburg, preaches among the Danes and Swedes and converts many (A.D. 903–936), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 498.—At Birka in Sweden (A.D. 915), ibid., 499. UNNI, bishop of Winchester, apostle in England (A.D. 660), Bede, XCV, 127. URSMARUS (St), bishop of Flanders, preaches at the city of Aldenburg in Flanders (A.D. 690), Hariulf, abbot of Aldenburg, CLXXIV, 1461.

## V

VALERIANUS, disciple of Saint Photinus, bishop of Lyons, evangelizes the Aedui in Gaul (A.D. 180), Baldric, CLXVI, 1210. VALERIUS, confessor, preaches at Trier in Belgica (A.D. 48), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493.—At Rheims in Gaul, Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1496; Heriger, CXXXIX, 1010; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, CLIV, 1116, 1118.—Through Gaul and Germany, ibid., 1124. VEDASTUS (St) proclaims the Gospel at Cambrai in Gaul (A.D. 490), Lambert of Arras, CXLIX, 26, 28.—He brings Clovis, king of the Franks, to Saint Remigius for baptism (A.D. 496), ibid., 28. VICELINUS, apostle of Wagria (A.D. 1125), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 455. VICTORICUS (St), a native of Rome, preaches in Gaul (A.D. 250), St Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1494; Folcard the monk, CXLVII, 1182. VINCENTIUS (St), also called Madelgarius, proclaims Christ at Altimontium and Sonegium in Gaul (A.D. 651), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 123. VIRGILIUS, bishop of Salzburg, labours with Blessed Paulinus of Aquileia to convert the Carantanians (A.D. 784), St Paulinus of Aquileia, CXIX, 70. VIVILIUS, or Vivalus of Passau, bishop in Bavaria, preaches with Saint Boniface of Mainz (A.D. 730), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 649, 687, 806. VULFRAMNUS (St), bishop of Sens, proclaims Christ among the Frisians (A.D. 718), Helinand, CCXII, 812.

## W

WACCAR, monk and companion of Saint Boniface, evangelizes Germany and Frisia with him (A.D. 740), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 660. WALLUS, bishop of Ribe, apostle in Jutland (A.D. 1026), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 552, 621. WALTHERI, priest and companion of Saint Boniface of Mainz, spreads the words of faith with him in Germany and Frisia (A.D. 730), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 660. WARBERSUS, co-bishop and fellow worker of St Boniface, apostle in Germany (A.D. 745), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 757. WELANDUS, king of the Danes, embraces the faith with his wife and sons (A.D. 862), Hincmar, CXXV, 1206. WERA, co-bishop and fellow worker of Saint Boniface of Mainz, preaches the faith in Germany (A.D. 745), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 757. WERENFRIDUS, one of the twelve companions of Willibrord, apostle in Frisia (A.D. 692), Bede, XCV, 243. WICBERTUS (St), monk of Gembloux, converts many by preaching in Hungary (A.D. 953), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 672. WIGBERTUS (St), abbot of Fritzlar, is joined to Saint Boniface in Germany in aid of the preaching of the Gospel [Col. 0548] (A.D. 730–747), Servatus Lupus of Ferrières, CXIX, 684. WIGO, bishop and disciple of Saint Boniface, preaches in Bavaria and Alemannia (A.D. 740), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 648. WILFERIUS, king of the Mercians, brings Edelwalt, king of the South Saxons, to Christ (A.D. 700), William, CLXXIX, 1549. WILFRID (St), bishop of York, converts the South Saxons to the faith (A.D. 678), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1338; William, CLXXIX, 1553; Henry, XCV, 866.—As an exile he preaches in Frisia and converts Adalgisus, king of the Frisians (A.D. 680), William, CLXXIX, 1559.—Having returned to England, he is chosen bishop of Selsey in Mercia, ibid., 1549. WILLEHAD (St), first bishop of Bremen, preaches in Frisia (A.D. 754), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 1015; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 465, 469, 471.—At Hamarcham, St Ansgar, CXVIII, 1016.—At Thrianta (Dreuterland), ibid.—Sent by Charlemagne into Saxony, he preaches among the people of Verden and Bremen, converts and baptizes many Saxons and Frisians (A.D. 780), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 1017; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 466.—Throughout Wigmodia he builds churches, St Ansgar, CXVIII, 1017.—Returning from Rome to Frisia, he is consecrated bishop of Bremen at Plexem and dies while preaching (A.D. 789), ibid., 1019–1021. WILLIAM (St), bishop, preaches in Zealand (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 616, 623. WILLERICUS, bishop of Bremen in Saxony, succeeds St Willehad (A.D. 789–838), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 471.—He first evangelizes the Transalbians and proclaims Christ at the city of the Milingi (A.D. 830), ibid., 472. WILLIBALD, fellow worker of Saint Boniface, preaches at the German city of Eichstätt (A.D. 731–747), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 646, 806.—He is consecrated bishop of Eichstätt (A.D. 746), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1342.—He preaches in Thuringia (A.D. 741), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 757, 806. WILLIBALD (St), sent by Pope John with Procorius, evangelizes the Poles and Wends (A.D. 970), Pope John XIII, 949. WILLIBRORD (St), first apostle of the Frisians, an Anglo-Saxon by nation and born in Northumbria, comes into Franconia with twelve companions in order to preach (A.D. 690), Alcuin, CI, 697.—He evangelizes Frisia (A.D. 692–700), Bede, XCV, 243; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1339; John the monk, CLXII, 786; Helinand, CCXII, 805. He goes to Rome, where he is ordained bishop of Utrecht, and returns to preach in Frisia, Alcuin, CI, 698.—He preaches in Denmark, ibid., 699.—He preaches throughout all Francia, builds churches, and ordains priests, ibid., 701.—With Saint Boniface of Mainz he spreads the faith of Christ far and wide in Germany and converts many to religion (A.D. 717–723), St Boniface, CXXXIX, 642. WILLIHERI, monk and companion of Saint Boniface of Mainz, preaches in Frisia and receives the glory of martyrdom from the Saxons (A.D. 755), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 660. WINFRIDUS, bishop of the English, preaches in England (A.D. 656), Helinand, CCXII, 782. WINFRIDUS, also called Boniface, English by origin, preaches in Germany (A.D. 717), Bernold, CXLVIII, 148, 1341.—He converts the Hessians and Thuringians, Adam of Bremen, CXLI, 466. See BONIFACE. WINNIBALD, brother of St Willibald, preaches in Germany with Saint Boniface of Mainz and is granted the crown of martyrdom (A.D. 736), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 1647; Freculf, CVI, 646. WINTRUNG, priest and companion of Saint Boniface, proclaims Christ in Frisia and suffers martyrdom (A.D. 755), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 660. WITMARUS, monk, preaches in Denmark and converts the king of the Swedes with his people to Christ (A.D. 830), St Ansgar, CXVIII, 791. WITTA, also called Wisa or Wethanus, of St Barbara’s, or Warbarbarana’s, at Warburg, sows the Word of faith in Germany (A.D. 730–742), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 749.—With Saint Winnibald, Freculf, CVI, 646. WOLFGANG, bishop of Regensburg, preaches in Pannonia (A.D. 974), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 402. WOLFREDUS, a native of Britain, converts many to Christ in Sweden by preaching and destroys the idols of false gods (A.D. 1029), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 543. WULFRANUS. See WULFRAMNUS.

## Z

ZACHARIAS (St), bishop of Lyons and successor of Saint Irenaeus [Col. 0549], proclaims Christ in Gaul (A.D. 195), John the monk, CLXV, 756. [Col. 0550] ZENO (St), bishop of Verona, brings the city of Verona to Christ (A.D. 368), St Zeno of Verona, XI, 150.

## LXXIII. GEOGRAPHICAL INDEX OF THE PREACHING OF THE GOSPEL AND THE CONVERSION OF THE NATIONS, OR AN ALPHABETICAL SYNOPSIS OF ALL PARTS OF THE WORLD, PROVINCES, REGIONS, PEOPLES, AND CITIES FIRST GIFTED WITH THE LIGHT OF THE GOSPEL, WITH MENTION OF THE APOSTLES AND PREACHERS WHO BROUGHT THEM THE WORDS OF LIFE, FROM THE INCARNATION OF THE WORD TO THE YEAR 1216.

[Col. 0553] A

**AARON**, an island of England, now Jersey, received the Christian faith from St Maclovius and Samson, bishops of Aletha (A.D. 560), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 737.

**ACHAIA**, the region of the Peloponnese, was evangelized by St Andrew the Apostle (A.D. 38), Freculf, bishop of Lisieux, CVI, 1147; Haymo, bishop of Halberstadt, CXVIII, 831; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 139, 142–147.—St Paul the Apostle and Silas (A.D. 50), Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVII, 464.

**ADGEBZIM**, the royal city of the East Angles or Northumbrians, was evangelized by Bishop Paulinus, apostle of the English together with St Augustine (A.D. 604–625), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 107; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 118; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 856.

**ADMURUM WALTON**, a city of the Middle Angles on the island of Lindisfarne, now Holy Island, was evangelized by Finanus, who converted King Penda and his people (A.D. 653), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 150; William of Malmesbury, monk, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 863.

**THE AEDUI**, a people of Gaul, were evangelized by Valerianus, disciple of St Photinus (A.D. 180), Baldric, archbishop of Dol, CLXVI, 1210.

**EGYPT** was evangelized by St Peter (A.D. 50), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 163.—St Mark the Evangelist (A.D. 50), St Prosper of Aquitaine, LI, 553; Haymo, bishop of Halberstadt, CXVIII, 829; St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 78, 79; Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVII, 460; Hermannus Contractus, CXLIII, 57; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 644, 648; Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1305.

**ETHIOPIA** was evangelized by St Matthew the Evangelist, Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88; Haymo, bishop of Halberstadt, CXVIII, 831; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 168–172.—St Philip the deacon baptized the eunuch of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. Haymo, bishop of Halberstadt, CXVIII, 825; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 107; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1670.

**AFRICA.** St Peter the Apostle went to Africa (A.D. 50), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 163.

**AGEDUNUM**, Agen, was evangelized by St Martial, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 286.

**ALBANIA** in Asia was preached to by St Bartholomew the Apostle (A.D. 34; others, 38), Freculf, bishop of Lisieux, CVI, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 165.

**ALBANUM**, or **ALBAGH**, Van, a city of Armenia, was evangelized by St Bartholomew, who there suffered martyrdom (A.D. 71), Freculf, bishop of Lisieux, CVI, 1147.

**AMONG THE ALBIGENSES**, inhabitants of southern Gaul, Peter of Castelnau and St Radulphus, Cistercian monks, preached (A.D. 1206), Peter the monk, CCXIII, 545, 549, 556, 557.—Diego, bishop of Osma, in the province of Narbonne (A.D. 1206), ibid., 549.—Arnaudus, Cistercian abbot, with twelve abbots of the same order (A.D. 1207), ibid., 554, 555.—Fulk, bishop of Toulouse, and Navarrus, bishop of Comminges (A.D. 1207), ibid., 554, 561.—Guy, abbot of Vaux-de-Cernay (A.D. 1207), ibid., 555, 578.—St Dominic (A.D. 1208), ibid., 555, 556.

**ALDENBURG**, or **OLDENBURG**, in Flanders, Oudenburg (Belgium), received the faith through Ursmarus, first bishop of Aldenburg (A.D. 690), Harnolfus, abbot of Aldenburg, appendix, CLXXIV, 1461.

**ALDINBURG** in Wagria, Altenburg (Holstein), was evangelized by Egwardus, or Evagrius, first bishop of Aldinburg [Col. 0554] (A.D. 980), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 508 (n.).—Two monks of unknown name coming from Bohemia (A.D. 1065), ibid., 574.—Ezzo, bishop of Aldinburg (A.D. 1065), ibid., 574, 617.

**AT ALETHA**, a city on the island of Aaron, Jersey, St Maclovius and Samson, bishops of Aletha, preached (A.D. 560), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 737.

**AT ALEXANDRIA**, in Egypt, St Mark the Evangelist preached (A.D. 50), St Prosper of Aquitaine, LI, 553; Freculf, CVI, 1149; St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 79; Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVII, 460; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 644, 648; Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1305; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 181.—Anianus, bishop of Alexandria and successor of St Mark (A.D. 68), Marianus Scotus, CXLVI, 649.—Apuleius, Marcellus, and Torpes (A.D. 72), Regino, abbot of Prüm, CXXXII, 18.

**THE ALEMANNI** were evangelized by St Gallus (A.D. 614–646), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 115.—St Boniface, bishop of Mainz, and his disciples Liudo, Rudalthus, and Wigo (A.D. 740), St Boniface, bishop of Mainz, LXXXIX, 648.

**ALONE**, Alicante? a city of Spain, received the Gospel through St Iscius (A.D. 52), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 167–169.

**IN ALSACE**, a region of Gaul, Eucharius, bishop of Trier, Valerius the confessor, and Maternus, sent into Gaul by St Peter, preached (A.D. 50), Anonymous, CLIV, 1117, 1118.

**ALTIMONIUM** in Gaul was evangelized by Vincentius and Tirtel, bishop of Hereford (A.D. 650–740), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 123; William of Malmesbury, monk, CLXXIX, 1599.

**AMBIANUM** in Belgium, Amiens, received the Gospel from St Quintinus, first bishop of Amiens (A.D. 70; others, 250), Folcard, monk, CXLVII, 1182; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 290.

**AT AMMONICO**, Syonah, St Mark the Evangelist preached (A.D. 50), St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 79; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 644, 648; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 182.

**ANDRINOPOLIS** in Thrace was evangelized by St Thomas the Apostle (A.D. 38–40), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 158.

**IN ENGLAND**, the following preached: St Peter the Apostle (A.D. 58), Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVII, 458, 466, 468; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008.—Preachers sent by St Peter, Anastasius, CXXVII, 460; and by St Philip the Apostle (A.D. 63), William of Malmesbury, monk, CLXXIX, 1683.—Joseph of Arimathea, ibid.—Phaganus and Deruvianus, sent by Pope Eleutherius at the request of the king of the English (A.D. 167), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 30; Anastasius, CXXVII, 528, 1249; Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1310; William of Malmesbury, monk, CLXXIX, 1685; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 814.—Germanus, bishop of Auxerre, Lupus, bishop of Troyes, Patrick of Ireland, and Severus, bishop of Trier (A.D. 429–433), Hericus, monk of Auxerre, CXXIV, 1164; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 82, 83; William of Malmesbury, monk, CLXXIX, 1688; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, XCV, 826, 827.—St Augustine, apostle of the English, sent by St Gregory the Great with forty companions, among whom were Mellitus, Justus, Paulinus, Lawrence, and Rufianus or Rufinianus (A.D. 596–655), St Gregory the Great, LXXVII, 835, 841; St Augustine, apostle of the English, LXXX, 59, 79; St Boniface, bishop of Mainz, LXXXIX, 874; Bede the Venerable, XCV, 52, 55; Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVIII, 645, 1370; John the deacon of Venice, CXXXIX, 883; Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1332; Lanfranc, CL, 743, 764; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, [Col. 0555] 112; William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 968, 1441; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 841.—John, Deusdedit, and Candidus (A.D. 596–655), William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1443.—Aedan, or Aldan, bishop of Iona (A.D. 615–640), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 19, 24; Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1336; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 120; William of Malmesbury, monk, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 860; Helinand, monk, CCXII, 772.—St Aldhelm, bishop of Sherborne (A.D. 630), William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1533, 1619.—St Birinus, bishop of Dorchester and Winchester (A.D. 630), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 126; William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1523; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 861.—Angilbertus, bishop of Dorchester and Winchester (A.D. 634–656), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 126; William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1523; Helinand, CCXII, 782.—Earcombertus, king of the English (A.D. 640), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 121.—James the deacon (A.D. 640), Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 850.—St Livinus, Foilanus, Furseus, and Helius (A.D. 648), St Boniface, bishop of Mainz, LXXXIX, 879; Bede the Venerable, XCV, 145.—Oswald, king of the English (A.D. 650), ibid., 115.—Alcfridus, son of King Oswi (A.D. 653), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 150.—Oswius, king of the English (A.D. 655), Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1336; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 863.—Winfridus, bishop of the English (A.D. 656), Helinand, CCXII, 782.—Wilfridus, bishop of the English (A.D. 678), Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1338; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 866; William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1549.
