**IN SOUTHERN OR MERIDIONAL ENGLAND**, the following preached: St Nima the Briton, consecrated bishop at Rome of Candida Casa (A.D. 432), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 121; William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1577; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 860.—St Paulinus in the city of Melmin (A.D. 625), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 107; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 118; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 856.—St Columbanus, abbot, among the Picts (A.D. 600), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 121.—Totta, bishop of Leicester (A.D. 640), William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1605.

**IN MIDDLE ENGLAND** the following preached: Edbertus, bishop of Leicester (A.D. 630), William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1605.—Hedhedus, bishop of Dorchester, and Epelpine or Edelwine (A.D. 650), ibid.—Betti, Adda, and Diuma (A.D. 653), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 150; William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1603.—Alcfridus, son of King Oswi, with Bishop Finanus (A.D. 653), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 150; William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 863.

**IN WESTERN ENGLAND** the following preached: Birinus, apostle of the English, bishop of Winchester and Dorchester (A.D. 630–650), Henry of Huntingdon, archdeacon, CXCV, 861.—Angilbertus and Leutherius (A.D. 634), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 126.

**IN EASTERN ENGLAND**, heralds of the Gospel were St Mellitus, bishop of London (A.D. 604), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 113; Henry, CXCV, 850.—St Paulinus, Bede the Venerable, XCV, 107; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 118; Henry, CXCV, 856.—Felix, bishop of Lincoln (A.D. 634–646), Henry, ibid., 858.—Honorius, bishop of Canterbury, in Kent (A.D. 634), Bede, XCV, 108; Henry, CXCV, 857, 858.—Aeduinus, king of the Northumbrians (A.D. 640), Bede, XCV, 107.—St Furseus, Bede, XCV, 145.

**THE ANGLES OF MERCIA** were evangelized by Adda, Cella, and Diuma (A.D. 650–655), Bede, XCV, 150; William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1603.—King Oswius (A.D. 655), Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1336; Henry, CXCV, 863.—St Wilfridus of Selegia (A.D. 678), William, CLXXIX, 1549.—Putta of Hereford, first bishop, and Borel and Ostcar, first bishops of Worcester (A.D. 720–730), William, CLXXIX, 1587, 1599.

**THE ANGLO-SAXONS** were evangelized by Cedd the Scot, afterwards bishop of Lichfield, who restored the faith which had been lost (A.D. 654), Bede the Venerable, XCV, 151; William, CLXXIX, 1603. See **SAXONY**.

**ANSIACUM**, Aixe? a city near Limoges, received the faith of Christ from St Martial (A.D. 50), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 194.

**ANTARADUS**, a city of Phoenicia, was evangelized by St Peter (A.D. 38), Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVII, 456; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Hugh, abbot of Flavigny, CLIV, 25, 667; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116, 122; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674, 1701.

**ANTIOCH OF PISIDIA**, Ak-Cheher, was evangelized by SS. Paul and Barnabas (A.D. 50), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 115; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1691, 1694.

**AT ANTIOCH** in Syria, Antakieh, the disciples scattered after the persecution against St Stephen preached [Col. 0556] (A.D. 34), Haymo of Halberstadt, CXVIII, 825; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 109.—St Peter the Apostle (A.D. 38–40), Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVII, 456; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Hugh, abbot of Flavigny, CLIV, 25, 667; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116, 122; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674, 1701.—SS. Paul and Barnabas (A.D. 39), Freculf of Lisieux, CVI, 1125; Anastasius, CXXVII, 456, 458; Orderic Vitalis, 114, 120; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1679.—Lucius of Cyrene and Manahen (A.D. 44), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 114.—Evodius, disciple of St Peter (A.D. 44–60), St Prosper of Aquitaine, LI, 553; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 644; Ekkeard of Aura, CLIV, 667.—Simon, son of Cleophas (A.D. 100–107), Freculf, CVI, 1158. St Ignatius, bishop of Antioch (A.D. 100), ibid.

**AUXERRE**, a city of Gaul, was evangelized through Germanus, bishop of Auxerre (A.D. 429), Hericus, monk of Auxerre, CXXIV, 1164; Cosmas, dean of Prague, CLXVI, 82, 83.

**AT APAMIA**, Pamiers, a city of the province of Toulouse, Diego, bishop of Osma, Fulk, bishop of Toulouse, and Navarrus, bishop of Comminges, defended the true faith against the Albigensians (A.D. 1207), Peter the monk, CCXIII, 550, 554, 561.

**AQUAE SEXTIAE**, Aix in Provence, received the word of life through the preaching of St Maximinus with St Mary Magdalene (A.D. 34–48), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 141.

**AQUILEIA**, a city of Italy, was converted to Christ by St Mark the Evangelist, who there appointed Hermagoras bishop (A.D. 50), St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 78; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 181.

**AQUITAINE** was evangelized by SS. Euphrasius, Saturninus of Toulouse, Martial of Limoges, Stremonius, and others (A.D. 48–58), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175, 183; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493; Ademar, monk, CXLI, 87, 112; Jordanus, bishop of Limoges, CXLII, 1353.

**IN ARABIA**, Paul the Apostle, Silas, Timothy, and Barnabas sowed the faith (A.D. 34–38), Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639.

**THE ARDENNES** were taught the faith by St Beregisus, bishop of the Ardennes (at an uncertain date in the fourth century), Anonymous, CLIV, 1342.—St Hubertus (A.D. 700–727), ibid., 1344.

**AT ARLES**, a city of Gaul, Arles, St Trophimus, sent by St Peter the Apostle, preached (A.D. 58), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129.

**ARHUSIM**, a city of Denmark, was evangelized by Poppo, who converted King Harold to the faith (A.D. 966), Thietmar, bishop, CXXXIX, 1207, 1208; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 525 (n.); Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 191.—Christianus, bishop of Aarhus (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 616.

**ARIAN HERETICS IN CELTIBERIA, SCYTHIA, GAUL, AND SPAIN.** John, bishop of Constantinople, converted the Celtic and Scythian Arians to the true faith (A.D. 400), Aurelius Cassiodorus, LXIX, 1167.—St Avitus, bishop of Vienne, defended the faith in Gaul against the Arians (A.D. 490), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 93.—Leander, bishop of Seville, evangelized the Arians in Spain and brought King Reccared, an Arian, to the true faith (A.D. 587), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1335.—Reccared, king of the Arian Visigoths, converted to Christ the peoples subject to him in Spain (A.D. 589), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 493; John of Biclaro, LXXII, 869.—King Sisebut restored the Arian Goths to the true faith (A.D. 639), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 121.

**IN ARMENIA**, the following preached: St Bartholomew the Apostle (A.D. 34–48), Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 165.—James the Apostle, son of Alphaeus, who wrote his Catholic Epistle at the city of Nerito and died (A.D. 70), Freculf, CVI, 1135, 1147.—Edessius, bishop (A.D. 330), ibid., 1198.

**TO THE ARVERNI**, St Peter the Apostle sent Strimonius (A.D. 58), St Gregory of Tours, CXXI, 175, 183.

**IN ASIA**, the following preached: St Peter the Apostle (A.D. 33–40), Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVII, 456; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Hugh, abbot of Flavigny, CLIV, 25; Ekkeard of Aura, ibid., 667; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116, 122; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674, 1701.—St John, Apostle and Evangelist (A.D. 33–110), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88; Freculf, CVI, 1154; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 148; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1698.—St Paul the Apostle (A.D. 38–50), Anastasius, CXXVII, 460.—St Timothy (A.D. 60), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129.—Certain captive priests converted innumerable Asians to Christ (A.D. 330), Aurelius Cassiodorus, LXIX, 939.

**ASIA MINOR** was evangelized by St Peter the Apostle (A.D. 38–40), Freculf, CVI, 1135; Haymo of Halberstadt, [Col. 0557] CXVIII, 831; Anonymous, CLIV, 1116; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 122, 124; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1679, 1696.—St Philip the Apostle (A.D. 40), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 156; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1698.—St John, Apostle and Evangelist, with St Philip and James the Greater (A.D. 38–50), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 148.—St Paul the Apostle (A.D. 53), Anastasius, CXXVII, 464.—Aquila, Prisca, and Priscilia with Paul (A.D. 50–53), CVI, 1130; Haymo, CXVIII, 829.—Archippus and Timothy (A.D. 60–100), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129.—St Ignatius, bishop of the Church of Antioch (A.D. 100), Freculf, CVI, 1158.

**ASSYRIA** was evangelized through Bartholomew (A.D. 38), Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 165.

**AT ASTIGI**, Écija, a city of Baetica in Spain, St Crispinus, bishop of Astigi, preached (A.D. 66), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 198.

**ASTURIAS**, a province of Spain, was evangelized by St Ephrem, disciple of St James (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129, 130.

**AT ATHENS**, SS. Paul and Timothy preached (A.D. 53), Haymo, CXVIII, 116, 124, 827; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1701.—St Barnabas (A.D. 53).—St Dionysius the Areopagite and first bishop of the Athenians (A.D. 53), Ekkeard of Aura, CLIV, 679; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116, 124, 129; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1701.—St Quadratus (A.D. 120), St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 82.

**ATTALIA**, Satalieh, a city of Pamphylia, was evangelized by SS. Paul and Barnabas (A.D. 50), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 115; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1694.

**ARRAS** received the faith from St Vedastus (A.D. 495), Alcuin, CI, 670, 672, 678.

**AUGUSTA VEROMANDUORUM** in Gaul, St-Quentin, was evangelized through St Quintinus, bishop of Amiens (A.D. 280), Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1496.

**AUGUSTODUNUM**, Autun, a city of Gaul, was evangelized by SS. Thyrsus, Andochius, and Benignus, sent by St Polycarp (A.D. 195), John the monk, CLXII, 756.

**THE AVARS** were converted to Christ by St Paulinus of Aquileia (A.D. 790–804), St Paulinus of Aquileia, XCIX, 69, 70; Alcuin, C, 190, 192. Rudum, king of the Avars, embraced the faith with his people (A.D. 792–796), St Ado, archbishop of Vienne, 123; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 62; Sigebert of Gembloux, CXL, 152.

**AT AVIGNON**, a city of Gaul, St Martha, Christ’s hostess, preached with St Marcella and Parmena (A.D. 35), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1495.

**AZOTUS**, a city of the Palestinian Pentapolis, was evangelized through St Philip the deacon (A.D. 35), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 107.

## B
BABYLON, the royal city of Persia, was evangelized by Saints Simon Jude and Jude [son] of James (A.D. 40–70), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 172, 176.—Abdias, first bishop of Babylon (A.D. 60–100), ibid., 175.

BACTRIANA, Balkh: Saint Thomas preached there (A.D. 33–53), Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 157.

BAJOUARIA, also BAGOARIA and BAWARIA, Bavaria, was evangelized by Saint Emmeram, first apostle of Bavaria (A.D. 648?), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 465.—Saint Boniface, bishop of Mainz and apostle of Germany (A.D. 716), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 624, 648.—Saint Erimbert, bishop of Freising; Gowibald, bishop of Regensburg; and John of Salzburg (A.D. 730–755), ibid., LXXXIX, 649.—Wivilius, or Vivalus, of Passau, ibid., 649, 806.—Ludo and Wiggo, Rudellus and Fulradus (A.D. 740–755), ibid., 648; Ekkehard of Aura, CLIV, 837.

BARBARANA, or WARBARANA, Warburg: Witta, called Wisa or Wetanus, preached there (A.D. 730–742), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 749.

BARCELONA, a city in Catalonia, was evangelized by Etherius, bishop of Barcelona (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129, 130.—Philip of Milan (A.D. 91), ibid., XXXI, 261, 263.

In BELGIUM preached Saint Valerius the confessor, Eucharius bishop of Trier, and Saint Maternus, sent into Gaul by Saint Peter (A.D. 50; others say 250), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493; Heriger of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1010; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1118, 1125.—Saint Antony, bishop of Meaux, and Sanctinus (A.D. 70–97), ibid., CLIV, 29.

BEAUVAIS was evangelized by Lucian (A.D. 300), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 390.

[Col. 0558] BEIRUT: in this Phoenician city Saint Peter the apostle preached (A.D. 38–40), Anastasius, CXXVII, 456; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25; Ekkehard of Aura, ibid., 667; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116, 122; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674, 1701.

The BERNICIANS, peoples of southern England, were evangelized by Nima, or Ninian (A.D. 394–432), Bede, XCV, 121; William of Malmesbury, monk, CLXXIX, 157; Henry, archdeacon of Huntingdon, CXCV, 860.—By Saint Paulinus, bishop of York and Rochester (A.D. 625), Bede, XCV, 107; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 118; Henry, archdeacon of Huntingdon, CXCV, 856.

BEREA, a city of Syria, was evangelized by Saints Paul, Barnabas, and Timothy (A.D. 50–58), Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1701.

BILBILIS, Baubola? in Tarraconensian Spain, was evangelized by Saint Paternus, bishop of Toledo (A.D. 94), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 265.

In BIRKA, a city of Sweden, preached Saint Ansgar, bishop of Hamburg (A.D. 826), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 499.—Herigarius (A.D. 840), ibid., 478, 479.—Rimbert, a Danish priest (A.D. 854), Saint Ansgar of Hamburg, 997; (A.D. 860), 999.—Unni, bishop of Hamburg (A.D. 915), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 499.—John, first an abbot and then the first bishop of Birka (A.D. 1025), ibid., 617, 636.—Adalwald the Younger, bishop of the Goths (A.D. 1070), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 645, 646.

BESANÇON was evangelized by Ferontius (A.D. 48), CXII, 1493.

BITHYNIA in Asia Minor was evangelized by Saint Peter the apostle (A.D. 38–40), Freculf, CVI, 1135; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anonymous, CLIV, 1116; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 122, 124; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1679, 1696.—Saints Paul, Luke, Timothy, and Barnabas (A.D. 50–55), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1698.

BITURICA, Bourges, was evangelized by Saint Austregisilus, sent by Saint Peter (A.D. 48–60), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1498.

In BLASCONIA, in the Orkney Islands, Thuralfus, bishop of Blasconia, and Meinhard proclaimed Christ (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 653.

Methodius evangelized the BOHEMIANS and converted Borvoy, king of the Bohemians, to Christ (A.D. 885), Cosmas, dean of Prague, CLXVI, 71, 81.—Dithmar, bishop of Prague, preached among the Bohemians, ibid., 90–91.

BÆTICA, in southern Spain, was evangelized by Tesiphorus, bishop of Vergilitanum, ordained at Rome (A.D. 41), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 175.—The bishops Caecilius, Iscius, Secundus, and Sexifirmus (A.D. 44–70), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 151, 163, 175.—Saint Crispinus, bishop of Astigi, ibid., 198.

BOULOGNE, in Gaul, received the faith from Saint Audomar, bishop of Thérouanne (A.D. 630), Folcard, abbot, CXLVII, 1182, 1190.

BRABANT, in Flanders, was evangelized by Saint Amandus, bishop of Trier and Tongeren (A.D. 645), CXXXIX, 1112.

At BRAGA in Spain preached Saint Peter, first bishop of Braga (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 109.—Saint Basil, second bishop of Braga (A.D. 60–65), ibid., 109.

BRIGANTIUM, a city of Celtiberia in Spain, received the faith (A.D. 86), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 252.

In BRITAIN preached Saint James the apostle, called the Greater (A.D. 41), ibid., XXXI, 135.—Saint Columba, teacher of the Britons (A.D. 565), Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1329.

At BREMEN in Germany Christ was proclaimed by Saint Willehad, first bishop of Bremen (A.D. 754), Ansgar, bishop of Hamburg, CXVIII, 1015; Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 465, 471.—Saint Willeric (A.D. 789–838), ibid., CXLVI, 471.—Saint Gerwald (A.D. 780), Saint Ansgar, CXVIII, 1017.—Saint Ansgar, or Ansgarius, bishop of Hamburg and Bremen (A.D. 826), ibid., CXVIII, 966.

BRUTTIUM in Italy was evangelized by Saint Adalbert, bishop of Prague, who also suffered martyrdom there (A.D. 1015), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 201.

BULGARIA. Pope Nicholas I and King Louis the German sent apostles into Bulgaria (A.D. 858), Anastasius, CXXVIII, 1374.—Dominic, bishop of Trier; Donatus, bishop of Ostia; Grimart, bishop of Polymartium; Leo, priest of the Holy Roman Church; Marinus, deacon of the Holy Apostolic See; and Paul, bishop of Populonium, sent by Pope Nicholas I and King Louis, converted many Bulgarians to Christ (A.D. 858–866), Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVIII, 1371, 1374, 1375; Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1350.

BORDEAUX, a city of Aquitaine, was evangelized by Saint Eutropius, sent by blessed Peter (A.D. 48), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493.

## C

CHÂLONS-SUR-SAÔNE, a city of Gaul, was evangelized by Saint Marcellus (A.D. 180), Baldric, archbishop of Dol, CLXVI, 1210.

CAECILIA CASTRA, Cazères, in Lusitania of Spain, was converted to Christ by Saint Jonas (A.D. 86–130), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 254.

At CAESARAUGUSTA in Celtiberia, a city of Spain, Saragossa, preached Saint Athanasius, first bishop of Saragossa (A.D. 37–70), XXXI, 128, 167.—Philip of Milan (A.D. 91), ibid., 261, 263.

CAESAREA, Kaisarieh, a city of Cappadocia, was evangelized by Saint Peter the apostle (A.D. 38–40), Freculf, CVI, 1135; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anonymous, CLIV, 1116; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 122, 123; Peter Comestor, CXVIII, 1679, 1696.—Saint Ananias preached in Caesarea and strengthened Paul in faith and in the grace of baptism (A.D. 34–38), Adam Scot, CXCVIII, 107.

In CAESAREA, a city of Palestine, Saint Peter the apostle preached and baptized Cornelius the centurion with his entire household (A.D. 34–40), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 134; Freculf, CVI, 1125; Haymo, CXVIII, 826; Anastasius, CXXVII, 456; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 109, 120; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674.

In CALAMINA, a city of India, Saint Thomas the apostle, who is also called Didymus, preached and was crowned with martyrdom (A.D. 53–70), Freculf, CVI, 1147.

CAMBRAI was evangelized by Saint Vedastus (A.D. 490), author uncertain, CXLIX, 26, 28.—Halitgarius of Cambrai (A.D. 830), Adam of Bremen, Canon, CXLVI, 474.

At CANDIDA CASA, a city of the Bernicians in England, Christ was proclaimed by Saint Nima, or Ninian, a Briton and bishop of Candida Casa (A.D. 394–432), Venerable Bede, XCV, 121; William, CLXXIX, 1577; Henry, archdeacon of Huntingdon, CXCV, 860.—Pethelmus, apostle of the West Saxons (A.D. 725), William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1577.

In KENT, a province of England, the heralds of the divine word were Saint Augustine, apostle of the English, who baptized King Ethelbert (A.D. 598), Venerable Bede, XCV, 55; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 112; Henry, archdeacon, CXCV, 842, 848.—Paulinus, Honorius, Mellitus, John, and others (A.D. 596–650), Venerable Bede, XCV, 85; Lanfranc, CL, 743, 764; William, CLXXIX, 1443; Henry, archdeacon, CXCV, 851, 852.

CAPPADOCIA, a province of Asia Minor, was evangelized by Saint Peter (A.D. 38–44), Freculf, CVI, 1135; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anonymous, CLIV, 1116; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 122, 124; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1679, 1696.

At CARCASSONNE, in the territory of Toulouse, Diego, bishop of Osma, and Guy—first abbot of Vaux-de-Cernay, then bishop of Carcassonne—preached against the Albigensian heresy (A.D. 1207), Peter the Monk, CCXIII, 550, 551, 555.

The CARANTANIANS, peoples of Bavaria, were evangelized by Arno, bishop of Salzburg; Paulinus, patriarch of Aquileia; and Virgil of Salzburg (A.D. 784–800), Saint Paulinus of Aquileia, XCIX, 70; Alcuin, C, 190, 192.

At CARMAN, a fortress in the province of Narbonne, Diego, bishop of Osma, with Peter and Ralph, Cistercian monks, preached against the Albigensians (A.D. 1206), Peter the Monk, CCXIII, 549, 555.

CHARTRES in Gaul was evangelized by Solemnis, bishop of Chartres (A.D. 490), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 93.

CARPENTRAS, in Narbonese Gaul, received the faith of Christ through the preaching of Saint Andeolus, bishop of Carpentras (A.D. 200), John the Monk, CLXII, 756.

CARPETANIA was evangelized by Saint Calocerus, a disciple of Saint James (A.D. 44–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 155.—Saint Athanasius, first bishop of Saragossa, and Saint Theodore (A.D. 52), ibid., 167.

CARTHAGO SPARTARIA, Cartagena, a city of Spain, received the word of God through the preaching of Saint Basil, bishop of Carthago Spartaria (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 128.—Saint Indalecius (A.D. 45), ibid., 169.

CARTHEIA, near the strait in Bætica, Algeciras, was evangelized by Iscius, sent by Saint Peter (A.D. 53), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 167.

The fortress of DIJON in Gaul was converted to the faith of Christ by Saint Benignus, sent into Gaul by Saint Polycarp to preach with Saints Andochius [Col. 0560] and Thyrsus (A.D. 110), John the Monk, CXLII, 757.

A fortress near Turgium in Spain, Castro, was evangelized by Saint Secundus (A.D. 100), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 275.

CHÂLONS, a city of Gaul, received the word of life from Saint Memmius Mantius (A.D. 48–60), Abbot Hugh of Flavigny, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1117, 1119.

CATALONIA, a region of Spain, was evangelized by Saint Etherius, bishop of Barcelona (A.D. 37–61), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129, 130.—Philip of Milan (A.D. 91), ibid., 261, 263.

CATARACTA DECRORUM, a city in England, was evangelized by Saint Paulinus (A.D. 600), Bede, XCV, 107; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 118; Henry, archdeacon, CXCV, 856.

At CELLES, a city of Gaul, Gislenus preached (A.D. 651), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 123.

CELTIBERIA, a province of Spain, was evangelized by Saint Athanasius, bishop of Saragossa (A.D. 37–70), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 128, 167.—Saint Philip (A.D. 91), ibid., 261.

John, bishop of Constantinople, converted the Arian CELTIC peoples of Thrace to the true faith (A.D. 400), Aurelius Cassiodorus, LXIX, 1167, 1168.

Near CENTULA, a city of Aquitaine, preached Saint Columbanus (A.D. 620), Hariulf, abbot, CLXXIV, 1220.—Madelgisilus (A.D. 650), ibid., 1443.

Near CERSONA in Lycia, Pope Saint Clement, an exile, preached and converted many peoples to Christ (A.D. 69–88), Freculf, CVI, 1156.

Two monks of uncertain name, coming from Bohemia, converted the CHIZZINI, a people of Sweden, to the faith under King Gotescalco (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 373, 574.

At CIBHRINSTRI in Saxony, Benjamin, companion and fellow-worker of Saint Willehad, preached in Cibhrinstri of Saxony and received the crown of martyrdom (A.D. 780), Saint Ansgar, bishop of Hamburg, CXVIII, 1018.

CILICIA, a region of Asia Minor, was evangelized by Saint Paul the apostle with Silas, Timothy, and Barnabas (A.D. 48–58), Freculf, CVI, 1130; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anastasius, CXXVII, 464; Heriger of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 115, 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1697.

The CIRCIPANI, a people of Sweden, received the faith from two monks of uncertain name (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 573.

At COLOGNE, a city of Germany, preached Saints Valerius the confessor, Eucharius bishop of Trier, and Maternus bishop of Tongeren (A.D. 50–80), Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1010, 1013; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1118, 1125.—Hildibald, bishop of Cologne (A.D. 780), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 471.

COLOSSAE, a city of Phrygia, was evangelized by Epaphras, a disciple of Saint Paul (A.D. 60–100), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129.—Saint Paul the apostle, preaching at Rome, wrote the Epistle to the Colossians (A.D. 68), Anastasius, CXXVII, 468.

COMPOSTELA. Saint James the apostle, called the Greater, son of Zebedee and brother of Saint John, preached throughout all Spain, and especially at Compostela (A.D. 37), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 109; Freculf, CVI, 1147; Munio of Mondoñedo, CLXX, 875.

At CONSORANNE in Gascony, Navarrus, bishop of Conserans, preached against the Albigensians (A.D. 1207), Peter the Monk, CCXIII, 554, 561.

At CONSTANTIA in Gaul, Saint Paternus of Toledo, first bishop of Toledo and then bishop of Constance, preached in Gaul (A.D. 76–100), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 311.

CORINTH, a city of the Peloponnese, was evangelized by Saint Paul the apostle, Silas, and Timothy (A.D. 48–50), CXXVII, 464; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 124; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1703.—Saint Dionysius the Areopagite, converted by Saint Paul, Freculf, CVI, 1166; Haymo, CXVIII, 830; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116, 124.—Apollos (A.D. 56), Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1705.—Sosthenes, disciple of Saint Paul the apostle (A.D. 60–100), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129.

In CRETE, Candia, an island of the Mediterranean Sea, preached Saint Titus, disciple of Saint Paul (A.D. 58), Freculf, CVI, 1149; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129.—Flegunta, Herman, and Patrobas (A.D. 68–100), Freculf, CVI, 1149.

CRIDIA, a city of West Saxony. Edilfrid, bishop of Cridia, preached in West Saxony (A.D. 850), William, CLXXIX, 1547.

CYPRUS, an island of the Mediterranean Sea, was evangelized by disciples dispersed in the persecution against Saint Stephen [Col. 0561] (A.D. 35), Haymo, CXVIII, 825; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 109.—Saint John the apostle (A.D. 80), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116.—Saint Paul the apostle with Saint Barnabas (A.D. 50–58), Anastasius, CXXVII, 460; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 114, 116.—Saint Lazarus, brother of Saint Mary Magdalene (A.D. 34–38), Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 638, 646.—Saint Mark the Evangelist (A.D. 50–100), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116.

Near CYRENE, a city of the Pentapolis, Saint Mark the Evangelist preached (A.D. 50), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 182.

## D

DALBOIA, a city of Scania. Eginon, bishop of Dalboia, preached in Scania (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 617, 627.

DAMASCUS, a city of Syria. Saint Paul was converted on the road to Damascus (A.D. 34), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 131; Anastasius, CXXVII, 454; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 17; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639; Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1304.—Near Damascus Saint Paul preached (A.D. 34–38), Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 107; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1697.

In DENMARK preached Saint Willibrord, first apostle of the Frisians (A.D. 690–700), Alcuin, CI, 699.—Saint Boniface of Mainz (A.D. 716–745), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 624, 641.—Herold, king of the Danes, who, converted to Christ, led his people to the faith (A.D. 825), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 158; Bernold, abbot, CXLVIII, 1347; Haymo, 966, 971.—Ansgar, or Ansgarius, bishop of Hamburg (A.D. 840), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 476, 480, 483; Honorius of Autun, CLXXII, 190.—Ebbo, bishop of Reims, and Halitgarius (A.D. 830–856), Saint Ansgar, CXVIII, 971; Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 474, 475.—The monks Gauzbertus and Witmarus (A.D. 830), Saint Ansgar, CXVIII, 971.—Harald, bishop of Schleswig; Gislemar; and Rimbert (A.D. 840–850), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 475, 486; Saint Ansgar, CXVIII, 971, 999.—Unni, bishop of Hamburg (A.D. 903–936), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 498.—Henry I, emperor of the Germans, who recalled the Danes with their king Cnut from their former error and brought them to the faith (A.D. 93 [probably 933]), Thietmar, bishop of Merseburg, CXXXIX, 1193.—Poppo of Aarhus (A.D. 966), ibid., 1207, 1208; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, [note], 525; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 191.—Poppo the Younger, bishop of Schleswig (A.D. 1010–1015), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 525, 526.—Heribert, bishop of Viborg; Eilbert, bishop; Christian and Sewerd; Radolph and Ratolph, bishops of Schleswig (A.D. 1036–1059–1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 616, 650.

CISMARINE DENMARK, or Jutland, was evangelized by Regimbrond, bishop of Harusam (A.D. 948), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 503.—Poppo, bishop of Schleswig, with Odinkar the Younger (A.D. 1010–1015), ibid., 526, 535. (See Jutland.)

The DETROS, a people of England, were instructed in the faith of Christ by Paulinus, bishop of York, with Saint Augustine, apostle of the English (A.D. 615), Bede, XCV, 107; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 118; Henry, CXCV, 856.

DERBY, or DERBE, a city of Isauria in Asia, was evangelized by Saint Paul the apostle with Silas and Timothy (A.D. 50–58), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1692, 1698.—Saint Barnabas (A.D. 50), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 178.—Silas, disciple of Saint Paul (A.D. 50), ibid., 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1692.

The fortress of DIJON in Gaul: see CASTRUM, etc.

DOKKUM, a city of Frisia, was brought to Christ by Saint Willehad, first bishop of Bremen (A.D. 754), CXVIII, 1015, 1016.

At DORCHESTER, a city of West Saxony, preached Birinus, bishop of Winchester and Dorchester, who converted King Kinegit (A.D. 630), Bede, XCV, 126; William, CLXXIX, 1523.—Angilbert, bishop of Dorchester, successor of Saint Birinus (A.D. 634), Bede, XCV, 126.—Leutherius, ibid., 634.—Hedhedus and Epelpine, or Edelwine, bishops of Dorchester (A.D. 650–651), William, CLXXIX, 1605.

DOROVERNIA, DUROVERNUM, Canterbury, royal city of the kingdom of the Kentish people. Ethelred, king of Kent, received Augustine and his companions, sent into England to preach, and granted them authority and permission to preach (A.D. 596), Henry, archdeacon of Huntingdon, CXCV, 848.—Saint Augustine, apostle of the English, with Saints Justus, Mellitus, Laurence, John, Paulinus, Honorius, Ruffianus, and others, first preached at Dorovernia (A.D. 596–645), Saint Augustine, apostle of the English, LXXX, 59, 79; Lanfranc, [Col. 0562] CL, 743, 764; William, CLXXIX, 968, 1441; Henry, CXV, 814, 857, 858.

At DORUBREVI, in the city of Rochester, Augustine ordained Justus bishop (A.D. 600), Henry, CXCV, 850.

DUMNOCA, a city of East Anglia, heard the preaching of Felix, bishop of Lincoln (A.D. 636), Bede, XCV, 108.

## E

At ÉVREUX, a city of Neustria, Saint Taurinus, disciple of Saint Dionysius, first occupied the episcopal see of the Eburovices (A.D. 90–119), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 386–390.

At YORK, a city of the Northumbrians, preached Saint Paulinus, bishop of York (A.D. 600–628), Saint Bernold, CXLVIII, 1334; Lanfranc, CL, 743; William, CLXXIX, 1509, 1553.—James, disciple of Saint Paulinus (A.D. 640), Henry, CXCV, 859.

EBORA, or ELBORA, Évora, a city in Lusitania of Spain, had Saint Memmius Mantius, herald of the divine word, as its bishop (A.D. 90), XXXI, 255.

EDESSA, a city of Mesopotamia, Orfa, was evangelized by Saint Simon Jude the apostle, who converted King Abgar to Christ (A.D. 36), Freculf, CVI, 1123; Haymo, CXVIII, 824.

EICHSTÄTT, a city of Germany, was evangelized by Saint Willibald, companion and fellow-worker of Saint Boniface of Mainz (A.D. 736–747), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 646, 806; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1342.

At ELEGIA, a city of Alsace, preached Eucharius, Valerius, and Maternus (A.D. 50), Anonymous, CLIV, 1117.

ELVIRA in Spain, Granada, was evangelized by Caecilius, bishop of Elvira and disciple of Saint James (A.D. 43–54), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 151–173.

ELIOTROCA, Valladolid? a city of Spain, had as herald of the Gospel Indalecius, sent into Spain by Saint Peter (A.D. 45), XXXI, 169.

ELNONA, a city of Gaul, was evangelized by Saint Amandus, bishop of Trier (A.D. 614), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 115.

Near EPHESUS, Ara-Solouk, a city of Ionia, preached Saints John and James the Greater (A.D. 38–50), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 135; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 149.—Saint Paul with Timothy, Silas, Prisca, and Aquila (A.D. 48–58), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 125; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1704.—Timothy (A.D. 68), CVI, 1149.—Saint Paul, who there wrote his First Epistle to the Corinthians (A.D. 56), Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1705.—Onesimus, disciple of Saint Paul (A.D. 60–100), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129.—At Ephesus Saint John the apostle wrote his Gospel (A.D. 99), Ekkehard of Aura, CLIV, 679.

ETSERA, a city of the East Saxons, was evangelized by Saint Mellitus, who converted King Sigebert to Christ (A.D. 604), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 113; Henry, CXCV, 850.

EUROPE. Christians dispersed in the persecution against Saint Stephen carried the faith into Europe (A.D. 35), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 95, 97.

## F

FARRIA, an island of Denmark, was evangelized by Eilbert, first a monk and then a bishop (A.D. 1059), Adam of Bremen, Canon, CXLVI, 616.

FIURNA, or Funen, an island of Denmark, had as heralds of the divine word Liofdag, first bishop of Ribe (A.D. 948), Adam of Bremen, Canon, 503, 518, 821.—Haredus, or Horit, bishop of Schleswig (A.D. 948), ibid., 503.—Behinerus, first bishop in Funen (A.D. 1040), Adam of Bremen, Canon, CXLVI, 623.—Eilbert (A.D. 1059), ibid., 616.

FLANDERS was evangelized by Saint Amandus, bishop of Trier and Tongeren (A.D. 628), Milo the monk, CXXI, 945; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1040; Philip of Harveng, abbot, CCIII, 1248; Helinand, abbot, CCXII, 785.—Saint Livinus and his disciples Foillan, Fursey, and Ultan (A.D. 648), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 882; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 122.—Elias and Kilian of Mainz (A.D. 648), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 880.—Ursmar, bishop of Flanders (A.D. 690), Hariulf, CLXXIV, 1461 (appendix).—Saint Arnulf, bishop of Soissons (A.D. 1056–1085), ibid., 1411–1464.

The FRANKS were evangelized by Saint Solemnis, bishop of Chartres (A.D. 490), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 93.—Saint Clotildis, queen of the Franks, with Saint Vedastus and Saint Remigius (A.D. 496), Saint Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 152; Anonymous, XCVI, 1433; Hincmar, CXXV, 1157; Albert of Micy, [Col. 0563] CXXXIX, 598.—Saint Vedastus (A.D. 496), Alcuin, CI, 670, 672, 678; Anonymous, CXLIX, 28.—Saint Remigius (A.D. 496), Saint Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 152; Saint Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 97; Hincmar, CXXV, 1157; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1329; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 79.—Clovis, with his people, received the faith (A.D. 496), Saint Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 225; Flodoard, canon of Reims, CXXXV, 50; Rorico the monk, CXXXIX, 601, 653; Anonymous, CXLIX, 26; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 110; Ekkehard, ibid., 716; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 95; Hugh of Saint Mary, CLXIII, 913.

In FRANCIA, or Franconia, heralds of the divine word were Kilian, first in Franconia (date uncertain: seventh or eighth century), Adam of Bremen, bishop, CXLVI, 465.—Willibrord (A.D. 690), Alcuin, CI, 697, 701.

FRISIA was evangelized by Wilfrid, bishop of the English, who converted Adalgisus, king of the Frisians (A.D. 680), William, CLXXIX, 1559.—Saint Willibrord (A.D. 692–700), Bede, XCV, 243; Alcuin, CI, 698, 699; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1339; John the Monk, CLXII, 786; Helinand, CCXII, 805.—Acca the priest; Adalbert the deacon; Lebuinus, son of the king of the Deirans; Marcellinus; Saint Swibert; Werenfrid; Ewald the White and his brother Ewald the Black; and twelve other companions of Saint Willibrord (A.D. 692–700), Bede, XCV, 243, 244, 245.—Saint Boniface of Mainz, apostle of the Germans (A.D. 716–745), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 609, 611, 624, 641; Saint Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 123; Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 465; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 761; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 135, 158.—Wulfram, bishop of Sens (A.D. 718), Helinand, CCXII, 812.—Skirbal the deacon; Walther the priest; Megengaudus, Lullus, Sturmius, Waccar, and Tatuinus; and other companions, disciples, and fellow-workers of Saint Boniface (A.D. 730–750), LXXXIX, 646, 647, 653, 660, 805.—Willehad, first bishop of Bremen (A.D. 754), Saint Ansgar, bishop, CXVIII, 1015, 1016; Adam of Bremen, bishop, CXLVI, 465, 469, 471.—Eabonus, bishop of Ahretat; Hadalfrid, or Hudolf, a monk; Hamung, a priest; Kundekar, a monk; Williheri, a monk; Wintrung, a priest; and other disciples of Saint Boniface of Mainz (A.D. 755), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 660, 667, 805.—Liudger, bishop of Münster (A.D. 780), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 467, 468.—Hildibald, bishop of Cologne (A.D. 780), Adam of Bremen, 47.—Ansgar of Hamburg (A.D. 836), ibid., 433.

Citerior FRISIA was evangelized by one of the twelve companions of Saint Willibrord (A.D. 692), Bede, XCV, 245.

FREISING, in Bavaria, received the Gospel from Erimbert, bishop of Freising (A.D. 730), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 649, 741.

## G

In GALATIA, a region of Asia Minor, heralds of the divine word were Saint Peter the apostle (A.D. 38–40), Freculf, CVI, 1135; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anonymous, CLIV, 1116; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 122, 124; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1679, 1696.—Saint Philip the apostle (A.D. 38–60), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 156; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1698.—Saint Paul the apostle with Silas and Barnabas (A.D. 38–58), Freculf, CVI, 1130; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anastasius the Librarian, CXXVII, 464, 468; Heriger of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 115, 116.—Saint Timothy (A.D. 50–58), ibid., 116.

In GALICIA, a province of Spain, seven disciples of Saint James, bishop of Jerusalem, proclaimed Christ (A.D. 44), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 113.—Saint Andeolus preached in Galicia (A.D. 208), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 358.

GAUL was evangelized by Saint Peter the apostle (A.D. 48–50), Anastasius, CXXVII, 458, 466, 468; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1117.—Saint Philip the apostle (A.D. 38), XXXI, 87, 88; Freculf, CVI, 1146; William, CLXXIX, 1683; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 156; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1698.—Saint James the apostle called the Greater (A.D. 41), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 135.—Saint Paul the apostle (A.D. 58–69), Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 128.—Ferontius, Austregisilus, Saint Eutropius, Irenaeus of Lyons, Lazarus, Maximinus, Joseph of Arimathea, Mary Magdalene, Martha, Marcella, Parmenas, and Valerius (A.D. 48–80), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 156, 158; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493, 1495, 1497; Saint Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1496; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1010; Hugh of Flavigny, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1116, 1118, 1124; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 141; Anonymous, CLXII, 755; William [Col. 0564] of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1683.—Saint Dionysius the Areopagite (A.D. 50), Saint Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175, 183; Othlonus, CXLVI, 387; Folcard the monk, CXLVII, 1182; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 26; Ekkehard of Aura, ibid., 679.—Clement, Eucharius, Frontinus, Mansuetus, Maternus, Sabinus, Potentianus, Saturninus, Saint Sixtus, Stremonius, Sinicius, and Martial, sent by Saint Peter (A.D. 48–50–58), Saint Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175, 183; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493, 1494, 1505; Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1496; Heriger of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1010, 1013; Ademar the monk, CXLI, 87; Jordan, bishop of Limoges, CXLII, 1353; Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1117, 1118, 1124; Flodoard, canon of Reims, CXXXV, 32; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129, 193, 286.—Crescens (A.D. 59), Saint Ado, bishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 79.—Quirinus, Nicasius, and Scuvilus, sent by Saint Dionysius (A.D. 70), Folcard, CXLVII, 1182; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 386, 388, 390.—Saint Coelestis, disciple of Saint Clement, and Secundus, bishop of Metz (A.D. 70), Anonymous, CLXIII, 581.—Austriclianus and Alpinianus (A.D. 70–72), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 186, 193.—Saint Paternus, bishop of Toledo and Constance (A.D. 130), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 311.—Mello and Taurinus (A.D. 119), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 386.—Saints Benignus, Andochius, and Thyrsus, sent by Saint Polycarp (A.D. 140), Saint Varnaharius, priest, LXXX, 187; Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 756; John the Monk, CLXII, 756, 757.—Saint Photinus, Valerianus, Marcellus, and Zacharias of Lyons (A.D. 166–195), Abbot Hugh, CLIV, 96; Baldric, CLXVI, 1209, 1210; John the Monk, CLXII, 756.—Saints Crispinus and Crispinianus, Fuscianus, Rufinus, Victoricus, Mallonus, Lucianus, and Avicianus (A.D. 250–300), Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1494, 1496; Folcard, CXLVII, 1182; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 390.—Saint Avitus of Vienne (A.D. 490), Ekkehard of Aura, CLIV, 778.—Saints Solemnis, Vedastus, Remigius, and Queen Clotildis (A.D. 490–500), Saint Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 152; Alcuin, CI, 670, 672, 678; Saint Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 97; Hincmar, CXXV, 1157; Rorico of Moissac, CXXXI, 598; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1329; Lambert of Arras, CXLIX, 26, 28.—Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 79.—Saints Amandus and Landoaldus (A.D. 614), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 115, 120.—Saints Ultan, Foillan, and Fursey (A.D. 640), ibid., 122.—Saints Eloquius, Etto, and Bertuinus, Scots (A.D. 651), ibid., 123.—Gislenus, Landelinus, Trudo, and Vincentius, who is also called Madelgarius (A.D. 651), ibid., 123.

GHENT, a city of Flanders, was evangelized by Saint Amandus, bishop of Trier and Tongeren (A.D. 628), CXXI, 945; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1040; Philip of Harveng, CCIII, 1248; CCXII, 785.—Saint Livinus with Frilan, Elias, and Kilian (A.D. 648), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 880, 882; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 122.

The GARUMNI, peoples of Aquitaine along the Garonne, had as herald of the divine word Saint Martial, bishop of Limoges (A.D. 70), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 193.—Austriclianus and Alpinianus (A.D. 73), ibid., 193.

GENTES [THE GENTILES]. Cypriot and Cyrenian men, dispersed after the martyrdom of Saint Stephen, preached in various regions to Greeks and Gentiles (A.D. 35), CXXVII, 456.—Paul and Barnabas were set apart for preaching among the Gentiles, Haymo, CXVIII, 825; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 17; Abbot Hugh of Flavigny, CLIV, 24.—They went among the Gentiles in order to preach, Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1692.

GERDANIA, a city of Denmark, was evangelized by Saint Gaudentius (A.D. 990), Saint Matilda, CLI, 1341.

In GERMANY, a region of Europe, heralds of the divine word were Saint Valerius the confessor (A.D. 48–60), Anonymous, CLIV, 1124.—Saint Willibrord, apostle of the Frisians, with Saint Boniface (A.D. 717–723), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 642.—Saint Boniface, bishop of Mainz and apostle of the Germans (A.D. 717–745), ibid., 641; Anastasius, CXXVIII, 975; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1341; Helinand the monk, CCXII, 812.—Adalheri, Burchard, Derso, Grimbert, Skirbalt, Walther, Swibert, Witta, Lullus, Winnibald, Willibald, Gregory of Utrecht, and Geppan, companions and fellow-workers of Saint Boniface (A.D. 717–730–736), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 646, 653, 660, 684, 741, 749, 757, 806; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1342.—Sturmius; Waccar, monk; Abel, bishop; Warbert, bishop; and Wera, bishop (A.D. 740–745), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 647, 660, 741, 757, 805.—Tatuisius and Fulrad, archchaplain (A.D. 750), Saint Boniface, LXXXIX, 741; Ekkehard of Aura, CLIV, 837.

GLASTONBURY, an island of England, was evangelized by Joseph of Arimathea, sent from Gaul into England by Saint Philip with eleven companions (A.D. 63), William, CLXXIX, 1683.—Saint Patrick the Irishman, against the Pelagians (A.D. 433), William, CLXXIX, 1688, 1689.

[Col. 0565] In GOTHIA, a region of Scandinavia, preached Turgot, first bishop of Skara in West Gothland (A.D. 1013), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 541, 640.—Radulf, or Radolf (A.D. 1026), ibid., 541.—Grimkil and Bernard (A.D. 1030–1059), ibid., 541, 650.—Olaph, king of the Northmen (A.D. 1040), ibid., CXLVI, 540.—Simon, also called Stemphi, bishop of Hälsingland (A.D. 1060), ibid., 617, 641.—Adalwaldus the Elder and Adawaldus the Younger (A.D. 1060–1070), ibid., 617, 640.

GOTHLAND, an island in the Baltic Sea, was evangelized by John, also called Hiltuinus, bishop of Birka (A.D. 1065), ibid., 617, 636.

GREENLAND, a region of North America, was evangelized by Ísleifr, bishop of Skálholt (A.D. 1065), ibid., CXLVI, 617, 654.

## H
HALSINGLAND. In the Swedish city, Simeon, bishop of Halsingland, preached (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 641. HAMARCAM, a city of Frisia, was evangelized by Willehad, bishop of Bremen (A.D. 754), St. Ansgar, CXVIII, 1015, 1016. HAMMABURG. In the German city, Christ was proclaimed by Heridag, first bishop of Hamburg (A.D. 804), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 472.—St. Ansgar, bishop of Hamburg (A.D. 826), St. Ansgar, CXVIII, 966.—Rimbert (A.D. 660), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 486.—Bishop Unni (A.D. 903–936), ibid., CXLVI, 498.—Bishop Adaldag (A.D. 936), ibid., 501. HARUSA, a city of Danish Cismar, received the faith of Christ from Regimbrond, bishop of Harusa (A.D. 948), ibid., CXLVI, 503. HASBANIA. In Gaul, Abbot Trudo evangelized Hasbania (A.D. 651), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 123. HEREFORD. In the city of the Mercian province preached Putta, first bishop of Hereford (A.D. 720), William, CLXXIX, 1599.—Trithel, Putta’s successor (A.D. 740), ibid., CLXXIX, 1599. THE HESSIANS, peoples of Germany, were converted to Christ by St. Boniface, archbishop of Mainz and apostle of the Germans (A.D. 720), St. Boniface, LXXXIX, 617, 642; Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 466. IRELAND. There preached St. Fingaris (A.D. 430), Spurious Writings of St. Anselm, CLIX, 325.—St. Patrick, bishop of the Irish (A.D. 432), Bede, XCV, 121 note; Guigo II, CLIII, 789, 801; Spurious Writings of St. Anselm, CLIX, 325; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 79; William, CLXXIX, 1688.—St. Benignus, disciple of St. Patrick (A.D. 460), ibid., CLXXIX, 1691.—St. Columba, an Irishman (A.D. 565), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1329, 1332.—Sts. Livinus, Foillan, Fursey, and Elias (A.D. 648), St. Boniface, LXXXIX, 877, 879.—Swibert (A.D. 692), Bede, XCV, 243. THE IBERIANS, peoples of Spain, had Christ preached to them by the seven disciples of St. James, bishop of Jerusalem (A.D. 44), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 113. THE HIENSES OR HII, peoples of an island of England lying near Ireland, had as preachers of the divine word St. Columba (A.D. 596), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1332.—Aidan (A.D. 615–640), Bede, XCV, 19–24; Abbot Bernold, CXLVIII, 1336; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 120; William, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry, CXCV, 860; Helinand, CCXII, 772. HIERAPOLIS, a royal city of India, was evangelized by St. Thomas, also called Didymus (“the Twin”) (A.D. 48), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 159–162. HIERAPOLIS, a city of Phrygia, was instructed in the faith of Christ by St. Philip the apostle (A.D. 50), Freculf, CVI, 1148; William, CLXXIX, 1683; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 157.—St. Apollinaris, bishop of Hierapolis (A.D. 130), Freculf, CVI, 1166. HIRCANIA, a region of Asia, was evangelized by St. Thomas Didymus the apostle (A.D. 33–53), Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 157. HISPALIS, a city of Baetica in Spain, Seville, was evangelized by St. Pius, first bishop of Hispalis (A.D. 37–70), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 128.—Philip of Milan, called Philotheus (A.D. 91), ibid., 261, 263. SPAIN. The preachers of the divine word there were St. Peter the apostle (A.D. 50–60), ibid., XXXI, 161.—Priests ordained at Rome by St. Peter and sent into the Spains (A.D. 53), ibid., XXXI, 151.—St. James the Greater (A.D. 34), ibid., 87, 88; (A.D. 37), ibid., 109; Freculf, CVI, 1147; Munio, CLXX, 875.—Christians dispersed after the persecution directed against St. Stephen (A.D. 35), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 91, 97.—St. Paul the apostle (A.D. 64), ibid., 190; St. Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 79.—Oppius the centurion; St. Memmius Mancius; St. Agathodorus [Col. 0566] of Tarragona; Arcadius of Juliobriga; Athanasius of Caesaraugusta; Basil of Braga; Capito of Lucus; and Elpidius of Toledo (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88, 129, 130, 167, 255.—St. Ephrem, disciple of St. James; St. Etherius of Barcelona; Eugenius Marcus; Nestor of Palentia; and Peter of Braga (A.D. 37–60), ibid., XXXI, 109, 129, 130.—Torquatus, Thesiphorus, Caecilius, Iscius, Secundus, Indalecius, and Euphrasius (A.D. 43), ibid., 131, 135, 151, 155, 167, 169, 173, 175.—The seven disciples of St. James the apostle who carried their master’s body into Spain (A.D. 44), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 113.—Calocerus, disciple of St. James (A.D. 44), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 151.—Paul Sergius, Martial of Limoges, Timothy, Philemon, and other disciples of St. Paul the apostle (A.D. 48–60), ibid., 169, 190, 195. HULMO, an island of Denmark, received Christ’s faith from Eginon, bishop of Dalby (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 627. HUNGARY. There preached St. Paulinus, patriarch of Aquileia (A.D. 790–804), St. Paulinus, XCIX, 73, 74.—St. Wicbert, monk of Gembloux (A.D. 953), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 672.—Henry II, king and emperor of the Germans (A.D. 1002), Honorius of Autun, CLXXII, 193.—Gisela, queen of the Hungarians, who brought her royal husband and imperial father to Christ, together with an innumerable multitude of peoples (A.D. 1010), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 200; Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 531.—Stephen, king of the Hungarians (A.D. 1025), Honorius of Autun, CLXXII, 193. THE HUNS. Arno, bishop of Salzburg, and Paulinus, patriarch of Aquileia, laboured zealously to convert the Huns (A.D. 794–800), St. Paulinus, XCIX, 76, 77; Alcuin, C, 187, 198.

## I

IBERIA. A captive woman converted the nation of the Iberians to Christ (A.D. 328), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 480.—Edessius preached among the Iberians (A.D. 328), Freculf, CVI, 1198. ICONIUM, Konieh, a city of Isauria in Asia Minor, had as preachers of the divine word Sts. Paul and Barnabas (A.D. 48–50), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 115; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1693, 1694. ILLIBERIS, a city of Spain, Granada, was evangelized by St. Indalecius, ordained bishop at Rome and sent by blessed Peter into Spain (A.D. 45), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 169. ILLYRIA. In this ancient region of Europe, Paul and Timothy, Silas and Barnabas preached (A.D. 50–58), Freculf, CVI, 1130; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anastasius, CXXVII, 464; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639. THE ROMAN EMPIRE. The Roman emperor Philip and his son Philip were converted through a certain Christian soldier named Pontius (A.D. 242), Freculf, CVI, 1178; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 70.—The emperor Constantine the Great was converted to Christ and spread the Christian faith throughout the empire far and wide (A.D. 312), Sulpicius Severus, XX, 147; Aurelius Cassiodorus, LXIX, 888; Freculf, CVI, 1190; Anastasius, CXXVII, 1510; Hugh, abbot of Flavigny, CLIV, 96; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 955; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 73, 204. INDIA was evangelized by St. Thomas Didymus the apostle (A.D. 34), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 478; Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88; Freculf, CVI, 1147; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 157–162.—St. Matthias the apostle, Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 111; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 168.—The peoples of India were converted to the faith (A.D. 330), Aurelius Cassiodorus, LXIX, 943. INNER INDIA was taught the faith of Christ by Bartholomew the apostle (A.D. 37–60), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 478; Freculf, CVI, 1147; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 165.—Frumentius and Edessius, captive boys belonging to Meropius, a philosopher of Tyre (A.D. 328), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 478.—Frumentius, ibid., 480; Freculf, CVI, 1198. THE ISLANDS OF NORWAY were evangelized by Grimkil, Rodulf, bishop of Schleswig, and Bernard (A.D. 1030–1060), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 541, 650.—Olaf, king of the Northmen, sent preachers throughout his kingdom and to many islands beyond Norway (A.D. 1040), ibid., 540. IONIA. In this region of Asia Minor, Christ was proclaimed by John the apostle together with James the Greater, the apostle (A.D. 38–50), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 135; CLXXXVIII, 149.—Sts. Paul and Timothy (A.D. 48–58), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 125; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1704.—Onesimus, disciple of St. Paul (A.D. 60–100), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129. [Col. 0567] ISAURIA, a region of Asia Minor, had as preachers of the divine word Paul and Barnabas (A.D. 48–50), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 115; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1693, 1694. THE GREAT ISLAND OF ICELAND, an island in the Atlantic, was evangelized by Liasdag, first bishop of Ribe (A.D. 948), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 503, 518, 521.—Hared, or Horit, bishop of Schleswig (A.D. 948), ibid., 503.—John, bishop of Magnopolis (A.D. 1023), ibid., 527, 540, 595, 617, 650.—Islef of Skálholt (A.D. 1065), ibid., 617, 654.—John, also called Hillimius, bishop of Birka (A.D. 1065), ibid., 617, 636. ITALY. There preached Peter the apostle and Paul, teacher of the Gentiles (A.D. 40–69), Lactantius, appendix VII, 621; Sulpicius Severus, XX, 145; St. Prosper of Aquitaine, priest, LI, 173; Freculf, CVI, 1128; Haymo, CXVIII, 829; Anastasius, CXXVII, 438; Hermannus Contractus, CXLIII, 57; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 641; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 25; Ekkehard, CLIV, 667; Anonymous, CLIV, 1116; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 122, 132.—St. Apollinaris, bishop of Ravenna; Barnabas, disciple of St. Paul and bishop of Milan; Celsus; Nazarius; Mark; and Hermagoras (A.D. 50–100), Freculf, CVI, 678; St. Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 78; Regino, abbot of Prüm, CXXXII, 118; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 955; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 181.

## J

JERUSALEM. At Jerusalem, our Lord Jesus Christ, God and man, preached and, to confirm his teaching, breathed his last upon the cross for the salvation of the world in the thirty-third year of his age, Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 101; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1632.—The twelve apostles—namely Simon Peter, John the Evangelist, James the Less son of Alphaeus, Andrew brother of Simon Peter, Philip, Thomas Didymus, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the Greater son of Zebedee and brother of John the Evangelist, Simon the Zealot, Judas son of James, and Matthias—assembled on the day of Pentecost, received the Holy Spirit, and preached at Jerusalem (A.D. 33), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 64, 65; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1034, 1631.—They apportioned the world among themselves for preaching (A.D. 34; others, 37), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88.—St. Peter, with John, preached at Jerusalem, ibid., 134; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 64, 65, 102.—At the gate of the Temple they healed a lame man, Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 103; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1655.—Peter held at Jerusalem the first council concerning the conversion of the Gentiles (A.D. 40), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 134; Anastasius, CXXVII, 456.—St. James the Less was ordained bishop of Jerusalem and preached (A.D. 33–40), Freculf, CVI, 1122; Haymo, CXVIII, 823; St. Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 76; Regino, abbot of Prüm, CXXXII, 16; Hermannus Contractus, CXLIII, 57; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 638; Abbot Bernold, CXLVIII, 1304; Ekkehard, CLIV, 663; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 154.—St. Stephen, the first martyr, proclaimed Christ at Jerusalem (A.D. 33), ibid., 105; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1663.—St. Paul the apostle preached at Jerusalem (A.D. 48), Anastasius, CXXVII, 466; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 17; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 610, 615; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 24; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 108; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1679, 1689, 1694.—Jerusalem had as a preacher of the divine word St. Barnabas (A.D. 48), Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 17; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 640, 645; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 24; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 108.—Titus, disciple of St. Paul (A.D. 50), Marianus Scotus, CXXVII, 640, 645. JOPPA. At Jaffa, a city of Palestine, St. Peter the apostle preached (A.D. 38–40), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 109; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674. JUDAEA. There preached St. John the Baptist (A.D. 30), Freculf, CVI, 1121; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 16; Ekkehard, CLIV, 661; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1552; Sicard, bishop of Cremona, CCXIII, 449.—John the Baptist baptized Christ in the Jordan, Anastasius, CXXVII, 452; Hermannus Contractus, CXLIII, 57; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1304; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 101; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1562.—Our Lord Jesus Christ, God and man, baptized in the Jordan, began the era of Gospel preaching in the thirtieth year of his age, Anastasius Bibliothecarius, CXXVII, 452; CXXIX, 525; Hermannus Contractus, CXLIII, 57; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1304; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 102; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1562.—He called the apostles (A.D. 30), Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 16; Ekkehard, CLIV, 661.—He sent them to evangelize through the cities of Judaea, Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1565.—He openly spread the Gospel throughout Judaea (A.D. 30–33), Haymo, CXVIII, 822; St. Ado, archbishop of Vienne, [Col. 0568] CXXIII, 76; Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 16; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 637; Ekkehard of Aura, CLIV, 661; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1562.—Having accomplished all things, he breathed his last upon the cross for the salvation of the world (A.D. 33), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 101; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1622.—St. Peter the apostle travelled throughout all Judaea and Palestine preaching (A.D. 37–40), Anastasius, CXXVII, 454, 456, 462; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 25; Ekkehard, CLIV, 667; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116, 122; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674, 1701; St. James the Less, ordained bishop of Jerusalem, preached through Judaea (A.D. 33–40), Freculf, CVI, 1122; Haymo, CXVIII, 823; St. Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXXII, 76; Regino, abbot of Prüm, CXXXII, 16; Hermannus Contractus, CXLIII, 55; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 638; Abbot Bernold, CXLVIII, 1304; Ekkehard, CLIV, 663; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 154.—St. Matthew, apostle and evangelist (A.D. 37–50), Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 111; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1680.—While preaching in Judaea, he wrote his holy Gospel in Hebrew (A.D. 45), St. Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 75; Anastasius, CXXVII, 458; Hermannus Contractus, CXLIII, 57; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1305; Ekkehard, CLIV, 665.—St. Matthias preached in Judaea (A.D. 33), Freculf, CVI, 1148; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 177.—St. Stephen, the first martyr, preached in Judaea (A.D. 33), ibid., 105; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1663.—The disciples dispersed after the persecution against St. Stephen preached throughout all Judaea, Haymo, CXVIII, 825; Anastasius, CXXVII, 454; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 109. JULIOBRIGA, Valdeviejo, a city of Spain, was evangelized through Arcadius, bishop of Juliobriga (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129, 130. JUTLAND. In this Danish region preached Harold, first bishop of Schleswig (A.D. 840), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 621.—Regimbrond of Harusa and Hared, or Harit, of Schleswig (A.D. 948), ibid., 503.—The bishops Odinkar the Younger of Ribe and Poppo the Younger of Schleswig (A.D. 1000–1015), ibid., 525, 526, 535.—The bishops Rodulf of Schleswig and Wallus of Ribe (A.D. 1056), ibid., 541, 552, 621, 622, 668.

## L

LAODICEA. In the Phrygian city, now Eski Hissar, St. Peter the apostle proclaimed Christ (A.D. 38–40), Anastasius, CXXVII, 456; Heriger, abbot of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 25; Ekkehard, ibid., 667; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116, 122; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674, 1701.—St. Barnabas (A.D. 50), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 178. LAURAN CASTLE, near Carcassonne, now Castelnaudary. Guy, abbot of Vaux-de-Cernay and afterwards bishop of Carcassonne, preached against the Albigensians at Lauran Castle (A.D. 1207), Sicard, bishop of Cremona, CCXIII, 555, 578. LEICESTER. Edbert, bishop of Leicester, and Totta evangelized this city of the Middle Angles (A.D. 630–640), William, CLXXIX, 1605. LIMOGES. In this Gallic city, Christ was proclaimed by St. Martial, bishop of Limoges (A.D. 58), St. Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175; Adam the monk, CXLI, 87, 112; Jordan, bishop of Limoges, CXLII, 1353; Rabanus Maurus, 1494.—Austrelianus and Alpinianus (A.D. 70), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 186. LERI. In this Saxon city, Emmingus and Folcard, companions of St. Willebad, apostle of the Frisians, preached and received the crown of martyrdom from the Saxons (A.D. 780), St. Ansgar, bishop, CXVIII, 1017. LIBYA, a region of Africa, was evangelized by St. Mark the Evangelist (A.D. 50–60), St. Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 79; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 644, 648; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 182. LICHFIELD, a city in the Mercian province, was evangelized by Cedd the Scot, bishop of Lichfield (A.D. 653), Bede, XCV, 150. LINCOLN. At Lincoln, in eastern England, St. Paulinus, together with St. Augustine, apostle of the English, preached (A.D. 625), Henry, CXCV, 844, 856.—Felix, bishop of Lincoln (A.D. 634–640), ibid., 857, 858.—Honorius, bishop of Lincoln (A.D. 640), ibid., 857. LINDISFARIA, in Middle England, had as preachers of the divine word Cella, bishop of Lindisfarne, and Diuma (A.D. 650–653), William, CLXXIX, 1603. LINDISFARNE. On the island of England, Holy Island, there preached Aedan or Aidan, bishop of Lindisfarne (A.D. 616–640), Bede, XCV, 19–24; Abbot Bernold, CXLVIII, [Col. 0569] 1336; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 120; William, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry, CXCX [sic], 860; Helinand, CCXII, 772; Colman, bishop of Lindisfarne (A.D. 650), William, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry, CXCV, 865; Finan (A.D. 653), Bede, XCV, 150; William, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry, CXCV, 863. LINDSEY, a province of eastern England, was evangelized by St. Paulinus, apostle of the English (A.D. 625), Henry, CXCV, 844. LANGRES. In this Gallic city, Sts. Benignus, Andochius, and Thyrsus the deacon—sent by St. Polycarp into Gaul to preach—preached (A.D. 140), St. Warnaharius, priest, LXXX, 188, 193, 199. LINOGES. Two monks of uncertain name evangelized the peoples of Slavonia (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, canon, CLXVI, 533, 574. LONDON. In the city of England, London, preached St. Laurence, bishop of London (A.D. 600–645), Henry, CXCV, 851, 853.—Mellitus, with Laurence and Justus (A.D. 604–655), Bede, XCV, 85.—Bernold, CXLVIII, 1332; Lanfranc, CL, 745, 764 (appendix); William, CCXXIX, 1443; Henry, CXCV, 853.—Sarrumnus and Cedd, bishops of London, William, CLXXIX, 1514; Henry, CXCV, 865. THE LOMBARDS were brought to Christ’s faith by St. Gregory the Great, pope (A.D. 595), Mozarabic Liturgy, LXLXV, 541.—Theudelinda, queen of the Lombards, who converted her husband Agilulf together with the people; and Agnellus, bishop of Trent (A.D. 595), ibid., 541; Ekkehard, CLIV, 797. LONTIUM. At this city of the Obotrites in Slavonia, two monks of uncertain name preached (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLXI, 573, 574. LUCA (Martos), a city of Spain, had as a preacher of the divine word Capito, bishop of Lucus and disciple of St. James the apostle (A.D. 37–60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129, 130. LYONS, a city of Gaul, was converted to Christ by St. Irenaeus, bishop of Lyons (A.D. 48), CXII, 1493; John the monk, CLXII, 755.—St. Pothinus (A.D. 166), Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 96; Baldric, archbishop of Dol, CLXVI, 1209.—Valerianus, successor of St. Pothinus (A.D. 180), ibid., 1210.—St. Zacharias of Lyons (A.D. 195), John the monk, CLXII, 756. LUND, a city of Scania in Sweden, was evangelized by Eginon, bishop of Dalby (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 617, 627. LUSITANIA, a region of Spain, received Christ’s faith from Jonah, disciple of St. Dionysius the Areopagite (A.D. 86), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 253. LUTETIA OF THE PARISII was converted to Christ through the preaching of St. Germanus (A.D. 554–570), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1331. LYCAONIA. In this region of Asia Minor, Christ was preached by St. Bartholomew the apostle (A.D. 38), Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 165.—Sts. Paul and Barnabas, ibid., 115, 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1693, 1694. LYDDA. At this city of Palestine, St. Peter preached (A.D. 38–40), Anastasius, CXXVII, 456; Heriger of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Hugh, abbot, CLIV, 25; Ekkehard, ibid., 667; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674. LYDIA, a region of Asia Minor, was evangelized by St. Paul the apostle with Silas, Timothy, and Barnabas (A.D. 48–58), Freculf, CVI, 1130; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anastasius, CXXVII, 464; Heriger of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116, 118. LYSTRA. In this city of Isauria, Vatik, Sts. Paul the apostle, Barnabas, and Silas preached (A.D. 48–50), Orderic Vitalis, CXXXVIII, 115, 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1693, 1694.

## M

MACEDONIA was evangelized by St. Andrew (A.D. 38), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 139, 142.—Matthew the apostle (A.D. 38–50), Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 111; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 168.—St. Paul, Timothy, Silas, and Luke (A.D. 48–58), Freculf, CVI, 1130; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anastasius, CXXVII, 467; Heriger of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 115, 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1699.—Erastus, disciple of St. Paul (A.D. 60–100), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129. MAGDEBURG, a city of Slavonia, was evangelized by Adalbert, first bishop of Magdeburg, who converted many peoples of the Slavs to Christ (A.D. 968–981), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 508. [Col. 0570] MAGNOPOLIS, a city of the Obotrites in Slavonia, had as preachers of the divine Word John, a Scot by nation, bishop of Magnopolis (A.D. 1023), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 527, 540, 595, 617, 650.—Two monks of uncertain name (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 574. MALMESBURY, a city of England, received the faith from Theodore, bishop of Malmesbury (A.D. 613), William, CLXXIX, 1443; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 782. MARMORICA, Marmorique, a region of inland Libya, had Christ preached there by St. Mark the Evangelist (A.D. 50–60), St. Ado, archbishop of Vienne, CXXIII, 79; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 644, 646; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 182. MARSEILLE. St. Lazarus, first bishop of Marseille, landed at the port of Marseille with Mary Magdalene, Maximinus, Martha, Joseph, and others, and preached Christ (A.D. 35), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 156, 158; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 141. MAURITANIA, a city of Aquitaine in Gaul, Mortagne-sur-Gironde, had as preachers of the divine word St. Martial, bishop of Limoges, and Sts. Austriclianus and Alpinianus (A.D. 73), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 193. MEDIA. In this region of Asia, Thomas Didymus the apostle preached Christ (A.D. 38–53), Freculf, CVI, 1117; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 157. MILAN was evangelized by St. Barnabas, first bishop of Milan (A.D. 58), Landulf the Elder, CXLVII, 955; Celsus (A.D. 79–100), Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 18; Nazarius, ibid.—St. Philip surnamed Philotheus (A.D. 91), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 261, 263. METZ. At Metz, Felix proclaimed Christ with St. Clement (A.D. 50–100), Anonymous, CLIV, 1119; CLXIII, 579, 581. MEAUX was evangelized by Sts. Antonius, bishop of Meaux, Sanctinus, and Dionysius (A.D. 70–79), Hugh, abbot, CLXV, 27, 29. MELMIN. In the city of the Bernicians, St. Paulinus, apostle of the English, preached Christ (A.D. 625), Henry, CXCV, 856. MERCIANS, English. See ENGLISH MERCIANS. MESOPOTAMIA, a region of Asia, was evangelized by Judas the apostle (A.D. 37–70), Freculf, CXI, 1132, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 115, 116. MILETUS. At Palatcha, a city of Caria in Asia, Sts. Paul, Barnabas, Silas, and Timothy proclaimed Christ (A.D. 50–58), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 124, 125; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1707. MILINDORF, a city of the Transalbians in Germany, was evangelized by St. Willeric, bishop of Bremen, Adam of Bremen, bishop, CXLVI, 472. MYTILENE, Medelin, the royal city of the island of Lesbos, was brought to Christ by St. Paul the apostle (A.D. 58), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 128. MONTPELLIER. Diego, bishop of Osma, and Peter and Radulf, Cistercian monks, preached among the Albigensians at Montpellier (A.D. 1206), Peter the Monk, CCXIII, 549. MONTRÉAL, a city in the territory of Carcassonne. Diego, bishop of Osma, Guy, abbot of Vaux-de-Cernay, and Dominic preached at Montréal (A.D. 1206–1208), Peter the Monk, CCXIII, 550, 554. MORAVIA, a region of Germany, was evangelized by Bishop Methodius; and Borvoy, king of the Bohemians, embraced the faith with his people (A.D. 885), Cosmas of Prague, dean, CLXVI, 71, 81. THE MYRMIDONS, peoples of Thessaly, had Christ proclaimed to them by Sts. Matthew and Andrew (A.D. 50), CLXXXVIII, 139. MYSIA. In this region of Asia Minor, the preachers of the divine word were Sts. Paul and Timothy (A.D. 50–56), Freculf, CVI, 1130; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anastasius, CXXVII, 464; Heriger of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1008; Marianus Scotus, CXLVII, 639; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116.

## N

NADABER, a royal city of Ethiopia, received the Gospel through St. Matthew (A.D. 48–70), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 168–170. NARBONNE. In this Gallic city, Paul Sergius, proconsul of Salamis and disciple of St. Paul, preached Christ with Paul (A.D. 60), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 195; St. Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175, 183; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 128. THE PROVINCE OF NARBONNE IN GAUL. Peter and Radulf, Cistercian monks; Diego, bishop of Osma; Guy, abbot of Vaux-de-Cernay; and St. Dominic preached against the Albigensian heresy in the province of Narbonne (A.D. 1206–1208), Sicard, bishop of Cremona, CCXIII, 155, 156. NERITUM, a city of Armenia, was evangelized by Simon the Zealot, apostle (A.D. 63), Freculf, CVI, 1135, 1147. [Col. 0571] NEUSTRIA. In this region of Gaul, Mansius, first bishop of York, and Taurinus, his successor, preached Christ (A.D. 90–119), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 255; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 386. NICAEA, Isnick, a city of Bithynia in Asia Minor, was evangelized by Andrew the apostle (A.D. 38–53), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 140. NICOMEDIA. In the royal city of Bithynia, Andrew the apostle proclaimed Christ (A.D. 38–53), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 140. NORDALBINGIA, a region of Sweden, was brought to Christ by Heridag, first bishop of Hamburg (A.D. 804), Adam of Bremen, canon, CXLVI, 472.—Ansgar, bishop of Hamburg and Bremen (A.D. 826–830), ibid., 483. NORTHUMBRIA. In this region of eastern England, the preachers of the divine word were St. Paulinus, who converted King Edwin with his people to Christ (A.D. 625), Bede, XCV, 105, 107; Bernold, CXLVIII, 1335; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 118; Henry, CXCV, 856.—King Oswald, who brought his people to the faith and made Aidan, summoned from Scotland, bishop of Lindisfarne (A.D. 640), Bede, XCV, 115, 117; Henry, CXCV, 860; Aidan or Aedan (A.D. 640), Bede, XCV, 19–24; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 120; William, CLXXIX, 1581; Henry, CXCV, 860; Helinand, CXII, 772. THE NORICI, peoples of Bavaria, received Christ’s faith from Severinus, abbot (A.D. 482), St. Paulinus of Aquileia, XCII, 69. NORMANDY IN GAUL was evangelized by Mallonus and Avicianus, first apostles of Normandy (A.D. 280), Orderic, CLXXXIII, 390.—Charles the Simple, king of the Franks, imposed the faith upon the Northmen, and their leader Rollo was converted, while Franco, bishop of Rouen, preached (A.D. 912), Dudo of St. Quentin, CXLI, 651; William of Jumièges, CXLIX, 801; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 232. NORWAY IN SWEDEN AND NORWAY was brought to Christ by Henry I, king and emperor of the Germans, who converted the Northmen and Danes with their king Cnut (A.D. 931), Thietmar of Merseburg, CXXXIX, 1193.—Olaf, king of the Northmen (A.D. 1040), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 540.—Sigfrid, bishop of Glastonbury, and Siguard and Asgoth (A.D. 1060), ibid., 651. NORWAY was evangelized by Gotebald, an Englishman by nationality (A.D. 985), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 529.—Forward, bishop of Slavonia (A.D. 992), ibid., 533.—The bishops Sigfrid and Sigward, Sirward, Theolf, Asgoth, and Adalwald the Elder (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 640, 650, 651, 671.—Bishop Osmand and Bishop Meinhard (A.D. 1069), ibid., 568, 617, 653.—Nicholas, an Englishman by nationality, later Pope Adrian IV, who, sent by Eugenius III, converted many peoples to Christ (A.D. 1145–1150).

## O

THE OBOTRITES, peoples of Slavonia, were converted to Christ by John, bishop of Magnopolis (A.D. 1023), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 527, 540, 595, 617, 650.—Two monks coming from Bohemia (A.D. 1065), ibid., 573, 574. THE WEST. Peter the apostle and Paul proclaimed the Gospel through the West (A.D. 45–60), Anastasius, CXXVII, 458, 466, 468; Heriger, CXXXIX, 1008; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 128. ÖLAND, an island of the Baltic Sea, had as preacher of the divine word John, commonly called Hilluin, bishop of Birka (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 636. ÖSEL, an island of the Baltic Sea, was evangelized by John, bishop of Birka (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 636. THE WHOLE WORLD. The eleven apostles received from Christ the Lord authority to preach throughout the whole world (A.D. 33), Pope Marcellus, VI, 1055.—The twelve apostles apportioned the world among themselves for preaching (A.D. 37), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88. THE ORKNEY ISLANDS, islands of the Atlantic Ocean, were evangelized by Thurolph, bishop of Blascona (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 617, 653.—Eginon, bishop of Dalby (A.D. 1070), ibid., 627. THE OSTGOTHS, peoples of Sweden, were brought to Christ by Thurgot, first bishop of Skara (A.D. 1013), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 541 (note).

## P
PALENTIA, a city of Spain, was evangelized by Nestor, first bishop of Palencia (A.D. 37), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 129, 130. PALAESTINE in its entirety was traversed in preaching by the apostle Peter [Col. 0572] (A.D. 38–40), Anastas., CXXVI, 456; Heriger., CXXXIX, 1008; Hugo, abb., CLIV, 25; Ekkeard., ibid., 667; CLXXXVIII, 116, 122; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674, 1701 (see JUDAEA, Jerusalem). PAMPHYLIA, a region of Asia Minor, was evangelized by Paul and Barnabas (A.D. 48–58), Orderic., CLXXXVIII, 115; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1691, 1694. PANNONIA was evangelized by Arno, bishop of Salzburg, and Paulinus, patriarch of Aquileia (A.D. 796–800), St Paulinus of Aquileia, XCIX, 76; Alcuin, C, 187, 188.—Wolfgang, bishop of Regensburg (A.D. 974), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 402.—St Adalbert, bishop of Prague (A.D. 980), Cosmas of Prague, CLXVI, 92; Honorius of Autun, CLXXII, 193; St Adalbert of Prague, CXXXVII, 866.

PAPHOS, a city on the island of Cyprus: Tychicus, a disciple of St Paul, proclaimed Christ at Paphos in Cyprus (A.D. 58–100), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 129. PARIS had as preachers of the divine word St Dionysius the Areopagite (A.D. 50–70), St Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 175–183; Othlo, monk, CXLVI, 387; Folcard, monk, CXLVII, 1182; CLIV, 26, 679.—Germanus, bishop of Paris (A.D. 554–570), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1331. PARTHIA, a region of Asia, was evangelized by St Thomas Didymus, apostle (A.D. 34–53), Rufinus of Aquileia, XXI, 478; Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 87, 88; Freculf, CVI, 1147; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 157.—St Matthew, apostle, Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 111; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 168.—Bishop Atticus (A.D. 379), Freculf, CVI, 1241, 1242.

At PATARA, a city of Lycia, the apostle Paul proclaimed Christ (A.D. 50–56), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 125. PATAVIA (Passau), a city of Bavaria, was evangelized through Vivilius or Vivalus, bishop of Passau (A.D. 730), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 649, 687, 806. The island of PATMOS was evangelized by St John the apostle, St Ado, CXXIII, 81; Anastas., CXXVII, 486; Ekkeard, CLIV, 69. St Andrew the apostle evangelized PATRAS, a city of Achaia, and received the crown of martyrdom (A.D. 60), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 139, 146.

Against the PELAGIANS in England preached St Germanus, bishop of Auxerre, Lupus of Troyes, Patrick the Irishman, and Severus (A.D. 429–438), Heric, CXXIV, 1164; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 82, 83.—William of Malmesbury, CLXXIX, 1688; Henry, CXCV, 826, 827. PENTAPOLIS, a region of Libya in Africa, received the faith of Christ from St Mark the Evangelist (A.D. 50–60), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 182. PERGAMUM, Karahissar, a city of Pamphylia in Asia Minor, was evangelized by Saints Paul and Barnabas (A.D. 50–58), Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1691, 1694.

In PERSIA, a region of Asia, the preachers of the divine word were St Thomas Didymus (A.D. 38–53), Freculf, CVI, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 157.—Simon Judas and Judas of James (A.D. 40–70), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 172–176.—Bishop Maruthas (A.D. 379), Freculf, CVI, 1241, 1242; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 30.—Bishop Atticus (A.D. 379), Freculf, CVI, 1241.—Caesara, queen of the Persians, who converted her husband Anaulf and a great multitude of the people to Christ (A.D. 588–600), Fredegar the Scholastic, LXXI, 613; John the Deacon of Venice, CXXXIX, 885; Ekkeard, CLIV, 837.—Anastasius, monk (A.D. 628), Bernold, CXLVIII, 1335.

PETRAGORICA, Périgueux, a city of Gaul, was evangelized by Frontinus, bishop of Périgueux (A.D. 50), Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1505. PHILIPPI, Filibé, a city of Macedonia: the apostle St Paul wrote to the Philippians (A.D. 60–69), Anastas., CXXVII, 468.—Erastus preached at Philippi (A.D. 60–100), Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 129. PHOENICIA in Asia Minor was evangelized by the disciples scattered after the persecution directed against St Stephen (A.D. 35), Haymo, CXVIII, 825; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 109.—St Peter the apostle (A.D. 38–40), Anastas., CXXVII, 456; Heriger, CXXXIX, 1008; Hugo, abb., CLIV, 25; Ekkeard, ibid., 667; Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 116, 122; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1674, 1701.—St Paul and Barnabas, Orderic, CLXXXVIII, 115, 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1691.

PHRYGIA, a region of Asia Minor, was evangelized by Saints Paul and Timothy (A.D. 50), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 116.—St Philip the apostle (A.D. 37–66), Freculf, CVI, 1148; William, CLXXIX, 1683. The PICTS were instructed in the faith by St Nima or Ninian, bishop of Candida Casa (A.D. 394, 432), Bede, XCV, 121; William, CLXXIX, 1577; Henry, CXCV, 860.—St Columba and St Columbanus (A.D. 565–660), Bede, XCV, 121; Bernold, [Col. 0573] CXLVIII, 1322; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 112; Henry, CXCV, 860. In PISIDIA, a region of Asia Minor, the apostle Paul and Barnabas proclaimed Christ (A.D. 48–50), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 115, 116; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1691.

Eginon, bishop of Dalby, converted the still barbarous PLEICANOS or PLEICHANOS, peoples of Scania, to Christ (A.D. 1060), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 627. Two monks of uncertain name, arriving from Bohemia, led the POLABYNIGI, peoples of Slavonia, to Christ (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 574. POLAND was evangelized by Jordan, bishop of Poznań (A.D. 966), St Queen Mathilda, CLI, 1336.—Dąbrówka, queen of the Poles, who brought her royal husband Mieszko and the people to the faith (A.D. 966), ibid., 1334; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 848, 849.—Willibald, Procorius, and Aegidius, sent by Pope John XIII (A.D. 970), Pope John XIII, CXXXV, 949.—King and Emperor Henry II (A.D. 1002), Honorius of Autun, CLXXII, 193.—Adalbert, bishop of Prague (A.D. 980), St Adalbert of Prague, CXXXVII, 866; Cosmas, dean of Prague, CLXVI, 92; Honorius of Autun, CLXXII, 193.

The POMERANIANS, peoples of Prussia, received baptism (A.D. 1108), Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 906. In PONTUS, a region of Asia Minor, Christ was proclaimed by St Paul the apostle (A.D. 38–40), Freculf, CVI, 1135; Haymo, CXVIII, 831; Anonymous, CLIV, 1116; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 122, 124; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1679, 1696.—The apostles Simon Judas and Judas of James (A.D. 37–70), Freculf, CVI, 1132, 1147; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 172. POSNAM, Poznań, the royal city of Poland, was evangelized by Jordan, bishop of Poznań (A.D. 966), St Queen Mathilda, CLI, 1336. PRAGUE, the royal city of Bohemia, was evangelized by Dethmar, bishop of Prague (A.D. 973), Cosmas, dean of Prague, CLXVI, 90, 91.—Adalbert, bishop of Prague (A.D. 990), Queen Mathilda, CLI, 1341; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 201.—Passion of St Adalbert of Prague (A.D. 1000), John Canaparius, CXXXVII, 866–888. In PRORUSSIA, St Gaudentius and Adalbert, bishop of Prague, proclaimed Christ (A.D. 990), Queen Mathilda, CLI, 1341.

PROVENCE, a region of Gaul, was evangelized by St Lazarus, Joseph of Arimathea, Maximinus, Mary Magdalene, Martha, and Marcella (A.D. 35–88), Lucius Dexter, XXXI, 156, 158; Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 1493, 1494; Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 141. PTOLEMAIS, a city of Palestine, was converted to the faith by St Peter (A.D. 38–60), Anastas., CXXVII, 456; Heriger, CXXXIX, 1008; Hugo, CLIV, 25; Ekkeard, ibid., 667; Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 120; Peter Comestor, CXCVIII, 1707.—St Paul the apostle, ibid., 1707.

## R

RATISBON, Regensburg, a city of Bavaria, had as teachers of the faith Gowibald, bishop of Regensburg (A.D. 730), St Boniface, LXXXIX, 649.—Wolfgang (A.D. 974), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 402. RAVENNA, a city of Italy, received the faith of Christ from St Apollinaris, bishop of Ravenna (A.D. 70), Agnellus, CVI, 476. RAZZISBURG, a city of the Obotrites in Slavonia, had as instructors in the divine word two monks (A.D. 1065), Adam of Bremen, CXLVI, 574.—Aristo, bishop of Razzisburg (A.D. 1067), ibid., 574.

RHEIMS, a city of Gaul, was evangelized by Sixtus, first bishop of Rheims, and blessed Valerius the confessor (A.D. 48; others say 250), Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 1496; Heriger of Lobbes, CXXXIX, 1010; Hugo, CLIV, 25; Anonymous, ibid., 1116, 1118.—Timothy, Apollinaris, and Sinicius (A.D. 50–90), Flodoard, canon of Rheims, CXXXV, 31, 32; Anonymous, CLIV, 1124. RHODES, an island of the Mediterranean Sea, was evangelized by St Paul (A.D. 57), Orderic Vitalis, CLXXXVIII, 125.
